'''Mahendra Singh Dhoni''' ({{IPA|hi|məˈɦeːnd̪ɾə ˈsɪŋɡʱ ˈd̪ʱoːniː||audio=Mahendra Singh Dhoni.ogg}}; born 7 July 1981) is an Indian professional [[cricketer]] who plays as a right-handed [[batsman|batter]] and a [[wicket-keeper]]. Widely regarded as one of the most prolific wicket-keeper batsmen and [[Captain (cricket)|captains]], he represented the [[Indian national cricket team|Indian cricket team]] and was the captain of the team in [[Limited overs cricket|limited overs]] formats from 2007 to 2017 and in [[Test cricket]] from 2008 to 2014. Dhoni has captained the most number of international matches and is the most successful Indian captain. He has led India to victory in the [[2007 ICC World Twenty20]], the [[2011 Cricket World Cup]], and the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]], being the only captain to win three different limited overs ICC tournaments. He also led the teams that won the [[Asia Cup]] in [[2010 Asia Cup|2010]] and [[2016 Asia Cup|2016]], and was a member of the title-winning squad in [[2018 Asia Cup|2018]]. Born in [[Ranchi]], Dhoni made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Bihar cricket team|Bihar]] in 1999. He made his debut for the Indian cricket team on 23 December 2004 in an [[One day international|ODI]] against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]] and played his first Test a year later against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]]. In 2007, he became the captain of the ODI team before taking over as captain in all formats by 2008. Dhoni retired from Test cricket in 2014 but continued playing in limited overs cricket until 2019. He has scored 17,266 runs in [[international cricket]], including 10,773 runs at an [[batting average (cricket)|average]] of more than 50 in ODIs. In the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL), Dhoni plays for the [[Chennai Super Kings]] (CSK), leading them to the finals on ten occasions and winning the title five times ([[2010 Indian Premier League|2010]], [[2011 Indian Premier League|2011]], [[2018 Indian Premier League|2018]], [[2021 Indian Premier League|2021]], and [[2023 Indian Premier League|2023]])– a record he jointly shares with [[Rohit Sharma]]. He has also led CSK to two [[Champions League T20]] titles in [[2010 Champions League Twenty20|2010]] and [[2014 Champions League Twenty20|2014]]. Dhoni is among the few batsmen to have scored more than five thousand runs in the IPL, as well as being the first [[wicket-keeper]] to do so. In 2008, Dhoni was awarded India's highest sporting honour, the [[Khel Ratna Award]], by the [[Government of India]]. He received the fourth highest civilian award, the [[Padma Shri]], in 2009 and third highest civilian award, the [[Padma Bhushan]], in 2018. Dhoni holds an [[honorary rank]] of [[Lieutenant Colonel]] in the [[Parachute Regiment (India)|Parachute Regiment]] of the [[Territorial Army (India)|Indian Territorial Army]] which was presented to him by the [[Indian Army]] in 2011. In June 2025, he was inducted into the [[ICC Cricket Hall of Fame]].

'''Rohit Gurunath Sharma''' (born 30 April 1987) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er and the former [[Captain (cricket)|captain]] of the [[India national cricket team]] in all formats of the game.<ref name="CI34102" /> He is a right-handed [[Batting order (cricket)#Top order|top-order batter]]. He represents [[Mumbai cricket team|Mumbai]] in domestic cricket and [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. Sharma was a member of the teams that won the [[2007 World Twenty20|2007 T20 World Cup]], the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]] and was the winning captain of the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]] and the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]]. Sharma is widely regarded as a modern-day great, known for his leadership and explosive batting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rohit Sharma: Indian cricket star who made batting look like art|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c071e9dnn85o |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=[[BBC]] |language=en}}</ref>

Sharma holds several batting records which include most runs in [[Twenty20 International|T20 Internationals]], most sixes in international cricket,{{Efn|624 as on 11 December 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Test+ODI+T20I matches {{!}} Batting records {{!}} Most sixes in career |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/most-sixes-in-career-284025 |access-date=6 March 2024 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He also has highest sixes in the T20I format (205).}} most double centuries in [[One Day International|ODI cricket]] (three), most centuries at [[Cricket World Cup]]s (seven) and joint most centuries in [[Twenty20 International]]s (five).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/ind-vs-afg-rohit-sharma-becomes-first-player-to-score-5-t20i-centuries-9114224/#:~:text=India%20skipper%20Rohit%20Sharma%20became,the%203rd%20T20I%20against%20Afghanistan | title=IND vs AFG: Rohit Sharma becomes first player to score 5 T20I centuries | date=17 January 2024 }}</ref> He also holds the world record for the highest individual score (264) in a [[One Day International]] (ODI) and also holds the record for scoring most centuries (five) in a single [[Cricket World Cup]], for which he won the [[ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year]] award in 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 June 2024 |title=T20 World Cup final: Rohit Sharma becomes first-ever captain to win 50 T20Is |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/t20-world-cup-2024-final-rohit-sharma-captain-50-t20-wins-9423328/ |access-date=30 June 2024 |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]] |language=en}}</ref> He is the first and only captain to lead a team in all{{efn|2023 World Test Championship final, 2023 Cricket World Cup final, 2024 T20 World Cup final, and 2025 ICC Champions Trophy final}} ICC tournament finals.<ref>{{cite news |date=6 March 2025 |title=The unmatched legacy of Rohit Sharma in men's ICC tournaments |url=https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1071455321682845&set=a.638015151693533 |work=ICC official Facebook Page}}</ref>

He formerly captained [[Mumbai Indians]] and the team has won five [[Indian Premier League]] titles in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020 under him, making him the most successful captain in [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] history, sharing this record with [[MS Dhoni]]. He is also one of two players who have played in every edition of the [[Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cup]], from the [[2007 ICC World Twenty20|inaugural edition in 2007]] till 2024.{{Efn|The other player is [[Shakib Al Hasan]] of Bangladesh.}} He is the only Indian player to win two [[Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cup]]s. He became the second Indian captain to win a [[Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cup]].

He has received three national honours, the [[Arjuna Award]] in 2015, the prestigious [[Khel Ratna Award]] in 2020 by the [[Government of India]], and the [[Padma Shri]], India's fourth-highest civilian award, in 2026, for his immense, long standing contribution to [[Cricket in India|Indian cricket]], which notably includes leading India to victory in the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/sports/former-indian-skipper-rohit-sharma-conferred-padma-shri/|title=Former Indian skipper Rohit Sharma conferred Padma Shri|date=June 23, 2026|website=The Tribune}}</ref><ref name="Vijay Amritraj, Mammootty, Rohit Sharma, Alka Yagnik take home Padma awards">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title=Vijay Amritraj, Mammootty, Rohit Sharma, Alka Yagnik take home Padma awards |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/president-droupadi-murmu-padma-awards-june-23-2026/article71137810.ece |access-date=24 June 2026 |publisher=The Hindu |date=23 June 2026 |language=en-IN}}</ref><ref name="Rohit Sharma receives Padma Shri from President Murmu, wife Ritika beams with pride">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title=Rohit Sharma receives Padma Shri from President Murmu, wife Ritika beams with pride |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/rohit-sharma-padma-shri-president-murmu-rashtrapathi-bhavan-2932652-2026-06-23 |access-date=24 June 2026 |publisher=India Today |date=23 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]]. Under his captaincy, India also won the [[2018 Asia Cup]] and the [[2023 Asia Cup]], the seventh and eighth time the country won the title, both in ODI format as well as the [[2018 Nidahas Trophy]], their second overall and first in T20I format.

'''Ravindrasinh Anirudhsinh Jadeja''' (born 6 December 1988) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who represents the [[India national cricket team|India national team]] currently in ODI and Test formats. He is an [[all-rounder]], who [[Batting (cricket)|bats]] left-handed and bowls left-arm orthodox spin. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest all-rounders and among the finest fielders of his generation. He represents [[Saurashtra cricket team|Saurashtra]] in domestic cricket and [[Rajasthan Royals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. Jadeja was a crucial member of the Indian teams that won the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy|2013]] and [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]], becoming leading wicket-taker and player of the final in the former and hitting the winning boundary in the latter final. He was also a part of the Indian squad that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 ICC T20 World Cup]], after which he announced his retirement from T20Is.

Jadeja was vice-captain of the [[Indian U-19 cricket team]] that won the [[Under-19 Cricket World Cup|World Cup]] in [[Malaysia]] in [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2008]], under the captaincy of former Indian captain [[Virat Kohli]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=AadyaS |date=4 June 2022 |title=Where Are India's 2008 U19 World Cup Winning Squad Members Now? |url=https://www.wisden.com/cricket-news/where-are-indias-2008-u19-world-cup-winning-squad-members-now |access-date=6 April 2025 |website=Wisden}}</ref> He made his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] on 8 February 2009 and scored an unbeaten 60 off 77 balls in that match. However, his Test debut came almost four years later, on 13 December 2012, against [[England cricket team|England]] at [[Nagpur]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ravindra Jadeja Debut and last played matches in Tests, ODIs, T20Is and other formats |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/ravindra-jadeja-234675/matches |access-date=25 August 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

Jadeja was bought for $2 million by the [[Chennai Super Kings]] at the [[2012 IPL Players Auction]]. He was bought by the [[Gujarat Lions]] in the 2016 IPL Players Auction for {{INR}}9.5 crores after the Chennai Super Kings were banned from the [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] for two seasons. On 22 January 2017, Jadeja became the first Indian left-arm spinner to take 150 [[One Day International]] wickets, when he dismissed [[Sam Billings]] at [[Eden Gardens]], [[Kolkata]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sarmah |first1=Bhargab |title=Ravindra Jadeja Becomes First Indian Left-Arm Spinner to Complete 150 Scalps in ODIs |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/india-vs-england-2016-17/ravindra-jadeja-becomes-first-indian-left-arm-spinner-to-complete-150-scalps-in-odis-1651436 |access-date=27 February 2021 |work=NDTV |date=22 January 2017 |language=en |archive-date=3 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603120820/https://sports.ndtv.com/india-vs-england-2016-17/ravindra-jadeja-becomes-first-indian-left-arm-spinner-to-complete-150-scalps-in-odis-1651436 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In March 2017, he became the [[ICC Player Rankings|top ranked bowler]] in the world leaving behind [[Ravichandran Ashwin]] who held that position for a long time.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Sikdar |first1=Sandip |title=Ravindra Jadeja Pips R Ashwin To Stay No.1, Cheteshwar Pujara No.2 In Batting List |publisher= NDTV |date=21 March 2017 |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/india-vs-australia-2017/ravindra-jadeja-pips-r-ashwin-to-stay-no-1-cheteshwar-pujara-no-2-in-batting-list-1671758 |access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref> He was announced as  captain of the [[Chennai Super Kings]] IPL franchise, for the [[2022 Indian Premier League|2022 IPL season]], succeeding [[MS Dhoni]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=MS Dhoni hands over CSK captaincy to Ravindra Jadeja |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/121619/ms-dhoni-hands-over-csk-captaincy-to-ravindra-jadeja |access-date=24 March 2022 |website=Cricbuzz |date=24 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He however stepped down in the middle of the season.<ref name="HT2022"/>

'''Kannaur Lokesh Rahul''' ({{IPA|kn|kaɳːuːɾ loːkeːʃ ɾaːhul|lang}}; born 18 April 1992) is an Indian [[cricket]]er. He plays for the [[India national cricket team|Indian national cricket team]]. He is a former Indian cricket team captain. Rahul represents the [[Karnataka cricket team]] in Indian domestic cricket and [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. He is currently the vice-captain of the Indian cricket team in the [[Test cricket|ODI cricket]] format.

Rahul made his international debut in 2014 against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] in the [[Boxing Day Test]] in [[Melbourne Cricket Ground|Melbourne]]. Two years after his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut, Rahul made his [[One Day International|One-Day International]] debut in 2016 against [[Zimbabwe national cricket team|Zimbabwe]], where he scored his first century by hitting a six on the last ball to reach 100* (115) from 94 (114), which was also the only six of the entire match. Rahul is the first and only Indian cricketer to score an ODI [[Century (cricket)|century]] on his debut. On the same tour, he made his [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] debut.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=KL Rahul|publisher=ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/kl-rahul-422108}}</ref>

'''Jasprit Jasbirsingh Bumrah''' ({{IPA|pa|dʒəsˈpɾiːt̪ bʊmˈɾaː|lang}}; born 6 December 1993) is an Indian International [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[India national cricket team|Indian national cricket team]] in all formats of this game and has captained India in [[Test cricket|Tests]] and [[Twenty20 International|T20Is]]. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest bowlers in the history of cricket. Bumrah became the first bowler to reach the No. 1 position in the [[ICC Men's Player Rankings]] across all three formats and the first Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in Tests, One Day Internationals, and Twenty20 Internationals. He represents [[Gujarat cricket team|Gujarat]] in domestic cricket and the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL).<ref name="NDTV">{{Cite news |title=Jasprit Bumrah Scripts ICC Rankings History With Never-Seen-Before Feat For India |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/australia-vs-india-2024-25/jasprit-bumrah-touches-unprecedented-high-in-indian-cricket-beats-r-ashwins-test-rankings-record-7376425 |work=NDTV |date=1 January 2025 |access-date=1 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Why Jasprit Bumrah is currently world's best bowler across formats |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/showstoppers/why-jasprit-bumrah-is-currently-worlds-best-bowler-across-formats/94972/1 |work=Forbes India |date=31 December 2024 |access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Is Jasprit Bumrah the GOAT? Glenn Maxwell hails Indian pacer as the 'best all-format bowler of all time' |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/in/cricket/news/jasprit-bumrah-glenn-maxwell-best-all-format-bowler-all-time/791da41bce13f7738a5d46ac |work=The Sporting News |date=28 October 2024 |access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=The Bumrah experience: What it's like facing the world's best bowler|url=https://www.wisden.com/series/india-vs-england-m-2025/cricket-news/the-bumrah-experience-what-its-like-facing-the-worlds-best-bowler|work=Wisden|date=18 June 2024 |access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Jasprit Bumrah is best ever all-format fast bowler: Michael Clarke|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/jasprit-bumrah-best-ever-all-format-fast-bowler-michael-clarke-2661379-2025-01-08 |magazine=India Today |date=8 January 2025 |access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref>

Among Indian fast bowlers, he was the fastest to 200 [[Test cricket|Test]] wickets and the second fastest to 100 [[One Day International|ODI]] wickets. He was a crucial member of the Indian team that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]], where he was named the Player of the Tournament for taking 15 wickets with an average economy of 4.17.

Bumrah made his domestic debut in the [[2012–13 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] and also helped his team clinch its maiden title victory. His [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut came against [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]], during the [[2013–14 Ranji Trophy|2013–14 season]] of the [[Ranji Trophy]]. Bumrah was signed by the Mumbai Indians for the [[2013 Indian Premier League|2013 season]] of IPL. Since then, he has played for MI, contributing to the team's title wins five times. He is the second highest wicket-taker for MI after [[Lasith Malinga]], with 181 wickets in 142 matches.

Bumrah made his international debut in January 2016 during [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2015–16|India's tour of Australia]], where he emerged as the highest wicket-taker of the [[Twenty20 International|T20]] series. In 2016, he was the highest wicket-taker in a calendar year in T20I cricket, with 28 wickets. He made his Test debut in 2018 against [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]]. {{As of|2023|12|since=y}}, he has served as the [[Captain (cricket)|vice-captain]] of the Indian team in Test cricket and has also captained the team thrice in the absence of regular skipper [[Rohit Sharma]]. He was named in the [[ICC Men's Test Team of the Year]] in 2018 and 2024, in the [[ICC Men's ODI Team of the Year]] in 2017 and 2018, and in the [[ICC Men's T20I Team of the Year]] in 2024. Additionally, he was named in the [[ICC Awards of the Decade|ICC Men's T20I Team of the Decade]] for 2011–2020. Bumrah was awarded the [[Polly Umrigar Award]] by the [[Board of Control for Cricket in India|BCCI]] thrice, in 2018–19, 2021–22 and 2023–24. He was also named in the [[Wisden Cricketers of the Year]] in 2022.

Notably, Bumrah achieved a milestone in 2024 by surpassing [[Ravichandran Ashwin]]'s highest ICC Test bowling rating for an Indian bowler. Bumrah concluded the year as the leading wicket-taker in Test cricket, with 71 wickets, and reached a career-high rating of 908 points, placing him joint-16th on the all-time list. His performances, including a nine-wicket haul in the Melbourne Test in December 2024, secured his position as the top-ranked bowler in the [[ICC Men's Test Team Rankings|ICC Men's Test Rankings]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=Jasprit Bumrah surpasses Ashwin's all-time record to set new high in ICC Test rankings |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/india-in-australia/jasprit-bumrah-surpasses-ashwins-all-time-record-to-set-new-high-in-icc-test-rankings/articleshow/116852899.cms |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257 |date=1 January 2025 |access-date=1 January 2025}}</ref><ref name="NDTV"/> and led to him being awarded the [[Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy]] and the [[ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year]] in the [[2024 ICC Awards]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/tournaments/world-test-championship/news/india-bowling-icon-named-icc-men-s-test-cricketer-of-the-year |title=India bowling icon named ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year |work=[[International Cricket Council]] |date=27 January 2025 |access-date=27 January 2025}}</ref>

'''Akshar Rajeshbhai Patel''' (born 20 January 1994) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er.<ref>{{cite web |title=Akshar Patel |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/554691.html |access-date=1 February 2015 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He plays for the [[India national cricket team|Indian national team]] as an [[all-rounder]] in all the three formats. He is a left-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batter]] and slow [[Left-arm orthodox spin|left-arm orthodox bowler]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Axar Patel Profile - Cricket Player India {{!}} Stats, Records, Video |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/axar-patel-554691 |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> Patel represents [[Gujarat cricket team|Gujarat]] in domestic cricket and captains [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. He was part of the Indian teams that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] and [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026]] [[Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cups]] and the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy|2025 Champions Trophy]].

He made his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut on 15 June 2014 against [[Bangladesh Cricket Team|Bangladesh]]. He was selected in India's 15-man squad for the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] held in [[Australia cricket team|Australia]] and [[New Zealand cricket team|New Zealand]]. He made his Test debut for [[Indian cricket team|India]] against [[England cricket team|England]] on 13 February 2021, where he took 7 wickets.<ref>{{cite web|title=2nd Test, Chennai, Feb 13 - Feb 17 2021, England tour of India 2021|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-tour-of-india-2020-21-1243364/india-vs-england-2nd-test-1243385/live-cricket-score|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=16 February 2021 |access-date=27 November 2022}}</ref> He became the ninth bowler for [[Indian cricket team|India]] to take a [[List of India cricketers who have taken five-wicket hauls on Test debut|five-wicket haul on debut]] in [[Test cricket]].<ref name=IT>{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/india-vs-england-axar-patel-joins-elite-list-after-taking-5-wicket-haul-on-test-debut-1769727-2021-02-16|title=India vs England: Axar Patel joins elite list after taking 5-wicket haul on Test debut|work=India Today|date=16 February 2021|access-date=27 November 2022}}</ref>

'''Prithvi Pankaj Shaw''' ({{IPA|hi|ˈpɾɪt̪ʋiː ʃɔː|lang}}; born 9 November 1999)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportsmintmedia.com/happy-birthday-prithvi-shaw-a-look-at-the-young-openers-net-worth-and-endorsements/|title=Happy Birthday Prithvi Shaw| work=Sports Mint |date=9 November 2022|access-date=10 August 2023}}</ref> is an Indian [[cricket]]er who has played for the [[India national cricket team|Indian cricket team]] in all formats. He represents [[Maharashtra cricket team|Maharashtra]] in domestic cricket and [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. Shaw captained the Indian team that won the [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2018 U19 Cricket World Cup]].

A right-handed opening batter, Shaw made his first international appearance aged 18 on 4 October 2018 and became the second-youngest Indian after [[Sachin Tendulkar]] to make a [[Test cricket|Test]] [[century (cricket)|century]] and the youngest Indian to do so on Test debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/cricket-news/article/prithvi-shaw-slams-ton-on-debut-becomes-second-youngest-indian-to-reach-three-figure-mark/294113 |title=Prithvi Shaw slams ton on debut, becomes 2nd-youngest Indian after Sachin Tendulkar to reach three-figure mark |work = Times Now |date=4 October 2018 |access-date=4 October 2018}}</ref>

Shaw made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Mumbai cricket team|Mumbai]] in the semi-finals of the [[2016–17 Ranji Trophy]] on 1 January 2017.<ref name="FC">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1053699.html |title=Ranji Trophy, 1st Semi-final: Mumbai v Tamil Nadu at Rajkot, Jan 1–5, 2017 |access-date=1 January 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He scored a century in the second innings and was man of the match.<ref name="FC"/> Shaw earned another distinction by scoring a century in his debut [[Duleep Trophy]] and equalled the record held by [[Sachin Tendulkar]], who had scored a century in each in his debut matches in the [[Ranji Trophy]] and Duleep Trophy.

The [[International Cricket Council]] named Shaw as one of the five breakout stars in men's cricket in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/948077 |title=2018 lookback – the breakout stars (men) |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=1 January 2019}}</ref> In July 2019, he was suspended by [[Board of Control for Cricket in India]] for a doping violation, the suspension lasting until November of the same year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/cricketer-prithvi-shaw-suspended-for-eight-months-for-doping-violation-2077754|title= Cricketer Prithvi Shaw Suspended For Eight Months For Doping Violation|publisher=[[NDTV Sports]] |date= 30 July 2019}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=BCCI's timeline of Prithvi Shaw's doping case |language=en |newspaper=India Today |agency=Ist |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/bcci-prithvi-shaw-doping-case-bcci-wada-anti-doping-prithvi-shaw-drugs-ipl-1578846-2019-08-08 |access-date=21 August 2019}}</ref>

'''Rashid Khan Arman'''{{Efn|{{langx|ps|راشد خان ارمان|translit=Rāshid Khān Armān}}}} (born 20 September 1998) is an Afghan international [[cricket]]er and captain of the [[Afghanistan national cricket team|Afghanistan national team]] in the [[T20I|T20I format]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Rashid Khan appointed Afghanistan's T20I captain .Regarded as one of the greatest player in T20I history,he broke several records.|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/rashid-khan-afghanistan-cricket-captain-t20i/article66317011.ece |access-date=29 December 2022 |work=[[Sportstar]] |date=29 December 2022 |language=en}}</ref> In franchise leagues, he plays for [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL), [[Adelaide Strikers]] in Australia's [[Big Bash League]] (BBL), [[Lahore Qalandars]] in the [[Pakistan Super League]] (PSL), [[Band-e-Amir Dragons]] in Afghanistan's [[Shpageeza Cricket League]] and [[MI New York]] in [[Major League Cricket]] (MLC). He [[Bowling (cricket)|bowls]] right-arm [[leg spin]] and is an aggressive right-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batsman]].<ref name="Bio">{{cite web|title=Rashid Khan|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/zimbabwe/content/player/793463.html|access-date=18 October 2015|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He was one of the eleven cricketers to play in Afghanistan's first [[Test cricket|Test match]], against [[India national cricket team|India]], in June 2018. He returned the most expensive bowling figures by a debutant (154 runs for 2 wickets in 34.3 overs) in a nation's maiden Test match.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://crictracker.com/stats-rashid-khan-co-turn-expensive-on-their-first-outing/|title=Stats: Rashid Khan & Co turn expensive on their first outing - CricTracker|date=15 June 2018|work=CricTracker|access-date=15 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> In September 2019, he led the team in the one-off Test [[Afghan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2019–20|against Bangladesh]], and at the age of 20 years and 350 days, became the youngest cricketer to captain a Test match team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/rashid-khan-youngest-test-captain-afghanistan-bangladesh-chittagong/2019-09-04 |title=Rashid to become Test cricket's youngest captain |work=Cricket Australia |access-date=5 September 2019}}</ref>

In June 2017, he took the best bowling figures (7 wickets for 18 runs) for an associate nation in a [[One Day International]] (ODI) match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/40231787 |title=Rashid Khan: Afghanistan spinner takes 7–18 against West Indies |access-date=9 June 2017 |work=BBS Sports}}</ref><ref name="Rashidspecial">{{cite web |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/rashid-khan-continues-international-surge-after-record-haul-vs-west-indies/story-P7ZT8iAsoFWGhQBOVlA0LM.html |title=Afghan sensation Rashid Khan continues surge after record haul vs West Indies |access-date=9 June 2017 |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref> In February 2018, he became the youngest player to top the [[ICC Player Rankings]] for bowlers in ODIs.<ref name="youngest">{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/623441 |title=Rashid Khan: The youngest No.1 in men's cricket |access-date=20 February 2018 |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref> Later the same month, he also topped the ICC Player Rankings for bowlers in T20Is.<ref name="T20I-rank">{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/628507 |title=Rashid, Munro and Maxwell take top spots in T20I rankings |access-date=25 February 2018 |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref> In September 2018, he became the number one player in the ICC's [[all-rounder]] rankings, following his performance at the [[2018 Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/864074 |title=Rashid Khan jumps to No.1 in ODI all-rounders' rankings |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=30 September 2018}}</ref>

In March 2018, during the [[2018 Cricket World Cup Qualifier]], he [[Afghan national cricket captains#One Day Internationals|captained Afghanistan]] for the first time in an ODI match. At the age of 19 years and 165 days, he became the youngest player to captain an international team.<ref name="Khan-Youngest">{{Cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/630348 |title=Why we can't get enough of Rashid Khan |access-date=4 March 2018 |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref> In the final of the Cricket World Cup Qualifier, against the [[West Indies national cricket team|West Indies]], Khan became the fastest and youngest bowler to take 100 wickets in ODIs when he dismissed [[Shai Hope]].<ref name="Khan100">{{Cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/rashid-khan-19-year-old-afghanistan-leg-spinner-becomes-fastest-to-reach-100-odi-wickets-1197523-2018-03-25 |title=Rashid Khan, 19-year-old Afghanistan leg-spinner, becomes fastest to reach 100 ODI wickets |access-date=25 March 2018 |work=India Today|date=25 March 2018 }}</ref> He took 44 matches to take his 100th dismissal, breaking the previous record of 52 matches, set by [[Mitchell Starc]] of Australia.<ref name="Khan100"/> In June 2018, he became the fastest bowler, in terms of time, to take 50 wickets in T20Is. He reached the milestone in two years and 220 days, in the first T20I [[Bangladeshi cricket team against Afghanistan in India in 2018|against Bangladesh]].<ref name="Khan50">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1148392.html |title=Advantage Afghanistan in spin-friendly Dehradun |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=2 June 2018 |access-date=3 June 2018}}</ref> In October 2021, he also became the fastest bowler, in terms of matches, to take [[List of Twenty20 International records#Most wickets in a career|100 wickets in T20I cricket]], in his 53rd match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/icc-mens-t20-world-cup/2021/news/afg-vs-pak-rashid-khan-fastest-to-100-t20i-wickets-afghanistan-pakistan-shakib-malinga-southee/article37228710.ece |title=AFG vs PAK: Rashid becomes fastest bowler to pick 100 T20I wickets |work=SportStar |date=29 October 2021 |access-date=29 October 2021}}</ref>

In April 2019, the [[Afghanistan Cricket Board]] (ACB) named Khan as the team's new T20I captain, replacing [[Asghar Afghan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1169014 |title=Asghar |access-date=5 April 2019}}</ref> In June 2019, during the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], Khan played in his 100th international cricket match for Afghanistan.<ref name="Khan100CWC">{{cite web|url=https://cricketaddictor.com/cricket/icc-cricket-world-cup-2019-match-7-afghanistan-vs-sri-lanka-stats-preview/ |title=ICC Cricket World Cup 2019 (Match 7): Afghanistan vs Sri Lanka – Stats Preview |work=Cricket Addictor |date=4 June 2019 |access-date=4 June 2019}}</ref> Following the World Cup, Khan was appointed as captain of the Afghanistan cricket team across all formats.<ref>{{cite '''Rishabh Rajendra Pant''' ({{IPA|hi|ɾɪˈʂʌbʰ ɾaː'dʒeːd̪ɾə pʌnt̪|lang}}; born 4 October 1997) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[India national cricket team|Indian national team]] as a [[Wicket-keeper|wicket-keeper batter]]. He plays for the [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] and [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in domestic cricket.

Pant became the most expensive player in the history of the [[Indian Premier League]] when he was bought for {{INRConvert|27.00|c}} by the [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the 2025 league auction. He was a member of the Indian team that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]] and [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy|2025 Champions Trophy]]. He was the vice-captain of the [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup squads|India U19 team]] that was runner-up at the [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2016 U19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="India">{{cite web |title=Ishan Kishan to lead India at U19 World Cup |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ishan-kishan-to-lead-india-at-u19-world-cup-954021 |access-date=22 December 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He made his [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] debut for India in January 2017, his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut in August 2018, and his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut in October 2018. He holds the record for most sixes hit by an Indian batter in Test cricket, and the third most overall. In June 2022, Pant was named as the Indian captain for the T20I series [[South African cricket team in India in 2022|against South Africa]], after the designated captain [[KL Rahul]] was ruled out of the series due to an injury.<ref name=":5" />

'''Ruturaj Dashrat Gaikwad''' (born 31 January 1997) is an Indian [[cricketer]] who plays for the [[India national cricket team]]. He is a right-handed [[batting order (cricket)|top order]] [[batter (cricket)|batter]]. He captained the Indian team that won the gold medal in the [[Cricket at the 2022 Asian Games – Men's tournament|2022 Asian Games]].

Ruturaj made his [[T20 International]] debut for the Indian team against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] in July 2021. He played his first [[One Day International]] in October 2022 against [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]]. In domestic cricket, he plays for [[Maharashtra cricket team|Maharashtra]] and captains the side in the [[Twenty20|T20]] and [[List A]] formats. He holds the records for the most number of [[century (cricket)|centuries]] in the [[Vijay Hazare Trophy]] and the fastest century for Maharashtra in List A cricket. He has also represented the [[West Zone cricket team|West Zone]] and captained the [[Rest of India cricket team|Rest of India]] side in the past.

In franchise cricket, Ruturaj plays for and captains the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL). He has won the IPL title in [[2021 Indian Premier League|2021]] and [[2023 Indian Premier League|2023]] with the Super Kings. He was the leading run-scorer in the [[2021 Indian Premier League|2021 IPL season]] and won emerging player of the season award.

'''Shubman Gill''' (born 8 September 1999) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[India national cricket team|India national team]]. Gill captains India in [[Test cricket|Tests]] and [[One Day International|ODIs]], the [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] and [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] when he plays [[first-class cricket]]. He has also captained India in [[Twenty20 International|T20I]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=India Test Squad For England Tour 2025, LIVE Updates: Shubman Gill Appointed Captain; New Vice Captain Is... {{!}} Cricket News |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/england-vs-india-2025/india-test-squad-announcement-live-updates-england-tour-2025-new-captain-shubman-gill-jasprit-bumrah-rishabh-pant-bcci-8494289 |access-date=2025-05-24 |website=NDTVSports.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250705-shubman-gill-the-prince-who-is-now-india-s-new-cricket-king|title=Shubman Gill, the 'Prince' who is now India's new cricket king|date=5 July 2025|website=France 24}}</ref> A right-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batsman]], Gill represents Punjab in domestic cricket.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web |title=Shubman Gill Profile – Cricket Player India |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/shubman-gill-1070173 |access-date=24 February 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In [[One Day International|ODI]] cricket, he is the fastest player to reach 2000 runs, in 38 innings, and 2500 runs, in 50 innings.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Shubman Gill Breaks Hashim Amla's Record, Becomes Fastest To 2000 ODI Runs |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/icc-world-cup/news/shubman-gill-breaks-hashim-amlas-record-becomes-fastest-to-2000-odi-runs/articleshow/104630831.cms |work=Times of India}}</ref> He also holds the record for the youngest cricketer to score a double century in ODIs at the age of 23.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Sublime Shubman Gill Hits Maiden ODI Double Century, Becomes Youngest To Attain The Feat |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/new-zealand-in-india/sublime-shubman-gill-hits-maiden-odi-double-century-becomes-youngest-to-attain-the-feat/articleshow/97092976.cms |work=Times of India}}</ref> With his country, he won the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]] as vice captain. He made his [[List A cricket|List-A]] debut against [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]] in 2017 and [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Punjab against [[Bengal cricket team|Bengal]] in the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]], scoring a half-century in the game,<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 November 2017 |title=Ranji Trophy 2017: Bengal inch closer to quarterfinal berth with innings victory over Punjab |work=[[The Indian Express]] |agency=[[Press Trust of India|PTI]] |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/ranji-trophy-2017-bengal-inch-closer-to-quarterfinal-berth-with-innings-victory-over-punjab-4945137/ |access-date=24 February 2023}}</ref> and 129 runs in the last match against [[Services cricket team|Services]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 November 2017 |title=Ranji Trophy 2017: Punjab in command with Shubman Gill, Anmolpreet Singh tons |work=[[The Indian Express]] |agency=[[Press Trust of India|PTI]] |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/ranji-trophy-2017-punjab-in-command-with-shubman-gill-anmolpreet-singh-tons-4954353/ |access-date=24 February 2023}}</ref>

As vice-captain of the [[India national under-19 cricket team|Indian under-19 team]], Gill scored 372 runs at an average of 124.00 in the [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]], where he played a crucial role in India's fourth title win, earning the edition's Player of the Tournament award.<ref>{{Cite news |date=5 February 2018 |title=How Shubman Gill, player of ICC U-19 World Cup, polished his 'Virat Kohli shot' |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/how-shubman-gill-player-of-icc-u-19-world-cup-polished-his-virat-kohli-shot/story-a9AuYnkNLFeTIXDZk5RysK.html |access-date=24 February 2023 |work=[[Hindustan Times]]}}</ref> His unbeaten 102 in the semi-final against [[Pakistan national under-19 cricket team|Pakistan U-19]] drew praise from batting greats such as [[Rahul Dravid]], [[Sachin Tendulkar]], [[VVS Laxman]], and [[Sourav Ganguly]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thaly |first=Dattaraj |date=30 January 2018 |title=ICC Under-19 World Cup: Shubman Gill Impresses With High-Quality Hundred Against Pakistan |work=[[NDTV Sports]] |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/icc-under-19-world-cup-2018/icc-under-19-world-cup-shubman-gill-impresses-with-high-quality-hundred-against-pakistan-1806215 |access-date=24 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Shubman Gill a better player than Prithvi Shaw: Sourav Ganguly |work=India Today |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/shubman-gill-a-better-player-than-prithvi-shaw-sourav-ganguly-to-india-today-1157220-2018-01-30 |access-date=30 January 2018}}</ref>

Shubman Gill was named [[ICC Awards#Men's Player of the Month|ICC Men's Player of the Month]] four times — in January 2023, September 2023, February 2025, and July 2025. He is also the first male player to win the award four times.<ref>{{Cite web |last=icc |date=2025-03-12 |title=Gill and King win ICC Player of the Month awards for February |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/gill-and-king-win-icc-player-of-the-month-awards-for-february |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=icc |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-05 |title=ICC Men's Player of the Month award: Which Indians have won the ICC award? {{!}} Sporting News India |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/in/cricket/news/icc-mens-player-month-award-which-indians-have-won-icc-award/970c7600de4528f1abab8469 |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=www.sportingnews.com |language=en-in}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=icc |date=2025-08-12 |title=Gill and Dunkley named ICC Players of the Month for July 2025 |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/gill-and-dunkley-named-icc-players-of-the-month-for-july-2025 |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=icc |language=en}}</ref> He was also named in the [[ICC Men's ODI Team of the Year|ICC Men's ODI Team of the Year]] in 2023. He is one of 2 batters, alongside [[Rohit Sharma]], to have hit more than one ODI double century.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=30 September 2026 |title=Gill cracks 200, becomes only 2nd batter with multiple ODI double centuries |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/shubman-gill-second-200-rohit-sharma-multiple-odi-double-centuries-10901235/lite/ |website=[[The Indian Express]]}}</ref>

'''Varun Chakravarthy Vinod''' (born 29 August 1991) is an Indian international [[cricketer]] who plays for the [[India national cricket team|India national team]] as a right-arm [[leg spin]] bowler. He was a member of the Indian team that won the [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026 T20 World Cup]], [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy|2025 Champions Trophy]] and the [[2025 Asia Cup]]. '''Mohammed Shami Ahmed'''{{efn|In his early career, Shami was often referred to as Shami Ahmed in media reports.}} ({{IPA|hi|ʃʌmiː|lang}}; born 3 September 1990) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er who plays as a right-arm [[fast bowling|fast-bowler]] for the [[India national cricket team]], for the [[Bengal cricket team]] in domestic cricket,<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 January 2015 |title=World Cup: How India discovered Mohammed Shami via Kolkata |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/worldcup2015/world-cup-how-india-discovered-mohammed-shami-via-kolkata/story-CSaAg2s6hUWPJIcf9xSHvO.html |access-date=13 December 2023 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> and for the [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. He also plays for [[Mohun Bagan AC (cricket)|Mohun Bagan]] in domestic competitions of [[West Bengal]].

One of the most consistent wicket takers in contemporary world cricket, Shami bowls the ball off the seam and uses [[Swing bowling|swing]], including [[reverse swing]], to move the ball both directions. He has been reputed to have an edge in the [[Death over bowling|death overs]] of a limited-overs innings and, in all formats, has been described as being at times "unplayable". Shami finished as the tournament's leading wicket taker in the [[2023 Cricket World Cup|ICC World Cup 2023]], and was also the fastest bowler to take 50 wickets in the 48-year history of the [[Cricket World Cup]], spanning 13 editions. He is the recipient of the [[List of Arjuna Award recipients (2020–2029)|2023]] [[Arjuna Award]] for Cricket. Having taken 7 wickets for 57 runs against New Zealand in the 2023 Cricket World Cup semi-final, he holds the record for the best figures for an Indian Bowler in ODIs and is currently the only Indian bowler to have taken 7 wickets in an ODI innings.<ref>{{Citation |title=List of India One Day International cricket records |date=24 August 2024 |work=Wikipedia |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_India_One_Day_International_cricket_records |access-date=26 October 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Shami was a member of the Indian team that won the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]].

'''Kieron Adrian Pollard''' (born 12 May 1987) is a [[Trinidadians and Tobagonians|Trinidadian]] [[cricket]]er, who captained the [[West Indies cricket team]] in [[limited overs cricket]]. He used to play in various T20 leagues around the globe as an all-rounder. He also used to captain [[MI Cape Town]], [[MI Emirates]] and [[MI New York]] in the [[SA20]], [[International League T20|ILT20]] and [[Major League Cricket|MLC]] respectively. He is currently playing for the [[Trinbago Knight Riders]] in the [[Caribbean Premier League]]. He is also the batting coach of the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] and was the assistant coach of the [[England cricket team]] for the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024]]. He was part of the [[2012 ICC World Twenty20]] winning team for West Indies. During his period, he was one of the most aggressive batsmen and he also has the record of six [[Boundary (cricket)|6s]] in an over against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka.]]

In September 2019, Pollard was named as the captain of the West Indies [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) teams.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kieron Pollard named West Indies ODI, T20I captain |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kieron-pollard-named-west-indies-odi-t20i-captain-1200156 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/kieron-pollard-to-lead-west-indies-in-odi-and-t20i-series-against-afghanistan-in-india/story-ZtVC8Of0iiN9WVh7JR88CN.html|title=Kieron Pollard to lead West Indies in ODI and T20I series against Afghanistan in India|date=2019-10-16|website=Hindustan Times|language=en|access-date=2019-10-16}}</ref> In March 2020, he became the first cricketer to play in 500 [[Twenty20]] matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aninews.in/news/sports/cricket/kieron-pollard-becomes-first-player-to-play-500-t20s20200304202444 |title=Kieron Pollard becomes first player to play 500 T20s |work=ANI News |access-date=4 March 2020}}</ref> His game has been suited for limited overs formats, in which he has enjoyed a long international career; he has never played [[Test cricket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/one-of-the-best-t20-players-but-not-good-enough-to-play-test-cricket-david-gower-on-kieron-pollard/story-Jzlfj0IqhbgeY4OAU9emwI.html|title=One of the best T20 players but not good enough to play Test cricket: David Gower on Kieron Pollard|work=Hindustan Times|date=2 September 2020 |access-date=2 July 2021}}</ref> In a match against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] in March 2021, he hit six [[Boundary (cricket)|sixes]] in one over bowled by [[Akila Dananjaya]] and became the third batsman to do so in international cricket after [[Herschelle Gibbs]] and [[Yuvraj Singh]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-04 |title=Kieron Pollard becomes 2nd player after YUVRAJ Singh to hit six sixes in an over in T20Is - WATCH |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/west-indies-vs-sri-lanka-kieron-pollard-becomes-2nd-player-after-yuvraj-singh-to-hit-six-sixes-in-an-over-in-t20s-101614824257156.html |access-date=2021-03-04 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2022, in the second match [[West Indian cricket team in India in 2021–22#T20I series|against India]], Pollard became the first cricketer for the West Indies to [[List of West Indies Twenty20 International cricket records#Most career matches|play in 100 T20I matches]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/india-vs-west-indies-second-t20i-series-kieron-pollard-set-for-100th-appearance/article38427794.ece |title=India vs West Indies 2nd T20I: Kieron Pollard set for 100th appearance |work=SportStar |date=17 February 2022 |access-date=18 February 2022}}</ref>

On April 20, 2022, Pollard announced his retirement from international cricket.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kieron Pollard retires from international cricket |work=ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/west-indies-allrounder-kieron-pollard-retires-from-international-cricket-1311662 |access-date=20 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportstiger.com/breaking-news-kieron-pollard-announces-retirement-from-international-cricket/ |title=Kieron Pollard announces retirement from international cricket |access-date=20 April 2022|website=SportsTiger|date=20 April 2022 }}</ref> On November 15, 2022, Pollard announced his retirement from [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] after playing for Mumbai Indians for 13 seasons. He was then appointed as the batting coach for Mumbai Indians.

'''Shikhar Dhawan''' (born 5 December 1985) is an Indian former [[cricket]]er who played as an [[opening batter]]. He was a regular member of the Indian team in limited-overs formats for over a decade and represented [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in domestic cricket.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rajesh |first1=S |title=Shikhar Dhawan, the king of global ODI tournaments |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/india-news-shikhar-dhawan-retires-the-king-of-the-odi-world-cup-and-the-champions-trophy-1448571 |website=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |date=24 August 2024 |access-date=24 August 2024}}</ref> He was leading run scorer and also named as the Player of the Tournament in the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]] and even he was leading run-scorer by an Indian at the [[2015 Cricket World Cup#Statistics|2015 World Cup]]. Across ICC World Cups and Champions Trophies, he averaged 65.15, the highest among players with over 1000 runs.<ref>{{cite web |title=ICC Cricket World Cup, 2014/15 / Records / Most runs |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/icc-cricket-world-cup-2015/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6537;type=tournament |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823120058/http://stats.espncricinfo.com/icc-cricket-world-cup-2015/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6537%3Btype%3Dtournament |archive-date=23 August 2015 |access-date=22 February 2015 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Dhawan made his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] in October 2010 at [[Visakhapatnam]]. His [[Test cricket|Test]] debut came against the same opposition in March 2013 at [[Mohali]], where he scored the fastest century by any batsman on [[List of centuries scored on Test cricket debut|Test debut]] (85 balls) and ended his innings with 187 runs from 174 balls. This is also the highest score by an Indian on a Test debut.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/28235.html |title=Shikhar Dhawan | Cricket Players and Officials |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 August 2013 |archive-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225202412/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/28235.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=8 June 2017 |title=Does Dhawan raise his game for ICC tournaments? |work=ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/does-shikhar-dhawan-raise-his-game-for-icc-tournaments-1102094 |access-date=26 July 2017 |archive-date=16 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416030656/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/does-shikhar-dhawan-raise-his-game-for-icc-tournaments-1102094 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In August 2013, Dhawan scored 248 off 150 balls for India A against South Africa A in a List A match, which was then the second-highest individual score in the format.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wisdenindia.com/match-report/magnificent-dhawan-powers-india-win/72096|title=Magnificent Dhawan powers India A win|publisher=Wisden India|date=12 August 2013|access-date=12 August 2013|archive-date=25 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225202417/http://www.wisdenindia.com/match-report/magnificent-dhawan-powers-india-win/72096|url-status=live}}</ref> He later became the first Indian to score a century in his 100th ODI, during a match against South Africa in Johannesburg. On 14 June 2018, he scored a century before lunch on the opening day of a Test against Afghanistan.<ref name="Dhawan">{{cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/ind-vs-afg-shikhar-dhawan-enters-exclusive-club-with-87-ball-hundred-1259981-2018-06-14 |title=IND vs AFG: Shikhar Dhawan enters exclusive club with 87-ball hundred |access-date=14 June 2018 |work=India Today |date=14 June 2018 |archive-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225202409/https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/ind-vs-afg-shikhar-dhawan-enters-exclusive-club-with-87-ball-hundred-1259981-2018-06-14 |url-status=live }}</ref> Dhawan also went through phases of [[Shikhar Dhawan#Struggle with form|inconsistent form]], both in domestic and international cricket.<ref>{{cite web |title=Finally, Dhawan's chance to shine |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/finally-shikhar-dhawan-s-chance-to-shine-624800 |website=ESPN |access-date=July 20, 2025 |date=March 12, 2013}}</ref> On 24 August 2024, Dhawan announced his retirement from all forms of cricket.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sports |first=Times of |title=Shikhar Dhawan Retires From All Forms of International Cricket |url=https://www.timesofsports.com/cricket/news/shikhar-dhawan-retires-from-all-forms-of-cricket/ |access-date=24 August 2024 |work=[[Times of Sports]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/india-batter-announces-retirement-from-all-cricket |title=Shikhar Dhawan announces retirement from all cricket |work=International Cricket Council |date=24 August 2024 |access-date=24 August 2024 |author1=Icc }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://fantasykhiladi.com/news/shikhar-dhawan-retirement-from-international-and-domestic-cricket/ |title=Shikhar Dhawan Announces Retirement from International and Domestic Cricket |date=24 August 2024 |access-date=24 August 2024}}</ref>

'''Virat Kohli''' (born 5 November 1988) is an Indian [[Cricket|international cricketer]] and former all-format [[Captain (cricket)|captain]] of the [[India national cricket team|Indian national cricket team]]. He is a right-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batter]] and an occasional right-arm medium-[[Bowling (cricket)|pace bowler]]. Considered one of the greatest batters in cricket, he has been acclaimed for his batting skills and records. Kohli has the [[List of One Day International cricket records#Most centuries|most centuries in ODIs]] and the [[List of cricketers by number of international centuries scored#Men's international cricket|second-most centuries in international cricket]] with [[List of international cricket centuries by Virat Kohli|86 tons]] across all formats. He is also the leading run-scorer in the [[List of Indian Premier League records and statistics#Individual batting records|Indian Premier League]].

Kohli was the captain of the [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2008 U19 World Cup]] winning team and was a crucial member of the Indian teams that won [[2011 Cricket World Cup]], [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy|2013 Champions Trophy]], [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]], and [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy|2025 Champions Trophy]]. He plays for [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] in the Indian Premier League and for [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in [[Cricket in India|domestic cricket]]. In 2013, Kohli was ranked number one in the ODI batting [[ICC Men's Player Rankings|rankings]]. In 2015, he achieved the same in T20I cricket. In 2018, he was ranked number one in Test cricket, making him the only Indian to hold the top spot in all three formats. He is the first player to score 20,000 international runs in a decade. He was the [[ICC Awards of the Decade|Cricketer of the Decade]] for [[2011-2020 ICC Awards of the Decade|2011 to 2020]].

Kohli has won ten [[ICC Awards]], making him the most awarded player in international cricket history. He won the [[ICC ODI Player of the Year|ODI Player of the Year]] award four times, in 2012, 2017, 2018, and 2023. He won the [[Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy|Cricketer of the Year]] award on two occasions, in 2017 and 2018. In 2018, he became the first player to win all three major ICC awards including Cricketer of the Year, ODI Player of the Year and Test Player of the Year in the same year. He was honored with the Spirit of Cricket Award in 2019 and given the [[ICC Awards of the Decade|Cricketer of the Decade]] and ODI Cricketer of the Decade in 2020. Kohli was named the [[Wisden Leading Cricketer in the World|''Wisden'' Leading Cricketer in the World]] for three consecutive years.

Kohli has won the most Player of the Series and second-most [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Player of the Match]] awards to his name in all three formats combined. He was honoured with the [[Arjuna Award]] in 2013, the [[Padma Shri]] in 2017, and India's highest sporting honour, the [[Khel Ratna Award]], in 2018. ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' included him on its [[Time 100|100 most influential people in the world]] list in 2018. Kohli has been deemed one of the most commercially valuable athletes, with estimated earnings of {{INR convert|634|c|year=2023}} in 2022.

After winning the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]] being named Player of the Match award in the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup final|final]], Kohli announced his retirement from T20Is. On 12 May 2025, at the age of 36, he announced his retirement from the Test cricket. He is married to actress [[Anushka Sharma]], and they have two children.

'''Ravichandran Ashwin''' ({{IPA|ta|ɾaʋitɕand̪iɾan aɕʋin|lang}}; {{audio|Ravichandran Ashwin.ogg|pronunciation}}) (born 17 September 1986) is an Indian [[cricket]]er. He is a right-arm [[off spin]] bowler and a [[Batting order (cricket)|lower order]] batter. Widely regarded as one of the most prolific spinners of all time, he represented the [[India national cricket team|Indian cricket team]] and was part of the Indian team that won the [[2011 Cricket World Cup]] and the [[2013 Champions Trophy]]. He represented [[Tamil Nadu cricket team|Tamil Nadu]] and [[South Zone cricket team|South Zone]] in domestic cricket.

Ashwin has taken more than 500 [[wicket]]s in [[Test cricket|Tests]] and was the fastest bowler to reach 300 test wickets in terms of number of innings. He has won eleven [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Man of the Series]] awards in Tests, which is the most for any cricketer, along with [[Muttiah Muralitharan]]. As an [[all-rounder]] in Test cricket, he bats down the order, has scored six Test centuries and is one of only three players to have scored 3000 runs and taken 500 wickets in Tests. He had been the highest-ranked bowler in the [[ICC Men's Player Rankings|ICC men's player rankings]] multiple times, and holds the record for the second highest rating points by an Indian bowler ever in Test cricket.

Ashwin started as an [[opening batsman]] but dropped down the order due to limited success and turned into an off-break bowler. He made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Tamil Nadu in December 2006 and captained the team the following season. He played for the [[Chennai Super Kings]] (CSK) in the [[2010 Indian Premier League]], where his economical bowling led to his maiden international call-up in the limited-overs formats in June 2010. He was the leading wicket-taker and player of the tournament of the [[2010 Champions League Twenty20]], which was won by CSK. He also won the [[2014 Champions League Twenty20]] and two IPL titles ([[2010 Indian Premier League|2010]], [[2011 Indian Premier League|2011]]) with CSK.

In 2011, Ashwin made his Test debut against [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] and became the seventh Indian bowler to [[List of India cricketers who have taken five-wicket hauls on Test debut|take a five-wicket haul]] on debut. He had greater success with the turning tracks in the [[Indian subcontinent]], including taking 29 wickets in a series against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]], the most by any Indian bowler in a four-match Test series. In the 2015–16 season, he took 48 wickets and scored 336 runs in eight Test matches, along with 27 wickets in 19 T20Is, enabling him to win the [[ICC Awards#Men's awards|ICC Cricketer of the Year]] and [[ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year]] awards for 2016. He has been named five times to the [[ICC Men's Test Team of the Year]] and was named in the [[ICC Awards of the Decade|ICC Men's Test Team of the Decade]] 2011–20. In 2015, he was awarded the [[Arjuna award]] by the [[Government of India]]. On 18 December 2024, Ashwin announced his retirement from all forms of international cricket. He was awarded the [[Padma Shri]], the fourth highest civilian award, by the [[Government of India]] in January 2025.

'''Kane Stuart Williamson''' (born 8 August 1990)<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.cricket.com.au/players/CA:160/kane-williamson | title=Kane Williamson – Biography | website=www.cricket.com.au | access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref> is a former international cricketer who [[Captain (cricket)|captained]] the [[New Zealand national cricket team]] in all formats of the game. A right-handed batsman and an occasional [[off spin]] bowler, Williamson is the leading run-scorer for New Zealand in [[Test cricket]] and is widely regarded as one of the world's best contemporary batsmen and one of the greatest New Zealand captains and batsmen of all time. He captained [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] to victory in the [[2021 World Test Championship final|2021 ICC World Test Championship final]] and to the finals of the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]] and [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup|2021 T20 World Cup]]. He was also a part of the New Zealand squad to finish as [[2015 Cricket World Cup final|runners-up]] at the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] and the [[2025 Champions Trophy|2025 ICC Champions Trophy]]. Williamson retired from international cricket on 12 June 2026.

Williamson made his [[first-class cricket]] debut while still a schoolboy at [[Tauranga Boys' College]], in December 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/159/159052/First-Class_Matches.html|title=List of First Class Matches Played by Kane Williamson|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=7 November 2010}}</ref> He made his U-19 debut against the touring [[India Under-19 cricket team|Indian U-19 team]] the same year and was named captain of the [[New Zealand Under-19 cricket team|New Zealand U-19 team]] for the [[2008 U-19 Cricket World Cup]]. He made his international debut in 2010. Williamson has represented New Zealand at the [[2011 ICC Cricket World Cup|2011]], [[2015 ICC Cricket World Cup|2015]], [[2019 ICC Cricket World Cup|2019]] and [[2023 ICC Cricket World Cup|2023]] editions of the [[Cricket World Cup]] and [[2012 World Twenty20|2012]], [[2014 World Twenty20|2014]], [[2016 World Twenty20|2016]], [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup|2021]], [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022]] and [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] editions of the [[Men's T20 World Cup|ICC World Twenty20]]. He made his full-time captaincy debut for New Zealand in the 2016 [[Men's T20 World Cup|ICC World Twenty20]] in [[India]]. He captained New Zealand at the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], leading the team to the [[2019 Cricket World Cup Final|final]] and winning the [[Cricket World Cup awards#Awards summary|Player of the Tournament award]] in the process. On 31 December 2020, he reached a Test batting rating of 890, surpassing [[Steve Smith (cricketer)|Steve Smith]] and [[Joe Root]] as the number one ranked Test batsmen in the world.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/cricket-kane-williamson-rises-to-number-one-in-world-test-batting-rankings/EPPVZHDNGLJ2MCF6LBAZQU5MVA/|title=Cricket: Kane Williamson rises to number one in world test batting rankings|publisher=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=13 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/1960320/|title=Williamson overtakes Smith and Kohli to top position |publisher=ICC|access-date=2 January 2021}}</ref> He was nominated for the Sir Garfield Sobers Award for ICC Male Cricketer of the Decade, and the award for Test cricketer of the decade. [[Ian Chappell]] and [[Martin Crowe]] have ranked Williamson among the top four Test cricket batsmen, along with [[Joe Root]], [[Steve Smith (cricketer)|Steve Smith]], [[Virat Kohli]] of the current era.<ref>{{cite web |title=Test cricket's young Fab Four |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/martin-crowe-test-cricket-s-young-fab-four-774705 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Virat Kohli, Joe Root, Steven Smith, Kane Williamson 'Fab Four' of Tests: Martin Crowe|date=29 August 2014|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/virat-kohli-joe-root-steven-smith-kane-williamson-fab-four-of-tests-martin-crowe/|publisher=The Indian Express|access-date=13 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Big four? What about Warner? |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ian-chappell-big-four-ought-to-be-five-with-warner-in-there-1120679 |access-date=10 May 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Williamson was the only New Zealander to be named in the ICC Test Team of the Decade (2011–2020).<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1956753/|title=Kohli named captain of ICC Test Team of the Decade|publisher=ICC|access-date=2 January 2021}}</ref> He won the ICC Spirit of Cricket award in 2018. The late former New Zealand cricketer [[Martin Crowe]] noted that "we're seeing the dawn of probably our greatest ever batsman" in Williamson.<ref>{{cite news|last=Alderson|first=Andrew|title=Crowe: Key to Cup win is fearlessness|url=http://m.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=11383165|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=7 January 2015|access-date=23 April 2017}}</ref> In June 2021, he captained New Zealand to win the inaugural [[World Test Championship|ICC World Test Championship]], the first ICC trophy the team won since winning the [[2000 KnockOut Trophy|2000 ICC KnockOut Trophy]]. In November 2021, he led New Zealand to the [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup final|final]] of the [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup|ICC T20 World Cup]]. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest batsmen of his generation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 February 2023 |title=Kane Williamson: New Zealand's greatest ever batsman |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/sport/484966/kane-williamson-new-zealand-s-greatest-ever-batsman |access-date=3 February 2024 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref> Williamson retired from all international cricket on June 12, 2026, with immediate effect, after making 0 and 18 against England at Lords. Speaking on the decision, Williamson said "I've thought about it for a while, but over the last few days it's become clear now is the right time," and "I've always felt a strong drive and hunger for international cricket, and I take pride in knowing I've given it my all in every match I've played for New Zealand. Continuing with anything less wouldn't be right and I feel fortunate to step away on my own terms.<ref name="espncricinfo.com">{{Cite web |date=12 June 2026 |title=Kane Williamson retires from international cricket |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kane-williamson-retires-from-international-cricket-1540723 |access-date=12 June 2026 |website=[[Cricinfo]] |language=en-nz}}</ref>

'''Trent Alexander Boult''' (born 22 July 1989) is a New Zealand [[cricket]]er who represented the [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand cricket team]] in all formats between 2011 and 2024. He continues to play in various [[Twenty20]] leagues around the globe as a [[Fast bowling|fast bowler]]. Boult was a key member of the New Zealand team that won the [[2019–2021 World Test Championship|2019–2021 ICC World Test Championship]]. He was also a part of the New Zealand squads to finish as runners-up in two [[List of Cricket World Cup finals|Cricket World Cup finals]] in [[2015 Cricket World Cup|2015]] and [[2019 Cricket World Cup|2019]].

He is a left-arm fast-medium bowler and a right-handed batsman,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://content-www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/story/339952.html  |title=New Zealand's prospects hinge on in-form bowlers |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=16 September 2008}}</ref> Boult made his Test debut for New Zealand in December 2011 and his One Day International debut the following July. He was the joint leading wicket taker at the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.icc-cricket.com/cricket-world-cup/stats/2015/player/most-wickets |title=Most wickets – player: Cricket World Cup 2015 |year=2015 |publisher=ICC Cricket |access-date=13 April 2015}}</ref> In November 2018, he became the third bowler for New Zealand to [[List of One Day International cricket hat-tricks|take a hat-trick in ODIs]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Trent Boult, the third New Zealander to take a hat-trick|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/trent-boult-the-third-new-zealander-to-take-a-hat-trick-1164408|access-date=25 January 2022|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> while in June 2019, Boult became the first bowler for New Zealand to take a hat-trick in the [[Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="CWCHT">{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/world-cup-2019-trent-boult-creates-history-becomes-first-nz-bowler-to-take-hat-trick-in-a-world-cup/story-5siju06GwxPGi0NocslIWJ.html |title=World Cup 2019: Trent Boult creates history, becomes first NZ bowler to take hat-trick in a World Cup |work=Hindustan Times |date=29 June 2019 |access-date=29 June 2019}}</ref>

'''Joseph Charles Buttler''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|MBE}} (born 8 September 1990) is an English international [[cricket]]er and the former captain of the [[England cricket team]]. He plays for [[Lancashire County Cricket Club|Lancashire]] in domestic cricket and has played in multiple [[Twenty20|T20]] leagues. Widely regarded as England's greatest-ever white-ball cricketer,<ref>{{Cite web | title=Jos Buttler is our greatest ever white-ball cricketer | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2020/09/07/jos-buttleris-greatest-ever-white-ball-cricketer/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200908044903/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2020/09/07/jos-buttleris-greatest-ever-white-ball-cricketer/ | access-date=2026-09-04 | archive-date=2020-09-08}}</ref> he is known for his innovative and aggressive batting style. He was part of the England team that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup|2019 ODI World Cup]] and led the team to victory at the [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]].

Buttler made his [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] debut in 2011, his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut in 2012, and his Test debut in 2014. He was the vice-captain and a crucial member of the [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#England|England team]] that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], and made the [[run out]] during the [[Super Over]] which sealed victory in the [[2019 Cricket World Cup final|final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48983890|title=England men win first Cricket World Cup|work=BBC Sport |access-date=15 July 2019|archive-date=15 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190715181544/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48983890|url-status=live}}</ref> He was appointed captain of England's [[Limited overs cricket|limited-overs]] teams in June 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/61994862|title=Jos Buttler named England white-ball captain after Eoin Morgan retirement|work=BBC Sport |access-date=30 June 2022}}</ref> He captained England to victory at the [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]], top-scoring for his country at the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63613694|title=T20 World Cup: England beat Pakistan to win pulsating final in Melbourne|work=BBC|access-date=13 November 2022|date=13 November 2022}}</ref>

Buttler plays as a right-handed [[Wicket-keeper|wicket-keeper-batsman]] and is England's most-capped T20I player.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/individual/most_matches_career.html?class=3&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=1 November 2021|archive-date=7 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107074617/https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/individual/most_matches_career.html?class=3;id=1;type=team|url-status=live}}</ref> Along with [[Adil Rashid]], he holds the world record for highest seventh-wicket stand in ODIs: 177 against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] during their [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2015|2015 tour of England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/252072.html|title=Records. '''Patrick <!--NOTE: Do not add "Pat" here per [[WP:HYPOCORISM]].--> James Cummins''' (born 8 May 1993) is an  international [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[Australian national cricket team|Australian men's cricket team]] in all three formats, captaining the team in both [[Test cricket|Test]] and [[One Day International]] cricket. A right-armed [[Fast bowling|pace bowler]], he also captains the [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].

Making his international debut in [[limited-overs cricket]] in 2011, Cummins came to prominence following his Test debut that same year [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2011–12|against South Africa]]. There, he became the youngest Australian test cricketer since 1953 and took six wickets during the second innings of his debut test match. His struggles with injuries then forced him out of all international cricket until 2015, where he was a member of the tournament-winning Australian [[2015 Cricket World Cup|Cricket World Cup]] squad. Only returning to Test cricket in 2017 [[Australian cricket team in India in 2017–18|against India]], he became known as one of the greatest fast bowlers in the world.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cherny |first1=Daniel |last2=Perik |first2=Jon |date=24 December 2019 |title=Barking obvious: Cummins the best bowler in the world |url=https://www.theage.com.au/sport/cricket/barking-obvious-cummins-the-best-bowler-in-the-world-20191224-p53mqw.html |work=The Age |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=27 December 2021 |title=Is Pat Cummins Already One Of The Great Fast Bowlers? |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/england-in-australia-2021-22/cricket-news/is-pat-cummins-already-one-of-the-great-fast-bowlers |access-date=4 April 2025 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title="I've got him in the top three of my time": Fleming's incredible praise for Cummins |url=https://www.sen.com.au/news/2022/12/03/ive-got-him-in-the-top-three-of-my-time-flemings-incredible-praise-for |access-date=12 January 2023 |website=[[Sports Entertainment Network]] |first=Seb |last=Mottram |date=3 December 2022 |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, he achieved 914 points in the [[ICC Men's Player Rankings|ICC Men's Test Bowling Rankings]], joint-highest for any Australian an fifth-highest for any bowler. He was also awarded with the [[Allan Border Medal]] in the same year. In 2023, he was awarded with the [[Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy]].

Cummins was named the [[List of Australia national cricket captains|Australian cricket captain]] in November 2021, and is also regarded as one of the best bowler captains in history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2021 |title=Pat Cummins: the pace-bowling captain who could prove a pioneer |first=Ali |last=Martin |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2021/dec/03/pat-cummins-the-pace-bowling-captain-who-could-prove-a-pioneer |access-date=12 January 2023 |website=[[The Guardian]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Vijaykumar |first=Ajit |date=12 January 2025 |title=Is Pat Cummins the greatest cricketer and captain of the modern era? |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2025/01/12/is-pat-cummins-the-greatest-cricketer-and-captain-of-the-modern-era/ |work=The National |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref> He captained Australia to win the [[2021–2023 World Test Championship]] and the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]] and took Australia to the [[2023–2025 World Test Championship|2023–25 ICC World Test Championship]] final.
