'''Glenn James Maxwell''' (born 14 October 1988) is an Australian professional [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[Australia national cricket team]] in [[Twenty20 International]]s (T20I). He also plays for [[Victoria cricket team|Victoria]] in domestic cricket and the [[Melbourne Stars]] in the [[Big Bash League]]. He previously played both [[Test cricket|Test]] and [[One Day International]] (ODI) cricket.

A right handed [[all-rounder]] who is known for his sometimes unorthodox batting, Maxwell originally bowled [[fast bowling|medium-pace]] before switching to off-spin at a young age. He rose to prominence in 2011 after setting an at-the-time record for the fastest [[Century (cricket)#Half-century|half-century]] in [[One-Day Cup (Australia)|Australian domestic one day cricket]]—scoring 51 runs from 19 balls. The record led to his international debut, playing an ODI against [[Australian cricket team against Afghanistan in the UAE in 2012|Afghanistan in 2012]], before making his T20I debut a month later [[Australian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2012|against Pakistan]] and his Test debut against [[Australian cricket team in India in 2012–13#1st Test|India the year after]]. {{as of|2026}}, he has played 7 Test matches, 149 ODIs and 130 T20I matches, the latter being the most of any Australian player.<ref>{{cite web |title=Most matches for Australia in T20s |url= https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/team/individual-most-matches-career/australia-2/twenty20-matches-6 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=30 December 2025}}</ref>

Maxwell has held numerous international batting records over his career. After scoring 104 against [[Australian cricket team in India in 2016–17#3rd Test|India in 2017]], Maxwell became the second Australian to have scored [[List of cricketers with centuries in all international formats|centuries in all three international cricket formats]]. Alongside [[Rohit Sharma]], he holds the record for the most career T20I centuries—both having scored 5. At the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]], he achieved a century in 40 balls against [[Netherlands national cricket team|the Netherlands]], the fastest century scored at a [[Cricket World Cup]] and [[List of One Day International cricket records#Fastest centuries|fourth fastest in ODIs]]. Against [[Afghanistan national cricket team|Afghanistan]] a month later, he set a new record for the fastest double century scored at the same event, the [[List of One Day International cricket records#Fastest double centuries|second fastest in ODI cricket]]—the innings regarded as one of the greatest in ODI history.

Known for his dramatic shot making and improvisation in short forms of the game,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fidel Fernando |first=Andrew |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8917/report/995467/ |title=Australia canter to win after record 263, Maxwell slams 145* |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=6 September 2016 |access-date=9 February 2018 |archive-date=8 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180208005353/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8917/report/995467/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Maxwell was part of the Australian squads that won the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]], the [[2021 T20 World Cup]], and the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]]. His ability to make unconventional shots, like reverse sweeps and pulls, often makes it hard to set fields that cover all of his scoring areas.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ramsey |first=Andrew |date=16 August 2014 |title=Maxwell reveals new 'mystery shot' |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/3259343/maxwell-reveals-new-mystery-shot |work=Cricket Australia |access-date=30 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Chopra |first=Aakash |date=10 February 2015 |title=What makes Maxwell different |url=https://www.espn.com.au/cricket/story/_/id/21294910/makes-glenn-maxwell-different |work=ESPN |access-date=30 December 2025}}</ref>

'''Suryakumar Ashok Yadav''' (born 14 September 1990), also known by his initials '''SKY''', is an Indian cricketer and [[List of India national cricket captains|former captain]] of the [[Twenty20 International]] team, a role he held as India won the [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup]] and the [[2025 Asia Cup]]. He was part of the national team that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup]] and the [[2023 Asia Cup]].

Yadav started playing club cricket in [[Mumbai]] before he was selected for the [[Mumbai cricket team]]. He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Mumbai in February 2010 before making his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] and [[T20 cricket|T20]] debut in the same year. In March 2021, he made his T20I debut and later made his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut in July of the same year. He has mainly played [[limited overs cricket|limited-overs cricket]] for India, having played his only [[Test cricket|Test]] match in February 2023. He was named as the captain of the Indian team for first time in November 2023 and was re-appointed as the captain of the Indian T20I team in July 2024 after the previous captain [[Rohit Sharma]] announced his retirement from T20Is.

As of August 2024, Yadav has scored more than 3,000 runs in international cricket with four [[century (cricket)|centuries]]. More than 75% of his career runs and all of his centuries have come from T20I matches. His four T20I centuries are the second most by any batter. He held the top ranking in the [[ICC men's player rankings]] for T20Is from October 2022 to June 2024. He won the [[ICC Men's T20I Cricketer of the Year]] award in [[2022 ICC Awards|2022]] and [[2023 ICC Awards|2023]], and was also named in the [[ICC Men's T20I Team of the Year]] in 2022 and 2023.

Yadav plays for Mumbai in the Indian domestic cricket, which he has captained in the past. He plays for [[Mumbai Indians]] and has previously played for [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[Indian Premier League]], and has won one title with Kolkata in 2014 and two with Mumbai, in 2019 and 2020.

'''Sanju Viswanadh Samson ''' ({{IPAc-en|audio=Sanju Samson.wav|ˌ|s|ʌ|n|dʒ|u|_|s|æ|m|s|ən}}; born 11 November 1994) is an Indian cricketer who plays for the [[India national cricket team]] in the [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] format. He was part of the  [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] and [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026]] T20 world cup winning teams, including a Player of the Tournament performance in 2026. He plays for [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] and for the [[Kerala cricket team]] domestically.

Samson started his cricketing career in [[Delhi]] and later moved to [[Kerala]]. After making an impact in junior cricket, he made his first-class debut for Kerala in 2011. He was the vice-captain of the [[India national under-19 cricket team|Indian U19 team]] for the [[2014 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2014 U19 Cricket World Cup]]. He made his Indian Premier League debut in 2013 for Rajasthan Royals and won the [[List of Indian Premier League awards#Emerging Player of the Year|Emerging Player of the Year]]. He scored an unbeaten 212 in the [[2019–20 Vijay Hazare Trophy]], the sixth time an Indian scored a double-century in [[List A cricket]], which is also the second-fastest double-century in the format. Sanju scored his maiden ODI century in the 3rd ODI in the three-match series against [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] on 21 December 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/sa-vs-ind-sanju-samson-first-odi-hundred-paarl-9078173|title=South Africa vs India: When the door was closing on him, Sanju Samson kicks it open with maiden ODI ton in series decider|work=Indian Express|date=21 December 2023 |access-date=21 December 2023|archive-date=21 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231221191738/https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/sa-vs-ind-sanju-samson-first-odi-hundred-paarl-9078173/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/128894/samson-century-lifts-india-to-296|title=Samson century lifts India to 296|work=Cric Buzz|access-date=21 December 2023|archive-date=21 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231221191732/https://m.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/128894/samson-century-lifts-india-to-296|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Kagiso Rabada''' (born 25 May 1995) is a South African professional cricketer who plays as a right-arm [[Fast bowling|fast bowler]] for the [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa national team]]. He also represents [[MI Cape Town]] in the [[SA20]] and the [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. Since making his senior international debut in 2014, Rabada has established himself as one of the leading fast bowlers of his generation, holding one of the best [[Strike rate|bowling strike rates]] in [[Test cricket]] history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waris |first=Sarah |date=2023-12-26 |title=Kagiso Rabada, the most lethal fast bowler of all-time? |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/india-in-south-africa-2023-24/cricket-news/kagiso-rabada-the-most-lethal-fast-bowler-of-all-time |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=Wisden |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-21 |title=Rabada - the most lethal bowler in the 300-wicket club |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kagiso-rabada-the-most-lethal-striker-in-the-300-wicket-club-1456454 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251008105740/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kagiso-rabada-the-most-lethal-striker-in-the-300-wicket-club-1456454 |archive-date=2025-10-08 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He has been a pivotal figure in the national team's successes, including their victory in the [[2023–2025 World Test Championship|2023–2025 ICC World Test Championship]].

By January 2018, he had topped both the [[ICC Player Rankings|ODI bowler rankings]] and the [[ICC Player Rankings|Test bowler rankings]] aged 22. In July 2018, he became the youngest bowler to take 150 wickets in Tests.<ref name="KG150">{{cite web|url=https://www.crictracker.com/kagiso-rabada-becomes-youngest-to-claim-150-test-wickets/|title=Kagiso Rabada becomes youngest to claim 150 Test wickets|work=Crictracker|date=14 July 2018 |access-date=14 July 2018}}</ref> In July 2016, Rabada became the first cricketer to win six awards at [[Cricket South Africa]]'s annual dinner, including the prize for Cricketer of the Year.<ref name="six">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/southafrica/content/story/1039711.html |title=Rabada dominates CSA awards |access-date=27 July 2016 |publisher=[[Cricinfo]]}}</ref> In June 2018, he again won six awards at CSA's annual dinner, including Cricketer of the Year, [[Test cricket|Test]] Cricketer and [[One Day International|ODI]] Cricketer of the Year.<ref name="six2">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23679070/kagiso-rabada-sweeps-csa-awards-six-trophies-again |title=Rabada sweeps CSA awards with six trophies again |access-date=3 June 2018 |publisher=[[Cricinfo]]}}</ref> In August 2018, ''[[Wisden]]'' named him the best young player in the world.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/806038 |title=Rabada crowned Wisden's best young player in the world |work=[[International Cricket Council]] |access-date=13 August 2018}}</ref> He is one of the few bowlers to have taken a hat-trick in two different formats: ODIs and T20Is.

'''Shreyas Santosh Iyer''' (born 6 December 1994) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[India national cricket team|India national team]]. Iyer captains India in [[Twenty20 International|T20Is]] and serves as the vice-captain in [[One Day International|ODIs]]. A right-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batter]], he primarily plays as a top-order or middle-order batter across formats. Iyer also captains [[Mumbai cricket team|Mumbai]] in domestic cricket and captains the [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL).

Iyer made his international debut in 2017 and has been a regular member of India's limited-overs teams. He achieved a notable milestone on his Test debut against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] in November 2021, scoring a century in the first innings and a half-century in the second, becoming the first Indian player to record both on Test debut.<ref name="ESPN">{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1278674.html |title=1st Test, Kanpur, Nov 25–29 2021, New Zealand tour of India |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=25 November 2021}}</ref><ref name="ndtv">{{Cite news|url=https://sports.ndtv.com/india-vs-new-zealand-2021/shreyas-iyer-becomes-16th-indian-to-score-a-century-on-test-debut-2625354|title=IND vs NZ: Shreyas Iyer 16th Indian To Score Century On Test Debut|work=ndtv.com|date=26 November 2021}}</ref> Earlier in his career, he represented the [[India Under-19 cricket team|India Under-19s]] at the [[2014 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ICC Under-19 World Cup / India Under-19s Squad |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-under-19-world-cup-2014/content/squad/709629.html |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=29 December 2014}}</ref>

In major international tournaments, Iyer was part of the Indian squad that finished runners-up at the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]], during which he scored a century against New Zealand in the semi-final at the [[Wankhede Stadium|Wankhede]]. He was also a member of the teams that won the [[2023 Asia Cup]] and the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]]. For his performances, he was named [[ICC Awards#Men's Player of the Month|ICC Men's Player of the Month]] in February 2022 and March 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Shreyas Iyer Scripts History, Becomes First Player In World To... |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/shreyas-iyer-scripts-history-becomes-first-player-in-world-to-8170085 |work=NDTV |date=15 April 2025 |access-date=16 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416070423/https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/shreyas-iyer-scripts-history-becomes-first-player-in-world-to-8170085 |archive-date=16 April 2025}}</ref><ref name="Shreyas Iyer wins ICC Men's Player of the Month award">{{cite news |title=Shreyas Iyer wins ICC Men's Player of the Month award |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/shreyas-iyer-wins-icc-mens-player-of-the-month-award/articleshow/120305645.cms |work=The Times of India |date=15 April 2025 |access-date=16 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416070518/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/shreyas-iyer-wins-icc-mens-player-of-the-month-award/articleshow/120305645.cms |archive-date=16 April 2025}}</ref>

In the IPL, Iyer began his career with the then [[Delhi Daredevils]] (now Delhi Capitals) in 2015, winning the Emerging Player of the Year award in his debut season, and played for them till 2021. He later captained the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] from 2022 to 2024, leading them to the IPL title in 2024. In 2025, he was signed by the Punjab Kings for {{INRConvert|26.75|c|year=2025}}, briefly becoming the most expensive player in IPL auction history before the record was surpassed in the same auction. He led the team to the finals in the Indian Premier League 2025, ending as the runner-ups.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Shreyas Iyer wins ICC Men's Player of the Month award {{!}} Cricket News - The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/shreyas-iyer-wins-icc-mens-player-of-the-month-award/articleshow/120305645.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416070518/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/shreyas-iyer-wins-icc-mens-player-of-the-month-award/articleshow/120305645.cms |archive-date=16 April 2025 |access-date=22 December 2025 |work=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref>

On 6 June 2026 Shreyas Iyer became India's 15th T20I captain replacing [[Suryakumar Yadav]].<ref name="espncricinfo.com">{{Cite news |title=Shreyas confirmed as India's T20I captain; Suryakumar dropped |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shreyas-iyer-confirmed-as-india-s-new-t20i-captain-suryakumar-yadav-dropped-1539867 |date=6 June 2026 |access-date=6 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Arshdeep Singh''' (born 1999) is an  Indian professional [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[India national cricket team]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-09-13 |title='Dream come true, want to see him win World Cup for India now': Arshdeep Singh's family |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/t20-world-cup-india-arshdeep-singh-8147237/ |access-date=2022-10-05 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> In Indian domestic cricket, he plays for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] and for [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. Arshdeep is a left-arm [[medium-fast bowler]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web |title=Arshdeep Singh |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1125976.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180601053408/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1125976.html |archive-date=1 June 2018 |access-date=19 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He was an integral member of the Indian team that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] and [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026]] [[Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cups]], and was the joint-highest wicket taker in the former. Singh was also a member of the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy|2025 Champions Trophy]] and [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2018 U19 World Cup]] winning squads.

Arshdeep made his international debut for the Indian team in July 2022 in a [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] match against [[England cricket team|England]]. He bowled a [[maiden over]] on debut, becoming just the third Indian bowler to do so on their T20I debut.{{efn|The others were [[Jhulan Goswami]], the former captain of the Indian women's team, and [[Ajit Agarkar]] who played for India's men's team between 1998 and 2007.}}<ref name=ie8jul22>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-08 |title=First in 16 years: Arshdeep Singh becomes third Indian bowler to bowl a maiden on T20I debut |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/eng-vs-ind-arshdeep-singh-breaks-16-year-old-record-becomes-first-indian-bowler-to-bowl-a-maiden-on-t20i-debut-8016211/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905153220/https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/eng-vs-ind-arshdeep-singh-breaks-16-year-old-record-becomes-first-indian-bowler-to-bowl-a-maiden-on-t20i-debut-8016211/ |archive-date=5 September 2022 |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> Arshdeep is the first Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in T20 internationals.<ref>{{Cite news |title=New record! Arshdeep Singh creates history, becomes first Indian bowler to ... |date=2025-09-20 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/asia-cup/new-record-arshdeep-singh-creates-history-becomes-first-indian-bowler-to-/articleshow/124002277.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250919185324/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/asia-cup/new-record-arshdeep-singh-creates-history-becomes-first-indian-bowler-to-/articleshow/124002277.cms |archive-date=2025-09-19 |access-date=2025-09-20 |work=[[The Times of India]]}}</ref>

'''Yashasvi Bhupendra Kumar Jaiswal''' ({{IPA|hi|jʌʃʌˈsʋiː ˈdʒɛːswaːl|lang}}; born 28 December 2001) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[Indian national cricket team]] in all formats of this game. He made his international debut in the first Test against the [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] in [[Indian cricket team in the West Indies and the United States in 2023|July 2023]], scoring a century in his first innings in [[Test cricket]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=13 July 2023 |title=Yashasvi Jaiswal becomes India's 17th centurion on Test debut |work=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/wi-vs-ind-1st-test-yashasvi-jaiswal-becomes-india-17th-centurion-on-test-debut-1387280?platform=amp}}</ref> He plays for [[Mumbai cricket team|Mumbai]] in domestic cricket and [[Rajasthan Royals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. He was featured in [[Time 100]] Next list of [[Time (magazine)|Time Magazine]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-10-01 |title=Indian cricketer Yashasvi Jaiswal features in TIME100 Next list |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/sports/indian-cricketer-yashasvi-jaiswal-features-in-time100-next-list/articleshow/124251084.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-10-01 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

A left-handed [[Batting order (cricket)|opening batter]], Jaiswal gained particular attention when he scored double centuries in two consecutive test matches against [[England cricket team|England]] in a [[English cricket team in India in 2023–24|5-match Test series in 2024]]. He is the third Indian batter to achieve the feat after [[Vinod Kambli]] and [[Virat Kohli]]. Yashasvi is the third youngest cricketer in Test history to have two double centuries to his name after [[Sir Don Bradman]] and Vinod Kambli.<ref>{{cite web |date=18 February 2024 |title=Sachin Tendulkar's priceless words for 'double-trouble' Jaiswal, Sarfaraz: 'Couldn't see them play live but...' |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/sachin-tendulkar-priceless-words-for-double-trouble-yashasvi-jaiswal-sarfaraz-khan-couldnt-see-them-play-live-101708263849857.html |access-date=19 August 2024 |website=[[Hindustan Times]]}}</ref> In the same series, he equaled the world record held by [[Wasim Akram]] for the most number of sixes (12) scored by a [[cricket]]er in a test innings.{{citation needed|date=May 2026}} Also he became only the second Indian after [[Sunil Gavaskar]] to score 700 runs in a Test series.<ref>{{cite news |date=7 March 2024 |title=Yashasvi Jaiswal breaks Virat Kohli's record in first Test series at home, joins Sunil Gavaskar in elite club |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/yashasvi-jaiswal-breaks-virat-kohli-record-test-series-700-runs-sunil-gavaskar-ind-vs-eng-9201294/ |access-date=10 March 2024 |work=[[The Indian Express]] |language=en}}</ref>

He was a member of the Indian squad which won the gold medal at the [[Cricket at the 2022 Asian Games – Men's tournament|2022 Asian Games]] in 2023 and the finalist squad of the [[2020 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]], where he was the Player of the Tournament<ref>{{cite news |title=Yashasvi Jaiswal's U-19 World Cup Man Of The Series Trophy Broken In 2: Report |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/under-19-world-cup-2020/yashasvi-jaiswals-u-19-world-cup-man-of-the-series-trophy-broken-in-2-report-2179855 |date=13 February 2020}}</ref> and the highest run scorer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/54293925 |title=IPL 2020: Meet Yashasvi Jaiswal who left home aged 10 to pursue cricketing dream |work=BBC Sport |access-date=27 September 2020}}</ref> He was also a standby member of the Indian squad which played the [[2023 World Test Championship final|2023 ICC World Test Championship final]] and finished as runners up.<ref>{{cite news |title=WTC 2023 Final: Yashasvi Jaiswal replaces Rururaj Gaikwad in India's standby players list |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/yashasvi-jaiswal-standby-india-vs-australia-wtc-final-2023-squad-2385637-2023-05-28 |agency=India Today |date=28 May 2023}}</ref> He was also a part of the Indian team which won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]], but did not feature in any of the matches during the tournament.

'''Dwayne John "DJ" Bravo''' (born 7 October 1983) is a Trinidadian retired [[cricket]]er, former captain of the [[West Indies cricket team]] and the current mentor of [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] as well as the head coach of the other teams of the [[Knight Riders Group]], including [[Trinbago Knight Riders]]. A right-arm seam bowling [[all-rounder]], Bravo was well known for his aggressive lower-order batting and for his bowling in the final overs of a match. During his prime, he was regarded as one of the best [[Glossary of cricket terms#bowling at the death|death bowlers]] in T20 cricket.<ref>{{cite news|title= death-becomes him|url=https://www.thecricketmonthly.com/story/1141333/death-becomes-him |access-date=2 April 2018}}</ref> He also performs as a singer.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bravo! Dancing Dwayne's 'Champion' tune has Windies on song |url=http://gulfnews.com/sport/cricket/world-twenty20/bravo-dancing-dwayne-s-champion-tune-has-windies-on-song-1.1703234 |access-date=4 April 2016}}</ref>

Between 2004 and 2021, Bravo represented in 40 [[Test cricket|Test matches]], 164 [[One Day International|ODI matche]]s and 91 [[Twenty20 International|T20I matche]]s for the West Indies. He was a key member of the West Indies team that won the [[2004 ICC Champions Trophy]], the [[2012 ICC World Twenty20]] (where he took the winning catch), and the [[2016 ICC World Twenty20]]. After initially announcing his retirement from international cricket in October 2018, he came out of retirement in December 2019 in preparation for the [[2020 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2020 T20 World Cup]].

In domestic cricket, Bravo has played for his native [[Trinidad and Tobago national cricket team|Trinidad and Tobago]] since 2002. He played for a number of other teams in leagues around the world until his retirement in September 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/c9qv0q5qrv7o|title=West Indies legend Bravo retires from cricket|date=27 September 2024 |publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=27 September 2024}}</ref>

'''David Andrew Warner''' (born 27 October 1986) is an Australian former international [[cricket]]er, captain of [[Big Bash League]] team [[Sydney Thunder]] and captain of [[Pakistan Super League]] team [[Karachi Kings]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/psl-2025-david-warner-takes-over-from-shan-masood-as-karachi-kings-captain-1478008 | title=Warner to lead Karachi Kings in PSL 2025 }}</ref> A left-handed [[Batting order (cricket)#Opening batsmen or openers|opening batter]], Warner was the first Australian cricketer in 132 years to be selected for the national team in any format without experience in [[first-class cricket]]. He captained Australia in ODIs and T20Is and served as a vice-captain across formats before his suspension and played his domestic cricket for [[New South Wales Cricket Team]]. Warner was a prominent member of the victorious Australian squad of the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]], the [[2021 T20 World Cup]], where he was the ''Player of the Tournament'', the [[2021–2023 World Test Championship|2021–2023 ICC World Test Championship]], and the [[2023 ICC Cricket World Cup]].  Warner also guided [[Indian Premier League]] team  [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] to their first and only IPL title,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 May 2021 |title=IPL 2021: David Warner replaced by Kane Williamson as Sunrisers Hyderabad captain |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/56956335 |access-date=14 April 2025 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> becoming the third Australian captain after [[Adam Gilchrist]] and [[Shane Warne]] to do so. Warner holds the record of the most international centuries as an opening batsman across all international formats. He also holds the record for most 50+ scores in [[Twenty20|T20 cricket]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=T20 matches {{!}} Batting records {{!}} Most fifties in career {{!}} ESPNcricinfo | url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/most-fifties-in-career-283488 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420023138/https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/most-fifties-in-career-283488 | access-date=2026-09-06 | archive-date=2024-04-20}}</ref>

In January 2017, he became the fourth player to win the [[Allan Border Medal]] more than once and to win the award in consecutive years. On 28 September 2017, he played in his 100th [[One Day International]] (ODI).

In March 2018, following a preliminary investigation into [[2018 Australian ball-tampering scandal|ball tampering by the Australian team]] in the third match of their [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|Test series against South Africa]], Warner was suspended and charged with bringing the game into disrepute.<ref name="cricket.com.au">{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-cameron-bancroft-david-warner-charged-cricket-australia-tampering-renshaw-burns-maxwell/2018-03-28|title=Trio suspended by Cricket Australia|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref> Following a board meeting later in the month, [[Cricket Australia]] banned Warner from all international and domestic cricket in Australia for one year, and from any leadership positions permanently.<ref name="Ban">{{Cite news|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/player-sanctions-steve-smith-cameron-bancroft-david-warner-australia-cricket-ball-tampering/2018-03-28|title=Tampering trio learn their fate|work=cricket.com.au|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref> The ban on leadership positions was lifted on 18 October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 October 2024 |title=Warner's leadership ban overturned by Cricket Australia |url=https://www.espn.com.au/cricket/story/_/id/41987465/australia-news-david-warner-leadership-banoverturned-cricket-australia |access-date=25 October 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2024, Warner played his final Test match for Australia and also announced his retirement from [[One Day International|ODI]] cricket. On 25 June 2024, Warner announced his retirement from international cricket after Australia's exit from the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 July 2024 |title=David Warner retirement: Australian opener calls curtains to international career |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/sports/david-warner-retirement-australian-opener-calls-curtains-to-international-career/articleshow/111594944.cms?from=mdr |access-date=14 April 2025 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

'''Ambati Thirupathi Rayudu''' (born 23 September 1985) is a former Indian international [[cricket]]er, commentator and politician. He played 61 limited overs matches for the [[India national cricket team]] between 2013 and 2019. He won the IPL trophy a record six times, being the only player other than [[Rohit Sharma]] to achieve this feat.  He played for [[Hyderabad cricket team|Hyderabad]] in domestic cricket, [[Mumbai Indians]] and [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL). He was a part of the Indian squad which won the [[2018 Asia Cup]]. He is a right-handed middle-order [[batsman]], who occasionally [[wicket-keeper|keeps wicket]] and bowls right-arm [[off break]]s.

Rayudu began his first-class career with [[Hyderabad cricket team|Hyderabad]] in 2002 at the age of 16 and, by the following year, was playing for [[India A]]. He captained the [[India national under-19 cricket team|India Under-19 team]] at the [[2004 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2004 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup]] and was expected to break into the senior team. Disputes with players and state association, followed by signing up with the "rebel" [[Indian Cricket League]], led to him being ignored for national team selection. He returned to domestic cricket in 2009 by accepting [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bcci-amnesty-for-79-players-407033 BCCI's amnesty offer] and terminating his ICL contract. After strong performances for Baroda in domestic cricket and Mumbai Indians in the IPL, he was named in the Indian squad for the first time in 2012. He eventually made his international debut in July 2013, in an ODI against Zimbabwe.

After being dropped from Indian squad for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup|2019 ICC World Cup]], Rayudu got an offer from Iceland cricket board to join Iceland team which he declined.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 July 2019 |title=Iceland Cricket offers Ambati Rayudu permanent residency post World Cup snub |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket-world-cup-2019/story/iceland-cricket-offers-ambati-rayudu-permanent-residency-post-world-cup-snub-1560914-2019-07-03 |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref> On 2 July 2019, he announced his retirement from all forms of international cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ambati-rayudu-announces-retirement-after-world-cup-snub/article28270143.ece|title=Ambati Rayudu retires from all forms of cricket|work=Sportstar|access-date=3 November 2018}}</ref>

On 28 May 2023, he announced his retirement from the [[Indian Premier League|IPL]]. On 29 May 2023, Rayudu announced his retirement from all forms of Indian cricket. Shortly after, in June 2023, Rayudu was added to the roster for the [[Texas Super Kings]] in the inaugural season of [[Major League Cricket]]. It was his first appearance in a franchise league outside of India.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Du Plessis, Conway, Santner, Rayudu reunite with coach Fleming at Texas Super Kings |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mlc-2023-devon-conway-mitchell-santner-ambati-rayudu-reunite-with-stephen-fleming-at-texas-super-kings-1381660 |access-date=2023-06-16 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, he announced his foray into politics in Andhra Pradesh. On 28 December 2023, he joined [[YSR Congress Party]], but left on 6 January 2024, in a record 9 days.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Livemint |date=2024-01-06 |title=Former cricketer Ambati Rayudu quits Jagan Reddy's YSRCP {{!}} Mint |url=https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/former-cricketer-ambati-rayudu-quits-jagan-reddys-ysrcp-days-after-joining-the-party-andhra-pradesh-11704530409941.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919204026/https://www.livemint.com/politics/news/former-cricketer-ambati-rayudu-quits-jagan-reddys-ysrcp-days-after-joining-the-party-andhra-pradesh-11704530409941.html |archive-date=2024-09-19 |access-date=2025-03-08 |work=mint |language=en}}</ref> On 10 January 2024, he joined the [[Janasena Party|Jana Sena Party]], stating that the party's ideologies match his more than YSRCP's.

'''Jason Jonathan Roy''' (born 21 July 1990) is an English [[cricket]]er who played for [[England cricket team|England]] in [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) cricket, and previously played for the [[Test cricket|Test]] team. In domestic cricket, he represents [[Surrey County Cricket Club|Surrey]], and has played in multiple [[Twenty20]] leagues around the world.

Born in South Africa, Roy moved to England as a child. He made his T20I debut in 2014, his ODI debut in 2015, and played for the Test team in 2019. He was part of the [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#England|England team]] that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/cricket/england-cricket-world-cup-player-ratings-how-every-star-fared-on-the-road-to-glory-a4189706.html |title=England Cricket World Cup player ratings: How every star fared on the road to glory |work=Evening Standard |date=15 July 2019 |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref>

Roy plays as a right-handed [[Batting order (cricket)#Opening batters|opening batter]]. Along with [[Alex Hales]], he holds the England record for highest ODI partnership, of 256[[Not out|*]] against Sri Lanka during their [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England and Ireland in 2016|2016 tour of England]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/fow/highest_partnerships_for_any_wicket.html?class=2&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> and previously held the England record for highest ODI score (180 against Australia during [[English cricket team in Australia in 2017–18|England's 2018 tour]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_innings.html?class=2&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> Roy was the [[List of unusual dismissals in international cricket#T20I cricket|first batter]] to be given out for [[obstructing the field]] in T20Is.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/england-v-south-africa-2017/content/story/1105570.html|title=Morris the spark as SA steal three-run win|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=26 June 2017}}</ref>

'''Quinton de Kock''' (born 17 December 1992) is a South African international [[cricket]]er and former [[Captain (cricket)|captain]] of the [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa national team]] in all three formats. He currently plays for [[Titans (cricket team)|Titans]] at the domestic level and for [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] in white ball cricket.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://supersport.com/cricket/south-africa-v-england-201920/news/200121_De_Kock_named_as_Proteas_ODI_captain |title=De Kock named as Proteas ODI captain |website=Supersport.com |access-date=21 January 2020 |archive-date=17 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217014715/https://supersport.com/cricket/south-africa-v-england-201920/news/200121_De_Kock_named_as_Proteas_ODI_captain |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was named the Cricketer of the Year at [[Cricket South Africa]]'s 2017 Annual Awards,<ref name="awards">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/southafrica/content/story/1097632.html |title=De Kock dominates South Africa's awards |access-date=14 May 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo|date=13 May 2017 }}</ref> and is considered as one of the best wicket keeper batsmen of his generation. An opening [[batsman]] and [[wicket-keeper]], de Kock made his domestic debut for the [[Highveld Lions]] during the 2012/2013 season. He quickly caught the national selectors' eye when he starred in a match-winning partnership with [[Neil McKenzie]] in the [[Champions League Twenty20|Champions League T20]] against the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL). He also finished fourth on the [[first-class cricket|first-class]] rankings, despite playing only six of the 10 matches that summer.

De Kock made his international debut in the first match of South Africa's home [[Twenty20 International]] series against the touring New Zealanders during the 2012/13 season. He was asked to keep wickets in place of [[AB de Villiers]], who asked to be rested. He has since played regularly for the team at both [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) level. In February 2014, he also made his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut for South Africa, playing solely as a batsman.

By his 20th ODI match, de Kock had already scored five centuries. He became the fourth player to score three successive one-day centuries and the second player to score four ODI centuries before his 21st birthday.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.icc-cricket.com/cricket-world-cup/news/2015/features-and-specials/85326/icc-cricket-world-cup-top-ten-debutants|title=ICC CRICKET WORLD CUP TOP TEN: DEBUTANTS|website=Icc-cricket.com|access-date=29 November 2021|archive-date=11 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211052310/http://www.icc-cricket.com/cricket-world-cup/news/2015/features-and-specials/85326/icc-cricket-world-cup-top-ten-debutants|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his 74th [[One Day International|ODI]], against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] on 10 February 2017, he became the fastest player to complete 12 [[One Day International|ODI]] hundreds, bettering [[Hashim Amla]], who had achieved the landmark in 81 innings.

Before joining the Titans in 2015, de Kock played domestic cricket for [[Gauteng cricket team|Gauteng]] and the [[Highveld Lions]]. He has also played in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) for [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]], [[Delhi Daredevils]], [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]], and [[Mumbai Indians]]. Although he opens the batting in One Day International and T20 cricket, he primarily bats in the middle order in Test cricket. In July 2020, he was named South Africa's Men's Cricketer of the Year at [[Cricket South Africa]]'s annual awards ceremony.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29410346/quinton-de-kock,-laura-wolvaardt-scoop-major-csa-awards |title=Quinton de Kock, Laura Wolvaardt scoop up major CSA awards |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=4 July 2020}}</ref> In December 2020, in the series [[Sri Lankan cricket team in South Africa in 2020–21|against Sri Lanka]], de Kock captained South Africa for the [[List of South Africa national cricket captains#Test match captains|first time in Test cricket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-in-sa-2020-21-1237354/south-africa-vs-sri-lanka-1st-test-1237356/match-preview |title=Armed with a stronger seam attack, Sri Lanka look to beat the odds again |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=25 December 2020 |access-date=26 December 2020}}</ref>

'''Jason Omar Holder''' (born 5 November 1991)<ref>{{cite web|title=Jason Holder|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-west-indies-2013/content/player/391485.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=3 February 2013}}</ref> is a [[Barbados|Barbadian]] cricketer and the former captain of the [[West Indies cricket team]]. In January 2019, he was ranked as the no. 1 all rounder in the ICC Test rankings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jason Holder|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/983074|publisher=International Cricket Council|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> In August 2019, [[Cricket West Indies]] named him as the Test Player of the Year<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27424079/jason-holder-deandra-dottin-dominate-cwi-awards |title=Jason Holder, Deandra Dottin dominate CWI awards |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 August 2019}}</ref> and on 14 April 2021, he was named one of [[Wisden Cricketers of the Year|Wisden's Five Cricketers of the Year]].<ref name=":0" /> Holder is the first West Indian male cricketer to take a [[Hat-trick (cricket)|hat-trick]] in a T20I,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mid-day.com/sports/cricket/article/jason-holder-becomes-first-west-indies-mens-bowler-take-hat-trick-t20is-23212107|title = Jason Holder becomes first West Indies' men's bowler to take hat-trick in T20Is|date = 31 January 2022}}</ref> and the 5th, to achieve both 2000 runs and 100 wickets in ODIs.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> He is also the second West Indian, after Sir [[Garfield Sobers]], to attain both 2500 runs and 150 wickets in  Tests.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /> Holder was a member of the West Indies team that won the [[2016 T20 World Cup]].

'''Ishan Pranav Kumar Pandey Kishan''' (born 18 July 1998) is an Indian International cricketer who plays for the [[India national cricket team|Indian national cricket team]]. He plays as for the Sunrisers Hyderabad In the Indian Premier League. He made his international debut in March 2021 against [[England cricket team|England]]. He captains [[Jharkhand cricket team|Jharkhand]] in domestic cricket and was [[stand-in]] captain for [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in [[Indian Premier League]] in the absence of full-time captain [[Pat Cummins]] for the first half of the [[2026 Indian Premier League|2026 season]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gollapudi |first=Nagraj |date=18 March 2026 |title=Kishan to lead Sunrisers Hyderabad in Cummins' absence |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2026-srh-ishan-kishan-to-lead-sunrisers-hyderabad-in-pat-cummins-absence-1528345 |work=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}}</ref>

In December 2022 he scored 210 runs in 131 balls in an [[One Day International|ODI]] match against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]], becoming the cricketer with the fastest ODI double century, youngest cricketer to score an ODI double century and the first to convert a maiden ODI century to a [[Century (cricket)|double century]].<ref name="ht-2022">{{Cite news |title=10 sixes, 24 fours: Full list of records broken by Ishan Kishan during monster knock of 210 in India vs Bangladesh ODI |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/ten-sixes-24-fours-full-list-of-records-broken-by-ishan-kishan-during-his-monster-innings-of-210-vs-bangladesh-101670663294208-amp.html |work=[[Hindustan Times]] |place=New Delhi |date=10 December 2022 |access-date=12 December 2022}}</ref>

He was the captain of [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup squads|India's squad]] for the [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="India">{{cite web |title=Ishan Kishan to lead India at U19 World Cup |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-under-19-world-cup-2016/content/story/954021.html |access-date=22 December 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref name="Debut" /> He was a part of the Indian squad which won the [[2023 Asia Cup]] and [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026 T20 World Cup]].

'''Krishnakumar Dinesh Karthik''' (born 1 June 1985) is an Indian [[cricket]] commentator, coach and former international cricketer. Karthik played for the [[India national cricket team]] and also captained [[Tamil Nadu cricket team|Tamil Nadu]] in domestic cricket. He is currently the mentor and batting coach for [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] and [[London Spirit]] in [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]].

Karthik made his debut for the [[Indian cricket team]] in 2004. He was the 4th Indian batsman to play 300 T20 matches.<ref name="300T20">{{cite news |last1=Kumar |first1=Utkarsh |title=IPL 2020, KXIP vs KKR: Dinesh Karthik becomes 4th Indian player to feature in 300 T20 matches |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/ipl-2020/story/dinesh-karthik-4th-indian-300-t20-matches-joins-ms-dhoni-rohit-sharma-suresh-raina-virat-kohli-next-1735310-2020-10-26 |access-date=24 November 2021 |work=India Today |date=26 October 2020 |language=en}}</ref> Karthik was a member of the team that won both the inaugural [[2007 T20 World Cup]] and the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]]. Karthik is also the first Indian ever to win a Player of The Match award in a T20 International, having done so in 2006. Known for his six hitting ability, aggressive batting style, longevity and ability to finish games strong, Karthik was viewed as a crucial asset in the [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] and the [[Indian Cricket Team|India national cricket team]] for almost two decades.

Karthik made his maiden [[Test cricket|Test]] [[Century (cricket)|century]] against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]] and was India's leading scorer in their [[Indian cricket team in England in 2007|2007 Test tour of England]],<ref>{{cite web|title =Bangladesh vs India 2nd test India tour of Bangladesh 2007|url =https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/14396/scorecard/282692/bangladesh-vs-india-2nd-test-india-tour-of-bangladesh-2007|access-date = 1 June 2007|publisher=Espn cric info }}</ref> helping [[Cricket in India|India]] win their first series in [[Cricket in England|England]] in 21 years. After a drop in form in September 2007, Karthik was dropped from the Test team and only made sporadic international appearances through 2022

Between 2018 and 2020, Karthik was the captain of [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] team [[Kolkata Knight Riders]]. He also occasionally worked as a commentator for British channel [[Sky Sports]], most notably during [[Indian cricket team in England in 2021|India's 2021 tour of England]].

'''Mark Andrew Wood''' (born 11 January 1990) is an English [[cricket]]er who played internationally for [[England cricket team|England]] in all formats, before announcing his international retirement in September 2026 due to a reoccurring knee injury. In domestic cricket, he represents [[Durham County Cricket Club|Durham]], and has played for [[Chennai Super Kings]] and [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].

Wood made his [[Test cricket|Test]], [[One Day International|One Day International (ODI)]] and [[Twenty20 International|Twenty20 International (T20I)]] debuts in 2015. He was part of the England teams that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/cricket/england-cricket-world-cup-player-ratings-how-every-star-fared-on-the-road-to-glory-a4189706.html |title=England Cricket World Cup player ratings: How every star fared on the road to glory |work=Evening Standard |access-date=15 July 2019|date=15 July 2019 }}</ref> and [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63613694|title=T20 World Cup: England beat Pakistan to win pulsating final in Melbourne|work=BBC|access-date=13 November 2022|date=13 November 2022}}</ref>

Wood plays as a right-handed [[Fast bowling|fast bowler]], and is currently one of the fastest bowlers in the world, with an average Test pace of 89 mph since 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricviz.com/the-insight-edge-with-ig-mark-woods-2021-22-ashes-series/|title=THE INSIGHT EDGE, WITH IG – Mark Wood's 2021/22 Ashes Series|work=CricViz|date=19 January 2022|access-date=22 May 2022}}</ref>

'''Bhuvneshwar Kumar Singh''' (born 5 February 1990) is an Indian [[cricketer]] who has played for the [[India national cricket team|Indian cricket team]] in all three formats of the game. He plays for [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] and [[Uttar Pradesh cricket team|Uttar Pradesh]] in domestic cricket. A right-arm [[Fast bowling|medium]] bowler, he is known for his ability to effectively swing the ball both ways at will. Kumar was a member of the India team that won the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]]. He is the first bowler to win the IPL Purple Cap in two consecutive seasons.

He made his international debut in December 2012 against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]], taking three wickets in a [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I), including one in his first over. He went on to make his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut in the series which followed, where he took a wicket on his first ball.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/about/bhuvneshwar-kumar/|publisher=[[The Indian Express]]|access-date=21 October 2021|title=Bhuvneshwar Kumar Biography}}</ref><ref name="BKbio">{{cite web|url=https://www.crickacademy.com/bhuvneshwar-kumar-biography/|publisher=Crick Academy|access-date=21 October 2021|title=Bhuvneshwar Kumar – Biography|last=Nanda|first=Chinmay|date=5 March 2018|archive-date=20 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520160919/https://www.crickacademy.com/bhuvneshwar-kumar-biography/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is the first Indian bowler to take a [[five-wicket haul]] in [[Test cricket]], ODIs and T20Is.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/india-vs-south-africa-1st-t20i-johannesburg-bhuvneshwar-kumar-becomes-first-indian-bowler-to-take-five-wickets-in-each-of-the-three-formats/200394|title=IND vs SA: Bhuvneshwar Kumar becomes first Indian bowler to take five-wickets in each of the three formats|work=Times Now |date=18 February 2018 |access-date=31 March 2019}}</ref> He is the only bowler whose first wicket in all three formats of the game was [[bowled]]. He was named as [[ICC Awards#Men's Player of the Month|ICC Men's Player of the Month]] award for March 2021. During the [[2022 Asia Cup]], he was the highest wicket taker with 11 wickets.

'''Yuzvendra "Yuzi" Chahal''' (born 23 July 1990) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[India national cricket team]] in [[Limited overs cricket]] as a [[leg spin]] bowler. He also represents [[Haryana cricket team|Haryana]] in domestic cricket, [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]], and [[Northamptonshire County Cricket Club|Northamptonshire]] in [[County Championship]].

Chahal was the second player, and first Indian, to take [[List of five-wicket hauls in Twenty20 International cricket|a 6 wicket haul in T20I history]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Yuzvendra Chahal Biography, Records, Achievements, Career & Stats |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/player/yuzvendra-chahal |access-date=28 April 2019 |website=Sportskeeda.com}}</ref> He was the first concussion substitute to be named [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|player of the match]] in an international cricket match.<ref>{{cite web |title=Yuzvendra Chahal: concussion substitute for Ravindra Jadeja, also Man of the Match |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/30447740/aus-vs-ind-1st-t20i-yuzvendra-chahal-comes-concussion-sub-ravindra-jadeja |access-date=4 December 2020 |work=ESPNcricinfo|date=4 December 2020 }}</ref> He is a former [[chess]] player and represented India internationally. He was part of the Indian team which won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 T20 World Cup]]; however, he did not feature in any of the matches during the tournament.

'''Kuldeep Yadav''' (born 14 December 1994) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er. A [[left-arm unorthodox spin]]ner, he plays for [[Uttar Pradesh cricket team|Uttar Pradesh]] in domestic cricket and [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the [[2022 Indian Premier League|Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|date=January 31, 2021 |title=Kuldeep Yadav reflects on his need to perform consistently for Kolkata Knight Riders ahead of IPL 2021|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/kuldeep-yadav-chinman-performance-consistency-kkr-ipl-cricket-1764510-2021-01-31|access-date=2021-08-29|magazine=India Today|language=en}}</ref> He was a member of the Indian team that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] and [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026]] [[Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cups]] and the [[2025 Champions Trophy]].

Yadav has played for the [[India Under-19 cricket team|Indian Under-19 cricket team]] and played in the [[2014 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2014 U19 Cricket World Cup]]. On 18 December 2019, against the West Indies, he became the first bowler for India to take two hat-tricks in international cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28324821/stats-rohit-sharma-second-only-sachin-tendulkar |title=Stats - Rohit Sharma second only to Sachin Tendulkar |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 December 2019}}</ref> On 17 January 2020, in the second ODI [[Australian cricket team in India in 2019–20|against Australia]], Yadav became the fastest [[spin bowling|spin bowler]] for India, in terms of innings, to take 100 wickets in ODI cricket, in his 58th innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news18.com/cricketnext/news/india-vs-australia-kuldeep-yadav-becomes-fastest-indian-spinner-to-get-100-odi-wickets-2462661.html |title=India vs Australia: Kuldeep Yadav Becomes Fastest Indian Spinner to Get 100 ODI Wickets |work=Network18 Media and Investments Ltd |access-date=17 January 2020}}</ref> He helped his national team to win the [[2018 Asia Cup]] as he took the most wickets during the tournament at 10 along with [[Rashid Khan]] and [[Mustafizur Rahman]], and being the highest wicket taker for India. He made his international test debut against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] in [[Dharamshala]] on 25 March 2017.

'''Nicholas Pooran''' ({{IPAc-en|pron|ˌ|p|uː|r|ɑː|n|}}; born 2 October 1995) is a Trinidadian [[cricket]]er who represented the [[West Indies cricket team]] in limited overs formats until 2024 and served as the team's captain. He also competes domestically for [[Trinidad and Tobago national cricket team|Trinidad and Tobago]] and plays for the [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL). Pooran made his international debut for the West Indies in September 2016. In May 2022, he was appointed captain of the West Indies limited-overs team. He stepped down from captaincy in November 2022. In June 2025, he announced his retirement from international cricket.

'''Mustafizur Rahman''' ([[Bengali language|Bengali]]: মুস্তাফিজুর রহমান; born 6 September 1995) is a Bangladeshi [[international cricket]]er. A left-arm [[Fast bowling|fast-medium]] bowler,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mustafizur Rahman Profile - Cricket Player Bangladesh {{!}} Stats, Records, Video |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/mustafizur-rahman-330902 |access-date=2024-03-23 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> he is recognized for his most prolific 'slower cutters' all over the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mustafizur Rahman Records, Test match, ODI, T20, IPL international batting bowling fielding records |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/mustafizur-rahman-330902/tests-odi-t20-records |access-date=2 July 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Want Mustafizur Rahman to become the leader of the Bangladesh bowling attack: Sanjay Manjrekar |url=https://www.daijiworld.com/news/newsDisplay?newsID=995403 |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=www.daijiworld.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Rathi |first1=Tejas |date=21 April 2022 |title=Mustafizur Rahman reveals the strategy to prolong his career |url=https://cricket.one/news/news-details/62e146c03094a4d5d6db3f10/mustafizur-rahman-reveals-the-strategy-to-prolong-his-career |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=OneCricket |language=en}}</ref> He has taken more wickets in the death overs of [[Twenty20 International]]s than any other bowler.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Isam |first1=Mohammad |title=Fizz at the finish: Mustafizur Rahman is on a roll, but can he keep India quiet? |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/asia-cup-2025-mustafizur-rahman-is-on-a-roll-but-can-he-keep-india-quiet-1504177 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=10 October 2025 |date=23 September 2025}}</ref> His career took off during the [[2015 Bangladesh Premier League]] when he caught the attention of cricket pundits with his ability to bowl accurate cutters and slower deliveries, earning him the nickname "''The Fizz'''''.'''"<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 December 2022 |title=Indian duo helped Mustafizur Rahman got his 'Fizz' back: Allan Donald |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/india-in-bangladesh/indian-duo-helped-mustafizur-rahman-got-his-fizz-back-allan-donald/articleshow/96345534.cms |access-date=2 July 2023 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> This talent quickly propelled him to international prominence. He is widely regarded as one of the best Fast-bowlers in Bangladesh, especially in limited-overs cricket. He plays for [[Lahore Qalandars]] in the [[Pakistan Super League]].

Making his debut for the [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh national team]] in 2015, Mustafizur Rahman showcased his skills in the limited-overs formats. Mustafizur's international career highlights includes his debut series against [[India national cricket team|India]] in 2015, where he became the first player to claim 11 wickets in his first two [[One Day International|one day international matches]]. This  achievement propelled Bangladesh to a historic series victory over India.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teale |first=Chris |title=Mustafizur Rahman Has Debut to Remember as Bangladesh Beat India |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2500218-mustafizur-rahman-has-debut-to-remember-as-bangladesh-beat-india |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> He has represented his country in numerous international tournaments, including the [[ICC Cricket World Cup]], the [[ICC Champions Trophy]], and the [[Asia Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barclay |first=Chris |date=24 December 2016 |title=Bangladeshi fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman quickly making a mark |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/87935004/bangladeshi-fast-bowler-mustafizur-rahman-quickly-making-a-mark |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=Stuff |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Stats: The rise and rise of prolific Mustafizur Rahman |url=https://www.rediff.com/cricket/report/stats-the-rise-and-rise-of-prolific-mustafizur-rahman-india-bangladesh/20150622.htm |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=Rediff |language=en}}</ref> In club career he was acquired by [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in 2016 with a fee of $208k, where he won his first [[Indian Premier League|Indian Premier League (IPL)]] title.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 February 2016 |title=IPL: Sunrisers snap up Mustafizur for $2 lakh |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/sunrisers-snap-mustafizur-ipl-2016-213466 |access-date=2 July 2023 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=29 May 2016 |title=Sunrisers Hyderabad win first Indian Premier League title after tense final |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |agency=Reuters |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/may/29/royal-challengers-bangalore-sunrisers-hyderabad-ipl-final-match-report |access-date=2 July 2023 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He was the fifth highest wicket taker in the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian Premier League, 2016 bowling most wickets career Records |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/tournament/bowling-most-wickets-career/indian-premier-league-2016-11001 |access-date=2 July 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He has subsequently played in the IPL for [[Mumbai Indians]], [[Rajasthan Royals]], [[Delhi Capitals]] and [[Chennai Super Kings]].

He is the only overseas player to win the Emerging Player Award in [[2016 IPL]] for [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL 2016: Emerging Player of the Season – Mustafizur Rahman |url=https://www.iplt20.com/video/4671/ipl-2016-emerging-player-of-the-season-mustafizur-rahman |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=www.iplt20.com |language=en}}</ref> He was listed in [[ICC Men's ODI Team of the Year]] three times (2015, 2018, 2021) and [[ICC Men's T20I Team of the Year]] once (2021).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mustafizur Rahman in top five of ODI rankings |url=https://www.t20worldcup.com/news/944893 |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=www.t20worldcup.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Muralikrishna Prasidh Krishna''' ({{IPA|kn|pɾɐsɪd̪ːʱ kɾʊʂɳɐ|lang}}; born 19 February 1996) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prasidh Krishna profile and biography, stats, records, averages, photos and videos |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/prasidh-krishna-917159 |access-date=24 April 2021 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He plays for the [[India national cricket team|Indian national cricket team]], as a right-arm [[Fast bowling|fast-medium bowler]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prasidh Krishna {{!}} CricketArchive |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/1556/1556435/1556435.html |website=CricketArchive}}</ref> He represents [[Karnataka cricket team|Karnataka]] in domestic cricket and [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=19 March 2021|title='Possible X-factor' Prasidh Krishna latest pacer to join Indian fast-bowling arsenal for England ODIs|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/prasidh-krishna-latest-fast-bowler-to-join-team-india-squad-for-odi-series-vs-england-1781097-2021-03-19|access-date=3 September 2021|website=India Today|language=en}}</ref> He was a part of the Indian squad which won the [[2023 Asia Cup]] and were runners-up in the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]].

Krishna made his [[One Day International]] debut for the [[India national cricket team|Indian cricket team]] on 23 March 2021 in their [[English cricket team in India in 2020–21|home series against England]] and took 4 wickets in the match, breaking a 24-year-old Indian record for most wickets on ODI debut.<ref>{{Cite web|date=23 March 2021|title=India vs England: Prasidh Krishna breaks Indian record with 4-wicket haul on ODI debut|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/india-vs-england-prasidh-krishna-odi-indian-record-4-wickets-debut-1782817-2021-03-23|access-date=3 September 2021|website=India Today|language=en}}</ref> He made his Test debut at [[Centurion Park]] against [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] where he took his debut Test wicket.

'''Ashwin Hebbar''' (born 15 November 1995) is an Indian [[first-class cricket]]er who plays for [[Andhra Pradesh cricket team|Andhra Pradesh]].<ref name="Cricinfo">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/801019.html |title=Ashwin Hebbar |access-date=7 October 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He was the leading run-scorer for Andhra in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]], with 299 runs in eight matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12591;team=1592;type=tournament |title=Vijay Hazare Trophy, 2018/19 - Andhra: Batting and bowling averages |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/ashwin-hebbar-801019 |title=Ashwin Hebbar Profile  |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=7 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/ashwin-hebbar-aiming-higher/article22437379.ece |title=Ashwin Hebbar aiming higher |work=[[The Hindu]]|access-date=7 August 2024}}</ref>

As vice captain of the Vizag Warriors, Hebbar was the standout player of the 2024 Andhra Premier League, scoring 456 runs with an average strike rate of 92 in 8 innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/andhra-premier-league-2024-1439793/stats |title=APL 2024 stats |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/visakhapatnam/vizag-warriors-win-apl-title-with-ashwin-hebbars-unbeaten-91/articleshow/111740349.cms |title=Vizag Warriors emerge APL 2024 champions |work=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=27 July 2024}}</ref>

'''Priyam Garg''' (born 30 November 2000) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1070180.html |title=Priyam Garg |access-date=19 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He plays for [[Uttar Pradesh cricket team|Uttar Pradesh]] ranji team. He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Uttar Pradesh cricket team|Uttar Pradesh]] in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 19 September 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156914.html |title=Elite B, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Delhi, Sep 19 2018 |access-date=19 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Uttar Pradesh in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 1 November 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156950.html |title=Elite, Group C, Ranji Trophy at Kanpur, Nov 1-4 2018 |access-date=1 November 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In December 2018, during the match against [[Tripura cricket team|Tripura]], he scored his maiden double century in first-class cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricketcountry.com/news/ranji-trophy-2018-19-elite-c-round-7-day-2-tripura-crumble-after-priyam-garg-rinku-singh-drive-up-to-552-781994 |title=Ranji Trophy: Tripura crumble after Priyam Garg, Rinku Singh drive UP to 552 |work=Cricket Country |access-date=23 December 2018}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Uttar Pradesh in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 21 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157106.html |title=Group E, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Delhi, Feb 21 2019 |access-date=21 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2019, he was named in the India Green squad for the [[2019–20 Duleep Trophy]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Shubman Gill, Priyank Panchal and Faiz Fazal to lead Duleep Trophy sides |work=ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shubman-gill-priyank-panchal-and-faiz-fazal-to-lead-duleep-trophy-sides-1196841 |access-date=6 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cricketcountry.com/news/duleep-trophy-2019-shubman-gill-faiz-fazal-and-priyank-panchal-to-lead-duleep-trophy-2019-squad-fixtures-schedule-876560 |title=Duleep Trophy 2019: Shubman Gill, Faiz Fazal and Priyank Panchal to lead as Indian domestic cricket season opens |work=Cricket Country |access-date=6 August 2019}}</ref> In October 2019, he was named in [[India C cricket team|India C]]'s squad for the [[2019–20 Deodhar Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/deodhar-trophy-2019-squads-india-a-india-b-india-c-parthiv-patel-shubman-gill-anuma-vihari-ranchi/article29788595.ece |title=Deodhar Trophy 2019: Hanuma Vihari, Parthiv, Shubman to lead; Yashasvi earns call-up |work=SportStar |access-date=25 October 2019}}</ref> In the [[2019–20 Vijay Hazare Trophy]], he scored 287 runs in six matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.penbugs.com/the-new-sunriser-priyam-garg/ |title=The new "Sunriser"- Priyam Garg |work=Penbugs |access-date=3 October 2020}}</ref> In December 2019, he was named as the captain of India's squad for the [[2020 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcci.tv/articles/2019/news/139375/four-time-champion-india-announce-u19-cricket-world-cup-squad |title=Four-time champion India announce U19 Cricket World Cup squad |work=Board of Control for Cricket in India |access-date=2 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Priyam Garg to lead India at Under-19 World Cup |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/priyam-garg-to-lead-india-at-under-19-world-cup-1208739 |access-date=2 December 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He led India to the finals where they lost to [[Bangladesh national under-19 cricket team|Bangladesh]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-02-10|title='That was biggest factor,': India U19 captain Priyam Garg after 'bad day' in U19 World Cup final|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/that-was-biggest-factor-india-u19-captain-priyam-garg-after-bad-day-in-u19-world-cup-final/story-9q4xURdk6aadSyBDYY65tL.html|access-date=2021-10-23|website=Hindustan Times|language=en}}</ref>

In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He was released by [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] before the 2023 Indian Premier League Auction and went unsold during the auction.<ref>{{cite news |website=indianexpress.com |access-date=2023-09-12 |title=Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) complete players list, SRH squad for IPL 2023 |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/ipl-2023-auction-sunrisers-hyderabad-srhcomplete-players-list-srh-squad-for-ipl-2023-8340074/}}</ref>

'''Kona Srikar Bharat''' (born 3 October 1993) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Andhra cricket team|Andhra]] in domestic cricket. In February 2015, he became the first wicket-keeper batsman to score a triple century in the [[Ranji Trophy]].

'''Avesh Khan''' (born 13 December 1996) is an Indian international [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/694211.html |title=Avesh Khan |access-date=23 June 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[India national cricket team|international]] debut in February 2022 against [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] and was part of [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup squads|India's squad]] for the [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2016 U19 World Cup]].<ref name="India">{{cite web |title=Ishan Kishan to lead India at U19 World Cup |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ishan-kishan-to-lead-india-at-u19-world-cup-954021 |access-date=22 December 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Avesh Khan Profile - Cricket Player India {{!}} Stats, Records, Video |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/avesh-khan-694211 |access-date=2024-09-07 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> A right-arm fast-medium bowler, he is known for bowling at speeds of around 145 km/h, with a recorded maximum of 149 km/h.<ref>{{Cite web |last=G |first=Sandip |date=30 January 2022 |title=Long Read: Avesh Khan and the maza of bowling fast |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/avesh-khan-and-the-maza-of-bowling-fast-7747021/lite/ |access-date=9 September 2022 |website=[[The Indian Express]] |quote=He consistently clocked 145kph, the fastest was measured at 149, matching his colleagues Rabada and Nortje for pace.}}</ref> He plays for [[Madhya Pradesh cricket team|Madhya Pradesh]] in domestic cricket and [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL 2024 {{!}} Rajasthan Royals {{!}} Avesh Khan Player Profile |url=https://www.iplt20.com/teams/rajasthan-royals/squad-details/1561 |access-date=2024-09-07 |website=www.iplt20.com |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2019, he was named in the India Blue team's squad for the [[2019–20 Duleep Trophy]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27331972/shubman-gill-priyank-panchal-faiz-fazal-lead-duleep-trophy-sides |title=Shubman Gill, Priyank Panchal and Faiz Fazal to lead Duleep Trophy sides |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=6 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cricketcountry.com/news/duleep-trophy-2019-shubman-gill-faiz-fazal-and-priyank-panchal-to-lead-duleep-trophy-2019-squad-fixtures-schedule-876560 |title=Duleep Trophy 2019: Shubman Gill, Faiz Fazal and Priyank Panchal to lead as Indian domestic cricket season opens |work=Cricket Country |access-date=6 August 2019}}</ref> In the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]], he was bought by the [[Delhi Capitals]] ahead of the [[2020 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28338426/ipl-auction-analysis-do-eight-teams-their-best-xis-place? |title=IPL auction analysis: Do the eight teams have their best XIs in place? |date=20 December 2019 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=20 December 2019}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He became the first Impact Player in the IPL history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-31 |title=The first Impact Players of IPL 2023: Gujarat's Sai Sudharsan sparkled, CSK's Tushar Deshpande couldn't impress |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/ipl/ipl-2023-tushar-deshpande-becomes-first-impact-substitute-in-history-of-league-8531206/ |access-date=2023-06-25 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> In July 2024, he was included in India's squad for T20 series against Zimbabwe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sudharsan, Jitesh and Rana added to India's squad for first two T20Is against Zimbabwe |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/zim-vs-ind-sai-sudharsan-jitesh-sharma-and-harshit-rana-added-to-india-squad-for-first-two-t20is-1441914 |access-date=2024-07-03 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>
