'''Kamlesh Lachham Nagarkoti''' (born 28 December 1999) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1070188.html |title=Kamlesh Nagarkoti |access-date=26 February 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29834871/ipl-2020-kamlesh-nagarkoti,-shahbaz-ahmed,-ravi-bishnoi-head-line-uncapped-indian-bowlers |title=IPL 2020 - Kamlesh Nagarkoti, Shahbaz Ahmed, Ravi Bishnoi head line-up of exciting uncapped Indian bowlers |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=10 September 2020}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Rajasthan cricket team|Rajasthan]] in the [[2016–17 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 26 February 2017.<ref name="LA">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1053745.html |title=Vijay Hazare Trophy, Group C: Mumbai v Rajasthan at Chennai, Feb 26, 2017 |access-date=26 February 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Two days later, he took the first-ever [[Hat-trick (cricket)|hat-trick]] for Rajasthan in List A cricket, in the Vijay Hazare Trophy match against [[Gujarat cricket team|Gujarat]].<ref name="hat">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/vijay-hazare-trophy-2016-17/content/story/1084680.html |title=Nagarkoti's hat-trick fires Rajasthan to narrow win |access-date=28 February 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Nagarkoti's father was a [[subedar]] in the [[Indian Army]]. He utilized his retirement corpus to buy a one-bedroom apartment in Jaipur so his son could learn to play cricket. Nagarkoti's childhood coach was Surendra Singh Rathod.<ref>{{cite web|title='I sat inside the washroom when my bidding was on'|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22238946/i-sat-washroom-my-bidding-was-kamlesh-nagarkoti|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref>

In December 2017, he was named in India's squad for the [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="IndiaU19">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21650381/prithvi-shaw-lead-india-19-world-cup |title=Prithvi Shaw to lead India in Under-19 World Cup |access-date=3 December 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In January 2018, he was bought by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[List of 2018 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2018 IPL auction]] for ₹3.2 crores.<ref name="IPL2018">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22218394/ipl-2018-player-auction-list-sold-unsold-players |title=List of sold and unsold players |access-date=27 January 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref name="IPLICC">{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/604757 |title=U19 World Cup stars snapped up in IPL auction |access-date=28 January 2018 |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref> However, he did not play a match due to injury concerns. Despite that, he was retained for the next season. Just ahead of the [[2019 Indian Premier League]] he was again ruled out of the tournament due to back injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/ipl-2019-kolkata-knight-riders-kamlesh-nagarkoti-ruled-out-shivam-mavi-sandeep-warrier/article26534120.ece|title=Injured Kamlesh Nagarkoti to miss IPL again|first=Team|last=Sportstar|website=Sportstar|access-date=21 March 2019}}</ref>

In November 2019, he was named in India's squad for the [[2019 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]] in Bangladesh.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/kamlesh-nagarkoti-returns-to-indian-team-for-emerging-asia-cup/articleshow/71378153.cms|title=India Under-23s Squad|work=Time of India|access-date=1 October 2019}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[2020 Indian Premier League]] on 26 September 2020.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1216545.html |title=8th Match (N), Abu Dhabi, Sep 26 2020, Indian Premier League |access-date=26 September 2020 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

On 26 October 2020, Nagarkoti was named as one of four additional bowlers to travel with the [[India national cricket team|India cricket team]] for their [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2020–21|tour to Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcci.tv/articles/2020/news/147414/team-india-s-t20i-odi-and-test-squads-for-tour-of-australia-announced |title=Team India's T20I, ODI and Test squads for Tour of Australia announced |work=Board of Control for Cricket in India |access-date=26 October 2020}}</ref> However, on 9 November 2020, Nagarkoti, was ruled out of the tour due to the management of his workload.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcci.tv/articles/2020/news/147420/updates-india-s-tour-of-australia |title=Updates- India's Tour of Australia |work=Board of Control for Cricket in India |access-date=9 November 2020}}</ref>

In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 24 February 2022, for Rajasthan in the [[2021–22 Ranji Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280436.html |title=Elite, Group E, Thiruvananthapuram, Feb 24 - 27 2022, Ranji Trophy |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=24 February 2022}}</ref>

'''Anuj Rawat''' (born 17 October 1999) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who represents [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in domestic cricket and [[Gujarat Titans]] in [[Indian Premier League]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1123073.html |title=Anuj Rawat |access-date=6 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He is a left-handed [[Batting order (cricket)#Top order|top order batsman]] and [[wicket-keeper]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/rajasthan-royals-wicketkeeper-anuj-rawat-recalls-gautam-gambhirs-advice-from-the-slip-cordon/articleshow/77458286.cms|title=Rajasthan Royals' wicketkeeper Anuj Rawat recalls Gautam Gambhir's advice from the slip cordon|first=Amit|last=Kumar|date= 10 August 2020|access-date=26 April 2021|work=[[Times of India]]|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210428220812/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/rajasthan-royals-wicketkeeper-anuj-rawat-recalls-gautam-gambhirs-advice-from-the-slip-cordon/articleshow/77458286.cms |archive-date=28 April 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-the-uncapped-ones-shahrukh-khan-umran-malik-and-more-1307144 |title=The uncapped ones: Shahrukh Khan, Umran Malik and more |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=25 March 2022}}</ref>

He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]] on 6 October 2017.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1118612.html |title=Group A, Ranji Trophy at Delhi, Oct 6-9 2017 |access-date=6 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Delhi in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 21 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157091.html |title=Group A, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Krishna, Feb 21 2019 |access-date=21 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 4 October 2019, for Delhi in the [[2019–20 Vijay Hazare Trophy]].<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1200751.html |title=Elite, Group B, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Vadodara, Oct 4 2019 |access-date=4 October 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]], he was bought by the [[Rajasthan Royals]] ahead of the [[2020 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28338426/ipl-auction-analysis-do-eight-teams-their-best-xis-place? |title=IPL auction analysis: Do the eight teams have their best XIs in place? |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 December 2019}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] in the [[2022 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Who is Anuj Rawat? All you need to know about uncapped wicketkeeper picked by RCB for Rs 3.40 cr|url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/sports/cricket/who-is-anuj-rawat-all-you-need-to-know-about-uncapped-wicketkeeper-picked-by-rcb-for-rs-340-cr|access-date=13 February 2022|website=Free Press Journal|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

'''Ajinkya Madhukar Rahane''' (born 6 June 1988) is a former Indian professional [[cricket]]er and also captained the [[India national cricket team]] in all three formats. He formerly played for and captained [[Mumbai cricket team|Mumbai in domestic cricket]]. He played primarily as a middle-order batsman in the [[Test cricket|Test format]] and as a top-order batsman in white-ball forms of the game. India lost only one match under his captaincy.

Rahane made his first-class debut in [[2007–08 Ranji Trophy]] season for Mumbai. He made his international debut in a [[Twenty20 International]] against [[England cricket team|England]] at [[Manchester]] in August 2011<ref name="espncricinfo.com">[http://www.espncricinfo.com/sri-lanka-v-india-2012/content/player/277916.html Ajinkya Rahane | India Cricket | Cricket Players and Officials]. ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved on 2013-12-23.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cricket.yahoo.com/news/professional-companies-should-manage-cricketers-041823900.html|title=Professional companies should manage cricketers|date=9 June 2013|work=Yahoo Cricket India}}</ref> and his Test debut in March 2013 against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]]. His first Test [[Century (cricket)|century]] came at the [[Basin Reserve]], [[Wellington]] against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/ajinkya-rahane-277916|title=Ajinkya Rahane profile and biography, stats, records, averages, photos and videos|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Under his captaincy, India won the [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2020–21|2020-21 Border–Gavaskar Trophy]] in Australia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/england-in-india/ajinkya-rahanes-captaincy-masterclass-puts-the-heat-on-virat-kohli-as-england-loom/articleshow/80362534.cms|title=Ajinkya Rahane's captaincy masterclass puts the heat on Virat Kohli as England loom. Cricket News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=20 January 2021 }}</ref>

On 30 July 2026, Rahane announced his retirement from all forms of professional cricket.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=30 July 2026 |title=India great calls time on glittering cricket career |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/india-great-calls-time-on-glittering-cricket-career |website=[[International Cricket Council]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |access-date=30 July 2026 |title=Rahane announces retirement from international cricket and all formats |url=https://www.cricinfo.com/story/ajinkya-rahane-announces-retirement-from-international-cricket-1548072 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref>

'''Mandeep Singh''' (born 18 December 1991) is an Indian cricketer.<ref name=ci/> He plays for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] in the top-flight of Indian cricket.<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/538684.html Punjab Squad, Ranji Trophy 2011/12]</ref> Ahead of India's 2024-25 domestic season, he moved to [[Tripura cricket team|Tripura]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mandeep Singh leaves home to find all-format comfort |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/indian-domestic-season-2024-25-mandeep-singh-leaves-punjab-tripura-find-all-format-comfort-1447022 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> A right-hand batsman who occasionally bowls [[fast bowling|right arm medium pace]], Mandeep has also played for India Blue,<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/534335.html India Blue Squad, Challenger Trophy 2011/12]</ref> and [[North Zone cricket team|North Zone]]<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/550513.html North Zone Squad, Duleep Trophy 2011/12]</ref> and for teams in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2011/content/squad/495843.html Kings XI Punjab]</ref> He was the vice-captain of the [[India under-19 cricket team]] for the [[2010 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2010 Under-19 World Cup]].

On 18 July 2012, he was among the 30 probables named for the World T20 tournament to be played in Sri Lanka in September 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wisdenindia.com/yuvraj-included-in-world-t20-probables |title=Yuvraj included in World T20 probables |publisher=Wisden India |date=18 July 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120826015206/http://www.wisdenindia.com/yuvraj-included-in-world-t20-probables |archive-date=26 August 2012 }}</ref> However, he was not selected in the final 15-member squad.

He made his [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) debut [[Indian cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2016|against Zimbabwe]] at [[Harare Sports Club]] on 18 June 2016.<ref name="T20I">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1007655.html |title=India tour of Zimbabwe, 1st T20I: Zimbabwe v India at Harare, Jun 18, 2016 |access-date=18 June 2016 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

'''Shahbaz Nadeem''' (born 12 August 1989)<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/surprise-package/article3376585.ece|title=Surprise package|author=Y. B. SARANGI|newspaper=The Hindu|date=2 May 2012}}</ref> is an Indian former international cricketer who played as a slow left-arm orthodox bowler. He made his [[first-class cricket]] debut in December 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27895367/if-slot-xi-empty-just-wait-your-chance-shahbaz-nadeem |title=If a slot in the XI isn't empty, then you just wait for your chance – Shahbaz Nadeem |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=21 October 2019|date=21 October 2019 }}</ref> He played for [[Bihar]] U-14, [[Indian U-19 cricket team|Indian U-19s]] and [[Jharkhand cricket team|Jharkhand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iplt20.com/teams/delhi-daredevils/squad/57/shahbaz-nadeem|title=Shahbaz Nadeem – Delhi Daredevils player – IPLT20.com|work=IPLT20|access-date=12 April 2013|archive-date=13 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513154052/https://www.iplt20.com/teams/delhi-daredevils/squad/57/shahbaz-nadeem|url-status=dead}}</ref> In March 2024, he announced his retirement from Indian international cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/shahbaz-nadeem-announces-retirement-from-all-forms-of-cricket-in-india-will-try-his-luck-in-t20-leagues-around-world-101709721081704-amp.html |title=Shahbaz Nadeem announces retirement from all forms of cricket in India, will try his luck in T20 leagues around world |work=Hindustan Times |accessdate=7 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/satisfied-shahbaz-nadeem-retires-from-all-cricket-in-india-1423667 |title='Satisfied' Shahbaz Nadeem retires from all cricket in India |work=ESPNcricinfo |accessdate=7 March 2024}}</ref>

'''Ramsingh Sanjay Yadav''' (born 10 May 1995) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Tamil Nadu cricket team|Tamil Nadu]] in domestic cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-the-uncapped-ones-shahrukh-khan-umran-malik-and-more-1307144 |title=The uncapped ones: Shahrukh Khan, Umran Malik and more |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=25 March 2022}}</ref> He is a batting [[all-rounder]] who bats left-handed and bowls [[slow left-arm orthodox]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sanjay Yadav, a daily wager's son, living his IPL dream with Kolkata Knight Riders|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/ipl-2017/sanjay-yadav-a-daily-wager-s-son-living-his-ipl-dream-with-kolkata-knight-riders/story-i79YyvMxkpWSh5BWP7vfyH.html|work=Hindustan Times|access-date=7 April 2017}}</ref>

He moved to [[Meghalaya cricket team]] ahead of the 2019–2020 season as a professional. He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 24 September 2019, for Meghalaya in the [[2019–20 Vijay Hazare Trophy]].<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1200644.html |title=Plate Group, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Dehra Dun, Sep 24 2019 |access-date=24 September 2019 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 9 December 2019, for Meghalaya in the [[2019–20 Ranji Trophy]].<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1203462.html |title=Plate Group, Ranji Trophy at Sovima, Dec 9-12 2019 |access-date=9 December 2019 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In the first innings of the match, he took nine wickets for 52 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/domestic/ranji-trophy/ranji-trophy-2019-20-sanjay-yadav-nine-wickets-meghalaya-nagaland-record-tamil-nadu-kkr-ipl-2020-vb-kanchi-veerans-tnpl/article30265440.ece |title=Ranji Trophy 2019-20: Meghalaya all-rounder Sanjay Yadav scalps nine wickets against Nagaland |work=Sport Star |access-date=10 December 2019}}</ref> They were the third-best figures in Indian domestic first-class cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latestly.com/sports/cricket/sanjay-yadav-records-third-best-bowling-figures-in-indian-first-class-cricket-history-meghalaya-all-rounder-takes-952-in-2019-20-ranji-trophy-match-against-nagaland-1394094.html |title=Sanjay Yadav Records Third-Best Bowling Figures in Indian First-Class Cricket History; Meghalaya All-Rounder Takes 9/52 in 2019–20 Ranji Trophy Match Against Nagaland |work=Latestly |access-date=10 December 2019}}</ref>

In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

In TNPL 2022 edition Sanjay Yadav scored his maiden hundred against Ruby Trichy Warriors 103(55)* in T20 format.

'''Anukul Sudhakar Roy''' ({{langx|mai|अनुकूल सुधाकर रॉय}}; born 30 November 1998) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Jharkhand cricket team|Jharkhand]] and [[Kolkata Knight Riders]]. In December 2017, he was named in India's squad for the [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="IndiaU19">{{cite web |title=Prithvi Shaw to lead India in Under-19 World Cup |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/prithvi-shaw-to-lead-india-in-under-19-world-cup-1128314 |access-date=3 December 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He was the joint highest wicket taker in the Under-19 Cricket World Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=11980&type=tournament|title=ICC Under-19 World Cup, 2017/18 Cricket Team Records & Stats - ESPNcricinfo|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=26 April 2019}}</ref>

He was born into a [[Maithil]] family in [[Seraikela Kharsawan district|Seraikela Kharsawan]] in the state of [[Jharkhand]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anukul Roy Profile|url=https://www.mumbaiindians.com/players/66983-anukul-roy-profile|website=Mumbai Indians|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Anukul Roy Profile - Cricket Player India {{!}} Stats, Records, Video|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/anukul-roy-1079839|website=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=2025-12-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815103243/https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/anukul-roy-1079839|archive-date=2025-08-15|language=en}}</ref> His family hails from Rosera, [[Samastipur district|Samastipur]] district in the [[Mithila (region)|Mithila region]] of Bihar.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/state-to-felicitate-samastipurs-anukul/articleshow/62773035.cms |title=Under-19 World Cup: Bihar govt to felicitate Samastipur's Anukul Roy
|website=The Times of India |access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Jharkhand cricket team|Jharkhand]] in the [[2017–18 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 8 February 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1118740.html |title=Group D, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Secunderabad, Feb 8 2018 |access-date=8 February 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Jharkhand in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 1 November 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156949.html |title=Elite, Group C, Ranji Trophy at Ranchi, Nov 1-4 2018 |access-date=1 November 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He was the leading wicket-taker for Jharkhand in the tournament, with 30 dismissals in nine matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12592;team=6558;type=tournament |title=Ranji Trophy, 2018/19 - Jharkhand: Batting and bowling averages |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=10 January 2019}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Jharkhand in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 21 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157091.html |title=Group A, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Krishna, Feb 21 2019 |access-date=21 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In October 2019, he was named in [[India B cricket team|India B]]'s squad for the [[2019–20 Deodhar Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/deodhar-trophy-2019-squads-india-a-india-b-india-c-parthiv-patel-shubman-gill-anuma-vihari-ranchi/article29788595.ece |title=Deodhar Trophy 2019: Hanuma Vihari, Parthiv, Shubman to lead; Yashasvi earns call-up |work=SportStar |access-date=25 October 2019}}</ref>

In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He made his debut for his new side against [[Rajasthan Royals|RR]] on 2 May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sportstar |first=Team |title=KKR vs RR Live Score, IPL 2022 updates: Umesh gets Padikkal early after Kolkata elects to bowl |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/kkr-vs-rr-live-score-rajasthan-royals-vs-kolkata-knight-riders-ipl-2022-today-match/article38483735.ece |access-date=2022-05-02 |website=Sportstar |language=en}}</ref> He won the [[2024 Indian Premier League]] title with them.

'''Darshan Nalkande''' (born 4 October 1998) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1111917.html |title=Darshan Nalkande |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]] in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 2 October 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156889.html |title=Elite, Group A, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Bengaluru, Oct 2 2018 |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Vidarbha in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 1 November 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156938.html |title=Elite, Group A, Ranji Trophy at Pune, Nov 1-4 2018 |access-date=1 November 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref name="IPL 2019: Darshan Nalkande, an all-rounder with promise">{{cite news |title=IPL 2019: Darshan Nalkande, an all-rounder with promise |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-2019-darshan-nalkande-an-all-rounder-with-promise/articleshow/68552626.cms |access-date=24 March 2025 |publisher=The Times of India |date=24 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250324104807/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-2019-darshan-nalkande-an-all-rounder-with-promise/articleshow/68552626.cms |archive-date=24 March 2025}}</ref>

In December 2018, he was bought by the [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[List of 2019 Indian Premier League personnel changes|player auction]] for the [[2019 Indian Premier League]] (IPL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/25390461/ipl-2019-auction-was-sold-whom |title=IPL 2019 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-auction-2019-who-got-whom/articleshow/67144375.cms |title=IPL 2019 Auction: Who got whom |work=The Times of India |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Vidarbha in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 21 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157096.html |title=Group B, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Surat, Feb 21 2019 |access-date=21 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> In April 2022, he made his IPL debut against [[Punjab Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/ipl-2022-who-are-sai-sudharsan-darshan-nalkande-all-you-need-to-know-about-gts-two-debutants-vs-pbks-article-90731373|title=IPL 2022: Who are Sai Sudharsan & Darshan Nalkande? All you need to know about GT's two debutants vs PBKS|work=Times Now|access-date=8 April 2022}}</ref>

Darshan Nalkande took four wickets in four balls in the final over of Karnataka's innings in [[2021–22 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] national T20 tournament 20 November 2021.<ref name="Syed Mushtaq Ali T20: 4 wickets in 4 balls for Nalkande, Karnataka beat Vidarbha to storm into final">{{cite news |title=Syed Mushtaq Ali T20: 4 wickets in 4 balls for Nalkande, Karnataka beat Vidarbha to storm into final |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/syed-mushtaq-ali-t20-four-wickets-four-balls-darshan-nalkande-karnataka-vidarbha-watch-7632883/ |access-date=24 March 2025 |publisher=The Indian Express |date=20 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250324105115/https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/syed-mushtaq-ali-t20-four-wickets-four-balls-darshan-nalkande-karnataka-vidarbha-watch-7632883/ |archive-date=24 March 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Lalit Yadav''' (born 3 January 1997) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/930189.html |title=Lalit Yadav |access-date=3 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]] on 17 November 2017.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1118675.html |title=Group A, Ranji Trophy at Delhi, Nov 17-20 2017 |access-date=17 November 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Delhi in the [[2017–18 Zonal T20 League]] on 9 January 2018.<ref name="T20">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1130675.html |title=North Zone, Inter State Twenty-20 Tournament at Delhi, Jan 9 2018 |access-date=9 January 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Delhi in the [[2017–18 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 15 February 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1118769.html |title=Group B, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Nadaun, Feb 15 2018 |access-date=3 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

'''Rajvardhan Hangargekar''' (born 10 November 2002) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1175429.html |title=Rajvardhan Hangargekar |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-the-uncapped-ones-shahrukh-khan-umran-malik-and-more-1307144 |title=The uncapped ones: Shahrukh Khan, Umran Malik and more |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=25 March 2022}}</ref> He plays for [[Maharashtra cricket team|Maharashtra]] in domestic cricket and [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].

He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 16 January 2021, for [[Maharashtra cricket team|Maharashtra]] in the [[2020–21 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]].<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1244370.html |title=Elite, Group C, Vadodara, Jan 16 2021, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 21 February 2021, for Maharashtra in the [[2020–21 Vijay Hazare Trophy]].<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1250902.html |title=Elite, Group D, Jaipur, Feb 21 2021, Vijay Hazare Trophy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=21 February 2021}}</ref> In December 2021, he was named in India's team for the [[2022 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup]] in the West Indies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcci.tv/articles/2021/news/158851/four-time-winners-india-announce-icc-u19-cricket-world-cup-2022-squad |title=Four-time winners India announce ICC U19 Cricket World Cup 2022 squad |work=Board of Control for Cricket in India |access-date=19 December 2021}}</ref>

In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |access-date=13 February 2022 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Quint |first=The |date=2022-02-13 |title=IPL 2022 Auction: CSK Bag U-19 WC Star Rajvardhan Hangargekar |url=https://www.thequint.com/indian-premier-league-ipl/ipl-2022-auction-rajvardhan-hangargekar-joins-chennai-super-kings-for-rs-15-crore |access-date=2022-03-25 |website=TheQuint |language=en}}</ref>

On 31 March 2023, he made his IPL debut for Chennai Super Kings in the [[2023 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=1st Match (N), Ahmedabad, March 31, 2023, Indian Premier League |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1359475.html |access-date=31 March 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

On 19 July 2023, in the [[2023 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]] match against [[Pakistan A cricket team]] Hangargekar picked up 5 wickets conceding only 42 runs guiding [[India A cricket team]] to a resounding victory.

'''Jason Paul Behrendorff''' (born 20 April 1990) is an Australian [[cricket]]er who played [[One Day International]]s and [[Twenty20 International]]s for [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] and first-class and List A cricket for [[Western Australia cricket team|Western Australia]], but has now retired from those formats of cricket. He currently plays [[Twenty20]] cricket in the [[Big Bash League]] for the [[Melbourne Renegades]].

Although born in [[New South Wales]], Behrendorff grew up in [[Canberra]] and played representative cricket for the [[ACT Comets|Australian Capital Territory]] at both junior and senior levels. A left-arm [[Fast bowling|fast bowler]], he transferred to [[Western Australia cricket team|Western Australia]] for the [[2009–10 Australian cricket season|2009–10 season]] and made his debut at state level the following season, playing several matches after injuries to other fast bowlers. Behrendorff has since become a regular for [[Western Australia cricket team|Western Australia]], opening the bowling in both the [[Sheffield Shield]] and the one-day [[Australian domestic limited-overs cricket tournament|Matador BBQs One-Day Cup]]. He made his debut for the [[Perth Scorchers]] during the [[2012–13 Big Bash League season|2012–13 season]] of the [[Big Bash League|BBL]], and featured in the Scorchers teams that won consecutive titles during the [[2013–14 Big Bash League season|2013–14]] and [[2014–15 Big Bash League season|2014–15 seasons]]. He later featured in the Scorchers' 2021–22 and 2022-23 championship triumphs. Behrendorff announced his retirement from first-class and List A cricket at the end of the 2024-25 Australian cricket season,<ref name="ESPNCricinfo">{{cite web|title=Behrendorff ends 16-year WA career with state retirement|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/jason-behrendorff-ends-16-year-wa-career-with-state-retirement-1474903|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]|date=26 February 2025}}</ref> but his intention to continue playing in the Big Bash League, leaving the Scorchers after 13 years for a 3-year contract with the [[Melbourne Renegades]],<ref name="Cricket.com.au">{{cite web|title=Renegades land Behrendorff in first major BBL free agency move|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/4205136/jason-behrendorff-bbl-melbourne-renegades-three-year-deal-player-movement-window-2025-signings-perth-scorchers|publisher=[[Cricket.com.au]]|date=28 January 2025}}</ref> citing his long-term ambition to move to Melbourne after his cricket career.<ref name="Jason Behrendorff">{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DFWbiyuzVOB|title=As you may have already seen, it is with a heavy heart that I am officially announcing that I won't be a part of the @scorchersbbl next season|publisher=Jason Behrendorff|via=[[Instagram]]|date=28 January 2025}}</ref>

'''Mitchell Josef Santner''' (born 5 February 1992) is a New Zealand international [[cricket]]er and current captain of [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand Cricket team]] in limited overs cricket. Domestically, he plays for [[Northern Districts men's cricket team|Northern Districts cricket team]]. He is a bowling all-rounder who bats left-handed, and bowls slow left-arm orthodox spin. He has been involved in the [[List of New Zealand Test cricket records#Highest wicket partnerships|highest 7th wicket partnership for New Zealand in Tests]]. Occasionally he plays golf as well.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/360680435/black-caps-captain-mitchell-santner-best-golfer-other-sports |title=Black Caps captain Mitchell Santner the best golfer from other sports |work=Stuff |access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref> He was a part of the New Zealand squad to finish as [[2019 Cricket World Cup final|runners-up]] at the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]]. He captained the New Zealand team in the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]], where they ended up as runners-up.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-18 |title=Mitchell Santner: New Zealand pick spinner as white-ball captain |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/c77j6ggk4p2o |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Um-E-Aymen |first=Babar |date=9 March 2025 |title=Champions Trophy 2025: India beat New Zealand by four wickets in tense final in Dubai |url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12123/13324931/champions-trophy-2025-india-beat-new-zealand-by-four-wickets-in-tense-final-in-dubai |work=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref>

Santner was elevated towards the [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] team after a promising 2014–15 domestic season. He was named in the one-day squad for the tour of England following the retirement of [[Daniel Vettori]] after the [[2015 Cricket World Cup|2015 World Cup]] as New Zealand searched for another left-arm spin option. Santner was then drafted into the touring squad at the start of the [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2015|England tour]] to cover for the absence of the players at the [[Indian Premier League]] and made an immediate impression with a well-crafted 94 against [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]]. He was handed his [[One Day International]] debut at [[Edgbaston Cricket Ground|Edgbaston]] having played just 19 [[List A cricket|List A]] matches for Northern Districts.

In November 2020, Santner [[List of New Zealand national cricket captains#Twenty20 International captains|captained New Zealand]] for the first time in an international fixture, leading the team in the third [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) match [[West Indian cricket team in New Zealand in 2020–21|against the West Indies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1918904 |title=No Southee, Taylor, Jamieson as New Zealand aim for clean sweep |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=30 November 2020}}</ref> He did so again in the first T20I match against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Debutant Jacob Duffy and Tim Seifert the difference as New Zealand guts it past Pakistan|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-v-pakistan-2020-21-1233950/new-zealand-vs-pakistan-1st-t20i-1233959/match-report|access-date=2020-12-19|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

In December 2024, he was named New Zealand's permanent white-ball captain.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Voerman |first1=Andrew |title=Black Caps name Mitchell Santner as new white-ball captain ahead of Champions Trophy |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/360526898/black-caps-name-mitchell-santner-new-white-ball-captain-ahead-champions-trophy |website=Stuff |access-date=17 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Praveen Dubey''' (born 1 July 1993) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Karnataka cricket team|Karnataka]] in domestic cricket. He is a right-handed batsman and [[leg break]] [[googly]] bowler. He was signed up by [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] at the 2016 IPL players auction for {{INR}} 35 lakh.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of players sold and unsold at IPL auction 2016|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2016/content/story/969473.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=5 March 2016}}</ref> In February 2017, he was bought by the [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] team for the [[2017 Indian Premier League]] for {{INR}} 10 [[lakh]].<ref name="IPL">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2017/content/story/1083407.html |title=List of players sold and unsold at IPL auction 2017 |accessdate=20 February 2017 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In 2020, the [[Delhi Capitals]] named him as a replacement for their injured player [[Amit Mishra]].<ref>{{Cite web|author=<!--staff writer-->|date=2020-10-19|title=IPL 2020: Delhi Capitals Announce Pravin Dubey as Replacement For Amit Mishra|url=https://www.india.com/sports/cricket-ipl-2020-delhi-capitals-announce-pravin-dubey-as-replacement-for-amit-mishra-4178209/|access-date=2020-10-31|website=India.com|language=en}}</ref>

He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Karnataka in the [[2017–18 Zonal T20 League]] on 8 January 2018.<ref name="T20">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1130665.html |title=South Zone, Inter State Twenty-20 Tournament at Visakhapatnam, Jan 8 2018 |accessdate=8 January 2018 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 11 January 2020, for Karnataka in the [[2019–20 Ranji Trophy]].<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1203522.html |title=Elite, Group B, Ranji Trophy at Rajkot, Jan 11-14 2020 |accessdate=11 January 2020 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> named 27-year-old uncapped leg-spinner Pravin Dube as a replacement for Amit Mishra who was ruled out of IPL 2020 with a finger injury.<ref>{{Cite magazine|author=Akshay Ramesh |date=19 October 2020 |title=IPL 2020: Delhi Capitals find replacement for injured Amit Mishra in leg-spinner Pravin Dube|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/ipl-2020/story/pravin-dube-delhi-capitals-replacement-injured-amit-mishra-karnataka-leg-spinner-1733033-2020-10-19|access-date=2021-08-27|magazine=India Today|language=en}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

'''Subhranshu Senapati''' (born 30 December 1996) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1059577.html |title=Subhranshu Senapati |access-date=6 October 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Odisha cricket team|Odisha]] in the [[2016–17 Ranji Trophy]] on 6 October 2016.<ref name="FC">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1053467.html |title=Ranji Trophy, Group B: Odisha v Vidarbha at Visakhapatnam, Oct 6-9, 2016 |access-date=6 October 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Odisha in the [[2016–17 Inter State Twenty-20 Tournament]] on 3 February 2017.<ref name="T20">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1079324.html |title=Inter State Twenty-20 Tournament, East Zone: Bengal v Odisha at Kolkata, Feb 3, 2017 |access-date=3 February 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Odisha in the [[2016–17 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 25 February 2017.<ref name="LA">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1053711.html |title=Vijay Hazare Trophy, Group A: Haryana v Odisha at Delhi, Feb 25, 2017 |access-date=25 February 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

He was the leading run-scorer for Odisha in the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]], with 427 runs in six matches.<ref name="Ranji1718">{{cite news |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12014;team=2039;type=tournament |title=Ranji Trophy, 2017/18: Odisha batting and bowling averages |publisher=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=3 April 2018}}</ref> He was also the leading run-scorer for Odisha in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]], with 617 runs in nine matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12592;team=2039;type=tournament |title=Ranji Trophy, 2018/19 - Odisha: Batting and bowling averages |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=10 January 2019}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He was retained by [[Chennai Super Kings]] for 2023 [[Indian Premier League]].

'''Timothy Hays David''' (born 16 March 1996) is a Singaporean-born Australian [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[Australian national cricket team]] in [[Twenty20 International]]. He also plays in various franchise leagues, including the [[Big Bash League]], for the [[Hobart Hurricanes]], and the [[Indian Premier League]], for [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] (RCB).

A right-handed batsman who can bowl [[off spin]], David was born in [[Singapore]] before moving to [[Perth]] when he was two. He played for the [[Singapore national cricket team]] in 2019–2020, making his international debut against Qatar during the [[2018–19 T20 World Cup Asia Qualifier]]. He switched allegiance to Australia from 2022 onwards, playing his first match [[Australian cricket team in India in 2022–23|against India that same year]].

David is known for his "explosive" shot-making and the ability generate power into any ball,<ref name="ESPN2022">{{cite web |last=Lavalette |first=Tristan |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-tim-david-singapores-most-famous-cricketer-might-be-the-ipls-and-australias-next-star-1306222 |title=Tim David, Singapore's most famous cricketer, might be the IPL's (and Australia's) next star |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=24 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Savage |first=Nic |date=3 October 2022 |title='This is wild': Tim David's explosive cameo creates T20 World Cup selection headache |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/this-is-wild-tim-davids-explosive-cameo-creates-t20-world-cup-selection-headache/news-story/cd421899ab5c31a494884fc6f6c74467 |work=news.com.au|access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Heverin |first=Dane |date=6 November 2025 |title='If they want to come knocking...': Aussie T20 gun's impressive comparison with MLB superstar |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/if-any-teams-want-to-come-knocking-aussie-t20-guns-stunning-comparison-with-baseball-superstar/news-story/9ba004a6d981886752bfe40c28e32607 |work=[[Fox Sports (Australia)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref> and was named  the [[Australian Cricket Awards#Men's Twenty20 International Player of the Year|Australian Men's Twenty20 International Player of the Year]] in 2026. He was part of the Australia's squads for the [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022]], [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] and [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup]].

'''Baba Indrajith''' (born 8 July 1994)<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/india/content/player/477069.html Baba Indrajith – ESPNcricinfo profile]</ref> is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[Tamil Nadu cricket team]]. Indrajith is a right hand batsman and legbreak bowler and an occasional wicket-keeper. He plays first-class cricket for [[Tamil Nadu cricket team|Tamil Nadu]].<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/ranji-trophy-2013-14/content/squad/679597.html Ranji Trophy 2013-14 / Tamil Nadu squad]</ref> In September 2017, he scored his first double-century in [[first-class cricket]], playing for India Red in the [[2017–18 Duleep Trophy]].<ref name="shaswat9407">{{cite news |title=Indrajith double-ton headlines batting-friendly day |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8630/report/1118609/day/2/ |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |date=14 September 2017 |access-date=14 September 2017}}</ref>

In July 2018, he was named in the squad for India Green for the [[2018–19 Duleep Trophy]].<ref name="Duleep18">{{cite news |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/24173214/sanju-samson-picked-india-passing-yo-yo-test |title=Samson picked for India A after passing Yo-Yo test |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=23 July 2018 |access-date=23 July 2018}}</ref> In the opening fixture of the tournament, he made a century, scoring 109 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/24425902/rajneesh-gurbani-seven-ensures-three-points-india-red |title=Gurbani's seven-for ensures three points for India Red |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=20 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1153166.html |title=(D/N)Duleep Trophy at Dindigul, Aug 17-20 2018 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=20 August 2018}}</ref> He was the leading run-scorer for India Green in the tournament, with 149 runs in two matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12493;team=4184;type=tournament |title=Duleep Trophy, 2018/19 – India Green: Batting and bowling averages |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=7 September 2018}}</ref>

He was the leading run-scorer for Tamil Nadu in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]], with 641 runs in eight matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12592;team=2184;type=tournament |title=Ranji Trophy, 2018/19 – Tamil Nadu: Batting and bowling averages |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=10 January 2019}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament as a wicket-keeper batsman.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> Indrajith finished the [[2021-22 Ranji Trophy]] season as the leading run-scorer for Tamil Nadu, with 396 runs in three matches, at an average of 99, with three centuries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ranji-trophy-2021-22-sarfaraz-khan-century-puts-mumbai-in-quarter-finals-tamil-nadu-knocked-out-1303996|title=Sarfaraz's century puts Mumbai in quarter-finals; Tamil Nadu knocked out |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=6 March 2022}}</ref>

In December 2017, he scored his maiden double-century in first-class cricket, batting for Bengal against [[Gujarat cricket team|Gujarat]] in the quarter-finals of the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]].<ref name="Chatterjee200">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8050/report/1118697/day/4/ |title=Chatterjee, Easwaran keep Bengal on course for semi-finals |accessdate=10 December 2017 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Bengal in the [[2017–18 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 5 February 2018.<ref name="LA">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1118708.html |title=Group B, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Nadaun, Feb 5 2018 |accessdate=5 February 2018 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In July 2018, he was named in the squad for India Red for the [[2018–19 Duleep Trophy]].<ref name="Duleep18">{{cite news |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/24173214/sanju-samson-picked-india-passing-yo-yo-test |title=Samson picked for India A after passing Yo-Yo test |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=23 July 2018 |accessdate=23 July 2018}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

'''Rasikh Salam Dar''' (born 5 April 2000) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who previously played for [[Jammu and Kashmir cricket team|Jammu and Kashmir]] and now plays for [[Baroda]] in domestic cricket. He also plays for [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL).<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1161489.html |title=Rasikh Salam |access-date=3 October 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In December 2018, he was signed by the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[List of 2019 Indian Premier League personnel changes|player auction]] for the [[2019 Indian Premier League|2019 Indian Premier League Season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/25390461/ipl-2019-auction-was-sold-whom |title=IPL 2019 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-auction-2019-who-got-whom/articleshow/67144375.cms |title=IPL 2019 Auction: Who got whom |work=The Times of India |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref> He became the third cricketer from [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]] to play in the Indian Premier League.<ref name=times/> At 17 years and 353 days, he became the youngest player to make his debut for the Mumbai Indians.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-2019-rasikh-salam-surprise-from-mumbai-indians/articleshow/68556558.cms|title=IPL 2019: Rasikh Salam surprise from Mumbai Indians - Times of India|website=The Times of India|access-date=25 March 2019}}</ref> However, in June 2019, the [[Board of Control for Cricket in India]] (BCCI) banned him for two years following a "discrepancy" in his birth certificate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1189770.html |title=BCCI hands Rasikh Salam two-year ban for age fraud |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=19 June 2019}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Jammu & Kashmir in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 3 October 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156897.html |title=Elite, Group C, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Chennai, Oct 3 2018 |access-date=3 October 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Jammu & Kashmir in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 30 December 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157066.html |title=Elite, Group C, Ranji Trophy at Guwahati, Dec 30 2018 - Jan 2 2019 |access-date=30 December 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Jammu & Kashmir in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 22 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157109.html |title=Group A, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Krishna, Feb 22 2019 |access-date=22 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He was released by the Mumbai Indians ahead of the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28087425/where-do-eight-franchises-stand-2020-auction |title=Where do the eight franchises stand before the 2020 auction? |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 November 2019}}</ref> In February 2022, he was signed by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League|2022 Indian Premier League Season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He was acquired by Delhi Capitals in the [[List of 2024 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2024 Indian Premier League auction]] as a fast bowler. In the 2025 Indian Premier League auction, he was sold to Royal Challengers Bengaluru, winning his maiden IPL title that same season. The following season, he took 19 wickets, as RCB won back-to-back IPL titles.<ref name="IPL 2025 auction: Complete list of sold, unsold players, teamwise remaining purse {{!}} Mint">{{cite news|url=https://www.livemint.com/sports/cricket-news/ipl-auction-2025-sold-unsold-full-players-list-costliest-cricketer-remaining-purse-amount-teamwise-rishabh-pant-11732478575379.html|title=IPL 2025 auction: Complete list of sold, unsold players, teamwise remaining purse {{!}} Mint|date=25 November 2024|work=mint|access-date=15 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415102416/https://www.livemint.com/sports/cricket-news/ipl-auction-2025-sold-unsold-full-players-list-costliest-cricketer-remaining-purse-amount-teamwise-rishabh-pant-11732478575379.html|archive-date=15 April 2025|publisher=Mint|language=en}}</ref>

'''Alexander Daniel Hales''' (born 3 January 1989) is an English [[cricket]]er. He is a right-handed opening batter who represented the [[England cricket team]] across all formats and played domestically for [[Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club|Nottinghamshire]]. He made his [[One Day International]] debut [[Indian cricket team in England in 2014|against India]] in August 2014 and his [[Test cricket]] debut [[English cricket team in South Africa in 2015–16|against South Africa]] in December 2015. Hales is the first English batter to score a T20I century, and had the highest individual score of an English batter in the format with his 116 not out against Sri Lanka in the [[2014 ICC World Twenty20]]. He is also the first batter to be dismissed for 99 in an ODI and a [[T20I]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/35512567|title=England beat South Africa in Port Elizabeth for 2-0 ODI series lead|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Hales was a key member of the England team that won the [[2022 T20 World Cup]]. In August 2023 Hales announced his retirement from international cricket, focusing on domestic and franchise [[T20 cricket]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Alex Hales announces international retirement |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-alex-hales-international-retirement-1390832 |access-date=4 August 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

'''David Andrew Miller''' (born 10 June 1989) is a South African professional [[cricket]]er. He currently plays for South African national team in [[limited overs cricket]]. He is an aggressive left-handed middle order batsman and an occasional wicket-keeper. He holds the record for the second fastest T20I century among full member ICC teams against full member opposition, tied with [[Rohit Sharma]], achieving the milestone in 35 deliveries.

He plays domestic cricket for the [[Dolphins (South African cricket team)|Dolphins]] and for [[Multan Sultan]]s in Pakistan super League and for the [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. He also represents the [[South Africa national cricket team]] in both [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] cricket. In September 2018, Miller announced that he would no longer be available to play [[first-class cricket]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cricket.co.za/news/25974/Miller-unavailable-to-play-first-class-cricket |title=Miller unavailable to play first-class cricket |work=Cricket South African |access-date=11 September 2018 |archive-date=11 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911152135/http://cricket.co.za/news/25974/Miller-unavailable-to-play-first-class-cricket |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Samuel William Billings''' (born 15 June 1991) is an English professional [[cricket]]er.<ref name="tory27jan17" /> Billings is a right-handed [[Batsman (cricket)|batsman]] who fields as a [[wicket-keeper]]. He was born at [[Pembury]] in [[Kent]] and has played for [[Kent County Cricket Club]] teams since he was eight years old, making his senior debut for the First XI in 2011. In October 2017, he was appointed as the vice-captain of the team, before being appointed as captain in January 2018, replacing [[Sam Northeast]].<ref name=ko10oct17 /><ref name=bbc17jan18>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/42718988 Sam Billings: England limited-overs player replaces Sam Northeast as Kent captain], [[BBC Sport]], 17 January 2018. Retrieved 30 January 2018.</ref> He served as the club's captain until the end of the 2023 season when he resigned, although he retained the captaincy of the club's [[Twenty20 cricket]] team.<ref name=bbc12oct23>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/67092095 Kent: Daniel Bell-Drummond appointed as club captain to replace Sam Billings], [[BBC Sport]], 12 October 2023. Retrieved 12 October 2023.</ref>

Billings has appeared mainly in limited overs formats for the [[England cricket team]] and made his [[Test cricket]] debut in January 2022. He has played [[Twenty20]] franchise cricket in the [[Pakistan Super League]], [[Indian Premier League]], [[Bangladesh Premier League]] and in the [[Big Bash League]] in Australia and captained [[Oval Invincibles]] in all four seasons of [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]].

'''Timothy Grant Southee''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|ONZM|size=85%}} (born 11 December 1988) is a former New Zealand international [[cricketer]] who has captained [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand cricket team]] in all formats of the game. He is a right-arm [[fast bowling|medium-fast]] bowler and a hard-hitting lower order batsman. The third New Zealand bowler to take 300 [[Test cricket|Test]] wickets, he was one of the country's youngest cricketers, debuting at the age of 19 in February 2008. On his Test debut against [[England national cricket team|England]] he took 5 wickets and made 77 off 40 balls in the second innings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/newzealand/content/player/232364.html|title=Tim Southee|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=2019-05-29}}</ref> He plays for [[Northern Districts men's cricket team|Northern Districts]] in the [[New Zealand first-class cricket championship|Plunket Shield]], [[Ford Trophy]] and [[Super Smash (men's cricket)|Super Smash]] as well as [[Northland cricket team|Northland]] in the [[Hawke Cup]]. He was named as [[List of New Zealand national cricket captains#Twenty20 International captains|New Zealand's captain]] for the first T20I [[West Indian cricket team in New Zealand in 2017–18#T20I series|against West Indies]] in place of [[Kane Williamson]], who was rested for that game.<ref name="NZT20Icaptain">{{cite news |title=Kitchen called up for WI T20s, Guptill returns |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21852167/anaru-kitchen-called-wi-t20s-martin-guptill-returns |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |date=23 December 2017 |access-date=23 December 2017}}</ref> The Blackcaps won that match by 47 runs.<ref>{{cite news |title=1st T20I, West Indies tour of New Zealand at Nelson, Dec 29 2017 |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1115798.html |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |date=29 December 2017 |access-date=29 December 2017}}</ref> Southee was a member of the New Zealand team that won the [[2019–2021 World Test Championship|2019–2021 ICC World Test Championship]]. Southee's Test batting strike rate of 82.68 is the third highest among batsmen with a minimum of 2000 career runs.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://crex.live/player-profile/7Z/tim-southee | title=Tim Southee Profile, Batting and Bowling stats, Recent form - CREX | crex.live }}</ref> He was also a part of the New Zealand squads to finish as runners-up in two [[List of Cricket World Cup finals|Cricket World Cup finals]] in [[2015 Cricket World Cup|2015]] and [[2019 Cricket World Cup|2019]].

Southee is known for his ability to generate late outswing at a brisk pace, and later with off cutting slower balls almost like a faster off-spinner on a damp wicket and death bowling. He was the third-highest wicket-taker at the [[2011 ICC World Cup]] (18 wickets at 17.33). He also impressed at the [[2015 ICC World Cup]], taking 7 wickets in a [[Round-robin tournament|round robin league]] match against England. '''Pramod Bhanuka Bandara Rajapaksa''' (born 24 October 1991), popularly known as '''Bhanuka Rajapaksa''', is a professional Sri Lankan [[cricket]]er, who plays limited over internationals for the [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|national team]]. He is a left-handed [[batsman (cricket)|batsman]] who bowls right-arm medium.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sl-vs-ind-five-lesser-known-sri-lanka-players-who-can-make-a-difference-against-india-1270071 |title=Five lesser-known Sri Lanka players who can make a difference against India |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=18 July 2021}}</ref> He was born in [[Colombo]]. Despite a prolific domestic career, Rajapaksa only made his international debut when he was called up for the [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Pakistan in 2019–20|T20I series against Pakistan in 2019]], ten years after his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut.

In July 2021, he was given a [[Suspended sentence|suspended]] ban from all forms of cricket for one year by the [[Sri Lanka Cricket]] for breach of contract and for not gaining the required permission from SLC to give media interviews.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-05|title=Bhanuka Rajapaksa penalized for breach of contract|url=https://www.newsfirst.lk/2021/07/05/bhanuka-rajapaksa-penalized-for-breach-of-contract/|access-date=2021-07-05|website=Sri Lanka News - Newsfirst|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bhanuka Rajapaksa gets suspended one-year ban, fined for breaching player contract|url=http://www.adaderana.lk/sports/8724/bhanuka-rajapaksa-gets-suspended-one-year-ban-fine-for-breaching-player-contract|access-date=2021-07-05|website=www.adaderana.lk|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-05|title=Bhanuka Rajapaksa, guilty for breaching Players Contract, handed one-year ban by SLC|url=https://www.crictracker.com/bhanuka-rajapaksa-guilty-for-breaching-players-contract-handed-one-year-ban-by-slc/|access-date=2021-07-05|website=CricTracker|language=en}}</ref>

'''Evin Earl Lewis''' (born 27 December 1991) is a [[Trinidad and Tobago|Trinidad]]ian [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] as a left-handed [[opening batsman]] in limited-overs internationals. Lewis is the third batsman, after [[Brendon McCullum]] and [[Chris Gayle]], to score two Twenty20 International centuries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/evin-lewis-joins-elite-club-with-second-t20i-century-1110275|title=Evin Lewis joins elite club with second T20I century|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=21 July 2021}}</ref> Lewis also holds the records of the highest retired hurt score, of 176 not out, in international cricket along with the highest score, of 125 not out, by a West Indian in T20 internationals.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Lewis was a member of the West Indies team that won the [[2016 T20 World Cup]].

He won the 2019 [[Bangladesh Premier League]] title with the [[Comilla Victorians]], the 2021 [[Caribbean Premier League]] title with the [[St Kitts & Nevis Patriots|St Kitts & Nevis]] Patriots. Lewis has also featured for CPL team [[Trinidad and Tobago Red Steel]], BPL outfits [[Barisal Bulls]] and [[Dhaka Dynamites]] along with [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] sides [[Mumbai Indians]] and [[Rajasthan Royals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Evin Lewis |url=https://www.wisden.com/players/evin-lewis-59314 |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Atharva Taide''' (born 26 April 2000) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]] in domestic cricket and previously appeared for [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1125958.html |title=Atharva Taide |access-date=20 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]] in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 20 September 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156798.html |title=Elite, Group A, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Bengaluru, Sep 20 2018 |access-date=20 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In December 2018, he was named in India's team for the [[2018 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/1167689.html |title=India Under-23s Squad |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 December 2018}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Vidarbha in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 22 December 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157040.html |title=Elite, Group A, Ranji Trophy at Nagpur, Dec 22-25 2018 |access-date=22 December 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Vidarbha in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 21 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157096.html |title=Group B, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Surat, Feb 21 2019 |access-date=21 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

Opening for Vidarbha in the final of the Cooch Vihar Trophy, Atharva played an innings of 320 to win the match for Vidarbha, equaling Yuvraj Singh's record.<ref name="Atharva Taide first from Vidarbha to score triple century">{{cite news|title=Atharva Taide first from Vidarbha to score triple century|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/atharva-taide-first-from-vidarbha-to-score-triple-century/articleshow/62719476.cms|accessdate=16 April 2025|publisher=The Times of India|date=31 January 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416161853/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/atharva-taide-first-from-vidarbha-to-score-triple-century/articleshow/62719476.cms|archivedate=16 April 2025}}</ref> In the final of the 2019 Irani Trophy, Atharva played a match-winning 72. Atharva's highest score in List A cricket is 164 not out against Andhra Pradesh in the Vijay Hazare Trophy on 9 December 2021. He was a member of the winning team of the Under-23 season 2019–20. Atharva was Vidarbha's captain for the Under-19 Coochbehar Trophy.

The '''Indian men's national Under-19 cricket team''' represents [[India]] in cricket at Under-19 level. The team has won a record six [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]] titles, and has the best win percentage in ODIs among all Under-19 national teams. Also, this team has won a record eight  [[Under-19 Men's Asia Cup|U19 Asia Cup]] titles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Under-19s Youth One-Day Internationals / Team records / Results summary|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/337074.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=30 June 2012}}</ref> India are the current holders of the [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]].

The team has won the [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]], a record six times and finished runners-up four times. In [[2000 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2000]], they won it under the captaincy of [[Mohammad Kaif]], in [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2008]], they won it under [[Virat Kohli]]'s leadership, in [[2012 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2012]] under [[Unmukt Chand]], in [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2018]] under [[Prithvi Shaw]], and in [[2022 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2022]] under [[Yash Dhull]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/boys-do-a-men-lift-under-19-cricket-world-cup/story-IndRmyY12yP3Y2x0lVwOUJ.html|title=Boys do a men, lift Under 19 cricket World Cup|first=|last=|date=26 August 2012|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/u19-world-cup-raj-bawa-nishant-sindhu-the-stars-as-all-round-india-beat-england-to-win-record-extending-fifth-title-101644073386391.html|title=U19 World Cup: Raj Bawa, Nishant Sindhu the stars as all-round India beat England to win record-extending fifth title|date=6 February 2022|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/icc-under-19-cricket-world-cup-final-india-vs-australia/story-yjJKkAHHschqhAr1IIV89H.html|title=ICC Under-19 World Cup: Manjot Kalra ton, bowlers give India record 4th title|date=3 February 2018|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref> [[Ayush Mhatre]] led the team to their 6th title in [[2026 Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|2026]].<ref>{{cite web |title=U19 World Cup: India Beat England by 100 Runs to Win 6th Title |url=https://www.khelwire.com/articles/u19-world-cup-india-beat-england-by-100-runs-to-win-6th-title |website=KhelWire |date=6 February 2026 |access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref>

The team has also won the [[Under-19 Men's Asia Cup|U19 Asia Cup]], a record eight times, in 1989, 2003, 2012, 2013–14, 2016, 2018, 2019, and 2021.

The team is currently captained by [[Ayush Mhatre]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 December 2025 |title=India’s U-19 World Cup 2026 squad: Ayush Mhatre to lead; Vaibhav Suryavanshi selected - full team |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/u19-world-cup-2026-india-cricket-team-squad |access-date=31 December 2025 |website=www.olympics.com}}</ref> and coached by former India cricketer [[Hrishikesh Kanitkar]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rahul Dravid replaced as India A India U19 coach| url=https://www.mykhel.com/cricket/rahul-dravid-replaced-as-india-a-india-u-19-coach-125777.html|access-date=24 Jan 2020}}</ref>

'''Siddarth Kaul''' (born 19 May 1990), also spelled '''Siddharth Kaul''', is an Indian former professional cricketer. A [[fast bowler]] who bowls at about 130 km/h, he made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] in 2007. Kaul was a part of the victorious [[Indian U-19 cricket team|India Under-19s team]] at the [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]] and was named as one of the players to be drafted for the [[Indian Premier League]], where he signed for the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]]. He was a part of the Indian squad<ref>{{Cite web |title=India ODI Squad - Asia Cup, 2018 Squad |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asia-cup-2018-1153237/india-odi-squad-1158029/series-squads |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> which won the [[2018 Asia Cup]]. In 2024, he retired from Indian cricket.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Siddarth Kaul retires from Indian cricket, open to playing overseas |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/india-news-siddarth-kaul-retires-from-indian-cricket-open-to-playing-overseas-1462439 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

His father, Tej Kaul, played across three seasons in the 1970s for [[Jammu and Kashmir cricket team|Jammu and Kashmir]]. His brother, [[Uday Kaul]], also played for Punjab, and later for Chandigarh and Mizoram.

'''Umeshkumar Tilak Yadav''' (born 25 October 1987) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who represented the [[India national cricket team|Indian cricket team]]. He currently plays for [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]] in domestic cricket. He played 57 [[Test cricket|test]] matches for India and his [[Fast bowling|fast-bowling]] contributed of India winning test matches particularly at home. Yadav was a member of the team that won the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]]. He was the highest wicket-taker for India in the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most Wickets For ICC Cricket World Cup, 2014/15 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/tournament/bowling-most-wickets-career/icc-cricket-world-cup-2014-15-6537 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

A right-arm fast bowler, Yadav has played for Vidarbha at domestic level since 2008 and is the first player from the team to have played Test cricket. He made his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut against [[Zimbabwe national cricket team|Zimbabwe]] in May 2010. The following year, in November, Yadav made his Test debut against the [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]]. He holds the record of the [[Strike rate|highest strike rate]] in an innings in Test cricket after scoring 31 runs in 10 balls at a strike rate of 310 against South Africa in October 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aninews.in/news/sports/cricket/umesh-yadav-breaks-stephen-flemings-15-year-old-record20191020191844/|title=Umesh Yadav breaks Stephen Fleming's 15-year-old record|website=ANI News|language=en|access-date=19 April 2020|archive-date=28 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028113616/https://aninews.in/news/sports/cricket/umesh-yadav-breaks-stephen-flemings-15-year-old-record20191020191844/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Mohammad Nabi Eisakhil''' ({{langx|ps|{{Nastaliq|محمد نبي عیسی خېل}}}}; born 1 January 1985{{efn|name=dob}}) is an Afghan cricketer and former captain of the [[Afghanistan national cricket team]]. Nabi is an attacking batting all-rounder, playing as a right-handed [[batsman (cricket)|batsman]] and [[off break|off-break]] bowler.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Full Scorecard of Afghanistan vs Ireland 2nd Match 2009/10 - Score Report  |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-associates-t20-series-2009-10-440159/afghanistan-vs-ireland-2nd-match-440224/full-scorecard |access-date=2022-12-21 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He played a major role in Afghanistan's rise to the top level of international cricket, playing in both their first [[One Day International]] in April 2009 and their first [[Test cricket|Test match]] in June 2018. He was also part of Afghanistan's first T20I team which played against Ireland on 1 February 2010 and became the fifth cap of Afghanistan national team in Twenty20 Internationals. Nabi was also part of Afghanistan's first T20 World Cup team which played the [[2010 ICC World Twenty20]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Full Scorecard of Afghanistan vs India 3rd Match, Group C 2010 - Score Report  |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-world-twenty20-2010-412671/afghanistan-vs-india-3rd-match-group-c-412679/full-scorecard |access-date=2022-12-21 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He captained the team during their appearances in the [[2014 Asia Cup]] and the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]]. Nabi has also played in numerous [[Twenty20]] franchise tournaments and was the first player from Afghanistan to be selected in the [[Indian Premier League]] player auction. As of June 2024, Nabi holds a unique record of having been an integral part of Afghanistan team in defeating 45 nations in international cricket.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-06-23 |title='Our journey starts now': Afghanistan's instant vow to continue freakish cricketing rise |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/our-journey-starts-now-afghanistan-s-instant-vow-to-continue-freakish-cricketing-rise |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=ICC |language=en}}</ref>

In September 2019, Nabi retired from Test cricket with the stated aim to prolong his [[limited overs cricket]] career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/bangladesh-vs-afghanistan-mohammad-nabi-set-to-retire-from-test-cricket/story-F53id57KzYfmUAR7kQifSI.html |title=Bangladesh vs Afghanistan: Mohammad Nabi set to retire from Test cricket |work=Hindustan Times |access-date=6 September 2019}}</ref> In August 2020, Nabi was inducted as a member of the [[Afghanistan Cricket Board]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29704387/mohammad-nabi-inducted-afghanistan-cricket-board- |title=Mohammad Nabi inducted into Afghanistan Cricket Board |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 August 2020}}</ref>
