'''Nathan Mitchell Coulter-Nile''' (born 11 October 1987) is an Australian [[cricket]]er who has played at [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] level for the [[Australia national cricket team|Australian national team]]. Domestically, he is contracted to [[Western Australia cricket team|Western Australia]] and the [[Melbourne Stars]].
From [[Perth, Western Australia]], Coulter-Nile attended [[Aquinas College, Perth|Aquinas College]], and represented the state under-17 and under-19 teams, later going on to play three youth ODI matches for the [[Australia Under-19 cricket team|Australian national under-19 team]]. Having held a rookie contract from the [[Western Australian Cricket Association]] (WACA) for several seasons, he made his debut at state level during the 2009–10 season, and has since become a regular selection in Western Australia and the Perth Scorchers' [[fast bowling]] attacks. Coulter-Nile made his Twenty20 International debut for the [[Australia national cricket team|Australian national cricket team]] in February 2013, and his ODI debut in September 2013.

'''Hendrik Erasmus '''"'''Rassie'''"''' van der Dussen''' (born 7 February 1989) is a South African professional [[cricket]]er who represents the [[South Africa national cricket team]] and plays for [[Gauteng (cricket team)|Gauteng]] in domestic cricket.<ref name="Cricinfo">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/337790.html |title=Rassie van der Dussen |access-date=7 November 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In the 2018 ''South African Cricket Annual'', he was named as one of the five Cricketers of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/27248/Markram-Ngidi-named-among-SA-Cricket-Annuals-Top-Five |title=Markram, Ngidi named among SA Cricket Annual's Top Five |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=29 November 2018 |archive-date=27 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327221829/https://cricket.co.za/news/27248/Markram-Ngidi-named-among-SA-Cricket-Annuals-Top-Five |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Markram, Ngidi among SA Cricket Annual's Cricketers of the Year |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/markram-ngidi-among-sa-cricket-annual-s-cricketers-of-the-year-1167457 |access-date=29 November 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2019, van der Dussen was named the International Men's Newcomer of the Year at [[Cricket South Africa]]'s annual award ceremony.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/31359/Du-Plessis-and-Van-Niekerk-honoured-with-CSAs-top-awards |title=Du Plessis and Van Niekerk honoured with CSA's top awards |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=4 August 2019 |archive-date=4 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190804070830/https://cricket.co.za/news/31359/Du-Plessis-and-Van-Niekerk-honoured-with-CSAs-top-awards |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Du Plessis, van Niekerk named CSA Cricketers of the Year |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/du-plessis-van-niekerk-named-csa-cricketers-of-the-year-1196665 |access-date=4 August 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Later the same month, [[Cricket South Africa]] awarded him with a central contract for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rassie van der Dussen earns Cricket South Africa central contract |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/rassie-van-der-dussen-earns-cricket-south-africa-central-contract-1197256 |access-date=12 August 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

'''Praveen Dubey''' (born 1 July 1993) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Karnataka cricket team|Karnataka]] in domestic cricket. He is a right-handed batsman and [[leg break]] [[googly]] bowler. He was signed up by [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] at the 2016 IPL players auction for {{INR}} 35 lakh.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of players sold and unsold at IPL auction 2016|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2016/content/story/969473.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=5 March 2016}}</ref> In February 2017, he was bought by the [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] team for the [[2017 Indian Premier League]] for {{INR}} 10 [[lakh]].<ref name="IPL">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2017/content/story/1083407.html |title=List of players sold and unsold at IPL auction 2017 |accessdate=20 February 2017 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In 2020, the [[Delhi Capitals]] named him as a replacement for their injured player [[Amit Mishra]].<ref>{{Cite web|author=<!--staff writer-->|date=2020-10-19|title=IPL 2020: Delhi Capitals Announce Pravin Dubey as Replacement For Amit Mishra|url=https://www.india.com/sports/cricket-ipl-2020-delhi-capitals-announce-pravin-dubey-as-replacement-for-amit-mishra-4178209/|access-date=2020-10-31|website=India.com|language=en}}</ref>

He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Karnataka in the [[2017–18 Zonal T20 League]] on 8 January 2018.<ref name="T20">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1130665.html |title=South Zone, Inter State Twenty-20 Tournament at Visakhapatnam, Jan 8 2018 |accessdate=8 January 2018 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 11 January 2020, for Karnataka in the [[2019–20 Ranji Trophy]].<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1203522.html |title=Elite, Group B, Ranji Trophy at Rajkot, Jan 11-14 2020 |accessdate=11 January 2020 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> named 27-year-old uncapped leg-spinner Pravin Dube as a replacement for Amit Mishra who was ruled out of IPL 2020 with a finger injury.<ref>{{Cite magazine|author=Akshay Ramesh |date=19 October 2020 |title=IPL 2020: Delhi Capitals find replacement for injured Amit Mishra in leg-spinner Pravin Dube|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/ipl-2020/story/pravin-dube-delhi-capitals-replacement-injured-amit-mishra-karnataka-leg-spinner-1733033-2020-10-19|access-date=2021-08-27|magazine=India Today|language=en}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

'''Heenatigala Pathiranage Matheesha Anushal Vihanga Pathirana''', popularly known as '''Matheesha Pathirana''' ({{langx|si|මතීෂ පතිරණ}}, {{IPA|si|mat̪iːʃə pat̪irənə|}}; {{langx|ta|மதிஷ பத்திரன}}; born 18 December 2002), is a professional Sri Lankan [[cricket]]er who currently plays limited over internationals for the national team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1194795.html |title=Matheesha Pathirana |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=22 August 2021}}</ref> He has been referred to as "Baby Malinga", as he has modelled his bowling action after [[Lasith Malinga]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=WATCH:'Baby Malinga' Matheesha Pathirana breaks camera lens with explosive bouncer during CSK net session |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/watch-baby-malinga-matheesha-pathirana-breaks-camera-lens-with-explosive-bounder-during-csk-net-session-article-91666619 |access-date=20 May 2022 |website=TimesNow |date=19 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2022 |title='Big shoes to fill': Next Malinga lights up IPL - and teenage star could take on Aussies next month |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/indian-premier-league/ipl-2022-matheesha-pathirana-compared-to-sri-lanka-legend-lasith-malinga-video-highlights-ms-dhoni-cricket-news/news-story/04a6e4d8b3af1656fd7b8d0dfc4d5c24 |access-date=20 May 2022 |website=Fox Sports |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ishant Sharma''' ({{audio|Ishant Sharma.ogg|pronunciation}}; born 2 September 1988) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who has represented India in [[Test cricket|Tests]], [[One Day International|ODIs]] and [[T20I]]s. He is a 6 ft 4 in tall<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/interviews/I-enjoy-being-Indias-bowling-spearhead-Ishant-Sharma/articleshow/21966873.cms|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130824002404/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-08-22/interviews/41436662_1_fast-bowling-ishant-sharma-bhuvneshwar-kumar|url-status=live|archive-date=24 August 2013|work=[[The Times of India]]|title=I enjoy being India's bowling spearhead: Ishant Sharma|date=22 August 2013 |access-date=19 September 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/series-tournament/england-in-india-2013/top-stories/Finn-and-Ishant-The-tale-of-two-tall-spearheads/articleshow/18067449.cms|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130521071229/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-01-18/top-stories/36416301_1_ishant-sharma-steven-finn-ashok-dinda|url-status=live|archive-date=21 May 2013|work=[[The Times of India]]|title=Finn and Ishant: The tale of two tall spearheads|date=18 January 2013 |access-date=19 September 2013}}</ref><ref>A CORRESPONDENT (20 October 2013), [https://www.telegraphindia.com/sports/all-over-in-one-ishant-over-australia-win-by-4-wickets-to-take-2-1-lead/cid/254920 "All over in one Ishant over - Australia win by 4 wickets to take 2-1 lead"], ''The Telegraph India''. Retrieved 13 February 2020.</ref> right-arm fast-medium bowler.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/236779.html |title=Ishant Sharma |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 January 2012}}</ref><ref name="Cricket Addictor">{{cite web |url=https://cricketaddictor.com/cricket/top-10-tallest-cricketers-of-all-time/ |title=First-class bowling for each team by Ishant Sharma |date=12 July 2019 |publisher=Cricket Addictor |access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref> In 2011, he became the fifth youngest player to take 100 Test wickets. While often considered a "rhythm" bowler, prioritizing accuracy, he still is one of the fastest Indian bowlers having bowled in excess of 150 km/h on several occasions. In 2020, Indian government has awarded him the [[Arjuna Award]] to recognize his outstanding achievement in cricket. Sharma was a member of the Indian team that won the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]].

In February 2021, during the series [[English cricket team in India in 2020–21|against England]], Ishant took  his [[List of bowlers who have taken 300 or more wickets in Test cricket|300th wicket in Test cricket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/england-in-india/ishant-sharma-the-man-for-the-dirty-job-climbs-mt-300/articleshow/80758767.cms |title=Ishant Sharma, the man for the 'dirty job', climbs Mt 300 |work=Times of India |access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Ishant Sharma Becomes 2nd Indian Pacer to Play 100 Tests|url=https://www.thequint.com/sports/cricket/pink-ball-test-ishant-sharma-becomes-2nd-indian-pacer-to-play-100-tests|access-date=2021-02-26|website=TheQuint|date=24 February 2021|language=en}}</ref> He is regarded as one of the greatest pacers in Indian Cricket.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/england-in-india/1st-test-ishant-sharma-becomes-third-indian-pacer-to-take-300-test-wickets/articleshow/80747352.cms |title=1st Test: Ishant Sharma becomes third Indian pacer to take 300 Test wickets |work=The TImes of India |date=2021-02-08 |access-date=2023-10-28}}</ref>

'''Adil Usman Rashid''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|MBE}} (born 17 February 1988) is an English [[cricket]]er who plays for [[England cricket team|England]] in [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) cricket, and previously played for the [[Test cricket|Test]] team. In domestic cricket, he represents [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]], and has played in multiple [[Twenty20]] leagues. He is regarded as one of the best limited overs English spinners of all time.

Rashid made his ODI and T20I debuts in 2009, and played for the Test team between 2015 and 2019. He was part of the England teams that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/cricket/england-cricket-world-cup-player-ratings-how-every-star-fared-on-the-road-to-glory-a4189706.html |title=England Cricket World Cup player ratings: How every star fared on the road to glory |work=Evening Standard |access-date=15 July 2019|date=15 July 2019 }}</ref> and [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63613694|title=T20 World Cup: England beat Pakistan to win pulsating final in Melbourne|work=BBC Sport|access-date=13 November 2022|date=13 November 2022}}</ref>

Rashid plays as a right-arm [[leg spin|leg break]] [[Bowling (cricket)|bowler]]. He is England's highest wicket-taker among spin bowlers in both ODIs and T20Is, and England's highest wicket-taker in T20Is.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?class=2;id=1;type=team|title=Records. England. One-Day Internationals. Most wickets |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=23 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?class=3;id=1;type=team|title=Records. England. Twenty20 Internationals. Most wickets |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=23 September 2022}}</ref> He surpassed the previous record held by Chris Jordan, who has 108 wickets. Along with [[Jos Buttler]], he holds the world record for highest seventh-wicket stand in ODIs: 177 against [[New Zealand cricket team|New Zealand]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/252072.html|title=Records. One-Day Internationals. Partnership records. Highest partnerships by wicket |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=23 September 2022|archive-date=28 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028191143/https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/252072.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2023 Rashid was named an MBE in [[Charles III|King Charles III]]'s Birthday honours list.

'''Benjamin Andrew Stokes''' (born 4 June 1991) is an <!-- Do not add New Zealand born! Per MOS:BLPLEAD and MOS:CONTEXTBIO unless ethnicity contributes to notability, it should not be mentioned in opening. Please use the talk page to gain consensus first --> English former international [[cricket]]er who [[List of England cricket captains|captained]] the [[England cricket team|England]] [[Test cricket|Test]] team from 2022 to 2026.<ref name=Ben>{{cite news |title=Ben Stokes named England men's Test captain |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ben-stokes-named-england-mens-test-captain-1312611 |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=28 April 2022}}</ref> Stokes played for England in all three formats and is regarded as one of England's greatest all-rounders.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ali |first=Moeen |date=2019-08-26 |title=Magnificent Ben Stokes is England's greatest ever all-rounder |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/aug/26/magnificent-ben-stokes-england-greatest-all-rounder |access-date=2024-06-02 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> In domestic cricket, he represents [[Durham County Cricket Club|Durham]] and has played in multiple [[Twenty20]] leagues around the world. He was part of the England team that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]] and the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]].

Born in [[Christchurch]], New Zealand, Stokes moved to England as a child.<ref name="Telegraph">{{Cite news|last=Hoult|first=Nick|date=15 May 2009|title=Durham's Ben Stokes wins generation game at the Oval|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/cricket/international/england/10345278/England-all-rounder-Ben-Stokes-sees-star-rise-still-further-as-he-puts-Australia-shame-behind-him.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/cricket/international/england/10345278/England-all-rounder-Ben-Stokes-sees-star-rise-still-further-as-he-puts-Australia-shame-behind-him.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|access-date=5 July 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He made his ODI and T20I debuts in 2011 and his Test debut in 2013. He was part of the [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#England|England team]] that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], top-scoring in England's innings in the [[2019 Cricket World Cup Final|final]] before batting in the tied Super Over, winning the [[Player of the match|Man of the Match]] award. He was named the [[Wisden Leading Cricketer in the World]] in 2019, 2020 and 2022, and won the [[Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy|ICC Award for Best Men's Cricketer]] and [[BBC Sports Personality of the Year Award]] in 2019. He was appointed captain of England's Test team in April 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|date=28 April 2022|title=Ben Stokes: England name all-rounder as new Test captain to succeed Joe Root|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/61163496|access-date=30 June 2022|website=bbc.co.uk}}</ref> He was part of the England team that won the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]], top-scoring in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63613694|title=T20 World Cup: England beat Pakistan to win pulsating final in Melbourne|work=BBC|access-date=13 November 2022|date=13 November 2022}}</ref>

An [[all-rounder]], Stokes is a left-handed [[Batting order (cricket)#Middle order|middle-order batsman]] and right-arm [[Fast bowling|fast bowler]]. He holds the Test world record for most runs in an innings at number six, scoring 258 against [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] during [[English cricket team in South Africa in 2015–16|England's 2015–16 tour]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/282860.html|title=Records. Test matches. Batting records. '''Philip Dean Salt''' (born 28 August 1996) is a [[Wales|Welsh]] professional [[cricket]]er who plays internationally for [[England cricket team|England]]{{Efn|Wales is a part of the [[England and Wales Cricket Board]], and Welsh cricketers are eligible to compete for [[England cricket team|England]] internationally.}} and domestically for [[Lancashire County Cricket Club]], and previously for [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]]. Primarily an aggressive right-handed opening [[Batting (cricket)|batter]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://worldtimes24.com/wright-charged-with-rousing-sussex-spirits/|title=Wright charged with rousing Sussex spirits|first=Samshad|last=Sattar|work=World Times 24|access-date=10 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160407080336/http://worldtimes24.com/wright-charged-with-rousing-sussex-spirits/|archive-date=7 April 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> he sometimes keeps wicket and, less frequently, bowls right-arm [[off spin]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/1104/1104883/1104883.html |title=Philip Salt |website=CricketArchive |access-date=12 April 2016}}</ref> Salt made his international debut for England in July 2021. Born in Wales, he moved in his youth to Barbados and then to England. Salt was part of the England team that won the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2022 ICC T20 World Cup]]. He made history after scoring two consecutive centuries in T20Is against West Indies.

'''Harry Cherrington Brook''' (born 22 February 1999) is an English international [[cricket]]er who plays for [[England cricket team|England]] in all three formats of the game and is the [[Test match cricket|Test]] [[Vice Captain (cricket)|vice-captain]], [[One Day International|ODI]] and [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] [[Captain (cricket)|captain]]. Brook plays domestic cricket for [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecricketpaper.com/news/379926/harrys-time-will-surely-come-again/|title=Harry's time will surely come again|date=3 October 2020|access-date=17 March 2021|archive-date=15 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415114529/https://www.thecricketpaper.com/news/379926/harrys-time-will-surely-come-again/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=CAprof>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/1317/1317007/1317007.html |title=Harry Brook |publisher=CricketArchive |access-date=3 July 2017}}</ref> Primarily a right-handed [[batting (cricket)|batsman]], he also bowls right-arm [[fast bowling|medium pace]]. He made his international debut for [[England cricket team|England]] in January 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Harry Brook profile and biography, stats, records, averages, photos and videos|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/harry-brook-911707|access-date=10 February 2022|website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He made a prolific start to his test career by amassing 809 runs in his first six test appearances having batted ten times with a career average of 80.90 and with a strike rate of almost 100.<ref>{{cite web |title=Believe the hype: Harry Brook is heading where few have gone before |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/nz-vs-england-2nd-test-wellington-believe-the-hype-harry-brook-is-heading-where-few-have-gone-before-1360352 |access-date=25 February 2023 |website=ESPNcricinfo }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Harry Brook batting bowling stats, averages and cricket statistics, 2023 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/harry-brook-911707/bowling-batting-stats |access-date=28 February 2023 |website=ESPNcricinfo }}</ref> Brook was part of the [[England cricket team]] that won the [[2022 T20 World Cup]]. In December 2024, he topped the [[ICC men's player rankings|ICC rankings]] for Test batsmen during [[English cricket team in New Zealand in 2024–25|England's tour of New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Brook Replaces Root as World Number One Test Batter |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/cx270jgqr53o|access-date=4 July 2025 |website=BBC Sport }}</ref>

Harry Brook was named as [[ICC Awards#Men's Player of the Month|ICC Men's Player of the Month]] award twice in December 2022 and February 2023.

'''Kumar Kartikeya Singh''' (born 26 December 1997) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who represents [[Madhya Pradesh cricket team|Madhya Pradesh]] in domestic cricket and previously appeared for the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL).<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1159843.html |title=Kumar Kartikeya |access-date=26 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Madhya Pradesh cricket team|Madhya Pradesh]] in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 26 September 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156826.html |title=Elite, Group B, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Delhi, Sep 26 2018 |access-date=26 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Subsequently, he made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Madhya Pradesh in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 28 November 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156995.html |title=Elite, Group B, Ranji Trophy at Thiruvananthapuram, Nov 28 - Dec 1 2018 |access-date=28 November 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Kartikeya also made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Madhya Pradesh in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 2 March 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157199.html |title=Group C, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Indore, Mar 2 2019 |access-date=2 March 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In April 2022, Kartikeya was named as the replacement for [[Arshad Khan (Indian cricketer)|Arshad Khan]] in the [[Mumbai Indians]] squad for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] (IPL), after Khan was ruled out due to an injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-kumar-kartikeya-replaces-injured-arshad-khan-for-mumbai-indians-1312602 |title=IPL 2022: Kumar Kartikeya replaces injured Arshad Khan for Mumbai Indians |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=28 April 2022}}</ref>

'''Akash Madhwal''' (born 25 November 1993) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who has played for [[Uttarakhand cricket team|Uttarakhand]] and [[Mumbai Indians]] as a [[Bowling (cricket)|bowler]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1206039.html |title=Akash Madhwal |access-date=8 November 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>  He is well known for his trajectory and ability to get the ball to skid and rip through from a quick-arm action. He is known for his connection with Indian wicket-keeper batsman [[Rishabh Pant]] as his close neighbour as both live in the same area in Uttarakhand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet Akash Madhwal, Rishabh Pant's engineer neighbour who helped Mukesh Ambani's team win crucial match |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/ipl/report-meet-akash-madhwal-rishabh-pant-s-engineer-neighbour-who-helped-mukesh-ambani-s-team-mi-win-crucial-match-lsg-3044368 |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=DNA India |language=en}}</ref>

On 24 May 2023, he took a [[five-wicket haul]] in the eliminator match against [[Lucknow Super Giants]], conceding only five runs. With this performance, he registered the record for best bowling figures by an uncapped player in IPL history and also won player of the match award for that match.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucknow Super Giants vs Mumbai Indians, Eliminator, Indian Premier League 2023 |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-commentary/69561/lsg-vs-mi-eliminator-indian-premier-league-2023 |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=Cricbuzz |language=en}}</ref>

'''Yash Thakur''' (born 28 December 1998) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1070196.html |title=Yash Thakur |access-date=25 February 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He plays for [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]] in domestic cricket and [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidarbha]] in the [[2016–17 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 25 February 2017.<ref name="LA">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1053707.html |title=Vijay Hazare Trophy, Group A: Punjab v Vidarbha at Delhi, Feb 25, 2017 |access-date=25 February 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Vidarbha in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 28 November 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156989.html |title=Elite, Group A, Ranji Trophy at Raipur, Nov 28 - Dec 1 2018 |access-date=28 November 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Vidarbha in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 21 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157096.html |title=Group B, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Surat, Feb 21 2019 |access-date=21 February 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> On 8 December 2021, on the opening day of the [[2021–22 Vijay Hazare Trophy]], Thakur took his first [[five-wicket haul]] in List A cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/vijay-hazare-trophy-thakurs-five-for-sets-up-seven-wicket-win-for-vidarbha/articleshow/88168431.cms |title=Vijay Hazare Trophy: Thakur's five-for sets up seven-wicket win for Vidarbha |work=The Times of India |access-date=8 December 2021}}</ref>

He was bought by [[Lucknow Super Giants]] for 45 lakhs in the players auction ahead of [[2023 Indian Premier League|2023 IPL]],<ref>{{cite news |title=2023 IPL Players Auction |url=https://cricbuzz.com/cricket-series/ipl-2023/auction/players/12096 |access-date=3 April 2023 |work=[[Cricbuzz]] |language=en}}</ref> and made his IPL debut on 3 April 2023 against [[Chennai Super Kings]].<ref>{{cite news |title=6th Match (N), Chennai, April 03, 2023, Indian Premier League |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/indian-premier-league-2023-1345038/chennai-super-kings-vs-lucknow-super-giants-6th-match-1359480/live-cricket-score |access-date=3 April 2023 |work=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en}}</ref>

Yash Thakur became the first bowler of IPL 2024 to take five wickets in a match against [[Gujarat Titans]] at the [[Ekana Cricket Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |title= IPL 2024 LSG vs GT|url=https://www.sportstiger.com/live-cricket-score/31253/10277/lsg-vs-gjt-t20-match-21-indian-premier-league-2024|access-date=14 April 2024 |work= SportsTiger |language=en}}</ref>

'''Sanvir Singh''' (born 12 October 1996) is an Indian domestic [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] in domestic cricket and previously appeared for [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1132219.html |title=Sanvir Singh |accessdate=28 September 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 28 September 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156862.html |title=Elite, Group A, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Bengaluru, Sep 28 2018 |accessdate=28 September 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Punjab in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 1 November 2018, scoring a century in the first innings.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156945.html |title=Elite, Group B, Ranji Trophy at Visakhapatnam, Nov 1-4 2018 |accessdate=1 November 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/104876/ranji-highlights-mumbai-up-assert-dominance |title=Ranji Highlights: Mumbai, UP assert dominance; Mudhasir picks four in four balls |work=Cricbuzz |accessdate=2 November 2018}}</ref> In November 2019, he was named in India's squad for the [[2019 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]] in Bangladesh.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/kamlesh-nagarkoti-returns-to-indian-team-for-emerging-asia-cup/articleshow/71378153.cms|title=India Under-23s Squad|work=Time of India|accessdate=1 October 2019}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 4 November 2021, for Punjab in the [[2021–22 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280199.html |title=Elite, Group A, Lucknow, Nov 4 2021, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=4 November 2021}}</ref> He was bought by Sunrisers Hyderabad for Rs.20 [[Lakh]], in the [[2023 Indian Premier League]] auction.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/ipl-auction-2023-full-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-101671785341463.html|title = IPL Auction 2023: Full list of sold and Unsold players|work=Hindustan Times|access-date= 17 February 2023}}</ref>

'''Duan Jansen''' (born 1 May 2000) is a South African [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/595954.html |title=Duan Jansen |access-date=12 January 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[North West cricket team|North West]] in the [[2018–19 CSA 3-Day Provincial Cup]] on 10 January 2019.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157482.html |title=Pool B, CSA 3-Day Provincial Cup at Potchefstroom, Jan 10-12 2019 |access-date=12 January 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for North West in the [[2018–19 CSA Provincial One-Day Challenge]] on 20 January 2019.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157578.html |title=Cross Pool, CSA Provincial One-Day Challenge at Bloemfontein, Jan 20 2019 |access-date=20 January 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In September 2019, he was named in [[Free State (cricket team)|Free State]]'s squad for the [[2019–20 CSA Provincial T20 Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/31632/Free-State-Announces-Provincial-T20-Squad |title=Free State Announces Provincial T20 Squad |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=10 September 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=March 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Free State in the 2019–20 CSA Provincial T20 Cup on 13 September 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1200364.html |title=1st Match, Pool A, CSA Provincial T20 Cup at Benoni, Sep 13 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=13 September 2019}}</ref> In April 2021, he was named in [[North West (cricket team)|North West]]'s squad, ahead of the 2021–22 cricket season in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |title=CSA reveals Division One squads for 2021/22 |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=20 April 2021 |archive-date=20 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420104034/http://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Duan's twin brother, [[Marco Jansen|Marco]], also played cricket for North West and currently plays for the [[South Africa national cricket team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/firstcricket/sports-news/india-vs-south-africa-meet-duan-and-marco-jansen-17-year-old-twins-who-have-impressed-virat-kohli-and-co-in-nets-4315541.html |title=India vs South Africa: Meet Duan and Marco Jansen, 17-year-old twins who have impressed Virat Kohli and Co in nets |work=First Post |access-date=5 March 2019}}</ref> Duan was part of the 2022 St Kitts & Nevis Patriots team competing in the 6ixty tournament and CPL. During the 6ixty tournament, he finished as one of the leading bowlers and helped his team win the tournament.

'''Vivrant Sharma''' (born 30 October 1999) is an Indian domestic [[cricket]]er.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1252370.html |title=Vivrant Sharma |work=ESPN Cricinfo|access-date=23 December 2022}}</ref> An integral part of the [[Jammu and Kashmir cricket team|Jammu & Kashmir]] middle order, he came into the limelight for his explosive batting in the [[2022–23 Vijay Hazare Trophy]]. He was Jammu & Kashmir's highest run scorer in the tournament amassing 395 runs at an average of 56.42.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/who-is-vivrant-sharma-the-jk-batter-who-fetched-rs-2-6-crore-at-ipl-auction/articleshow/96458965.cms |title= Who is Vibrant Sharma |work=Times of India |access-date=23 December 2022}}</ref>

He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 4 November 2021, for Jammu & Kashmir in the [[2021–22 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280206.html |title=Elite, Group C, Vadodara, Nov 4 2021, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=4 November 2021}}</ref> After spending a year with [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] as a net bowler, he was bought by them for Rs 2.6 [[crore]], 13 times his base price in the [[2023 Indian Premier League]] auction.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/ipl-auction-2023-full-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-101671785341463.html |title=IPL Auction 2023: Full list of sold and unsold players|work=Hindustan Times|access-date=17 February 2023}}</ref> He was released by [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in November 2023 after just one season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/sunrisers-hyderabad-ipl-auction-2024-srh-full-list-of-players-retained-released-retention-deadline-day/article67572784.ece|title=Sunrisers Hyderabad full list of players retained, released and traded ahead of IPL 2024 auction|work=The Hindu Sportstar|access-date=26 November 2023}}</ref>

'''David Wiese''' (born 18 May 1985) is a South African-born Namibian former [[cricket]]er who has played for [[Namibia national cricket team|Namibia]] in international cricket.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-10-06|title=David Wiese keen to make up for lost time with Namibia: 'It's been 10 years in the making'|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2021/10/06/david-wiese-keen-to-make-up-for-lost-time-with-namibia-its-been-10-years-in-the-making/|access-date=2021-12-10|website=The National}}</ref> Wiese became eligible to play international cricket for [[Namibia national cricket team|Namibia]] due to his father having been born in [[Namibia]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.namibian.com.na/104346/read/Eagles-to-face-Emerging-Zimbabwe |title=Eagles to face Emerging Zimbabwe |access-date=14 August 2021 |work=The Namibian}}</ref> Wiese played international cricket for [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] from 2013 to 2016, before making his international debut for Namibia in October 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/david-wiese-221140 |title=David Wiese |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|title=The man who played for two countries|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/58822715|access-date=2021-12-10}}</ref>

Previously, Wiese ended his South Africa career in 2017 to play in county cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/jan/09/david-weise-south-africa-country-county-kolpak-sussex|title=South Africa's David Wiese turns back on country for Sussex deal|website=The Guardian|access-date=1 November 2021}}</ref> He has also made 67 [[First-class cricket|first-class]] appearances since his debut in October 2005. He currently plays for [[Lahore Qalandars]] in [[Pakistan Super League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Former Protea David Wiese stars in Pakistan Super League|url=https://www.news24.com/sport/cricket/former-protea-david-wiese-stars-in-pakistan-super-league-20201117|access-date=2021-08-14|website=Sport|language=en-US}}</ref> His form since his breakthrough into first-class cricket saw him selected to play for [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] in the [[2009 Hong Kong Cricket Sixes]], where he was the leading wicket-taker,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://stats.cricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5566;type=tournament |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718093237/http://stats.cricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5566;type=tournament |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-18 |title=Records / Hong Kong Cricket Sixes, 2009/10 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=2010-01-14 }}</ref> and for the South Africa Invitation XI in two matches against [[England cricket team|England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Articles/12/12145.html |title=Tod sign David Wiese |publisher=CricketArchive |last=Stockley |first=Nigel |date=2009-12-21 |access-date=2010-01-14}}</ref> He is known for his explosive low-order batting and an ability to deliver slow balls.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESPNcricinfo Awards 2015 T20 bowling winner: David Wiese, variety seamer |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/espncricinfo-awards-2015-t20-bowling-winner-david-wiese-5-for-23-vs-west-indies-975929 |access-date=2021-08-14 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

'''Swapnil Kamlesh Singh''' (born 22 January 1991) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Tripura cricket team|Tripura]] and [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]]. He is a [[Bowler (cricket)|bowler]] who bats right-handed and bowls [[slow left-arm orthodox]].

He made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Baroda in 2006 at the age of 14 and was a member of the [[Mumbai Indians]] squad in 2008. In a match of the [[2014–15 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] against Saurashtra, he took six wickets for 19 runs from four overs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, West Zone: Baroda v Saurashtra at Pune, Mar 27, 2015|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india/engine/match/776067.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=2 June 2015}}</ref>

He was the leading run-scorer for Baroda in the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]], with 565 runs in six matches.<ref name="Ranji1718">{{cite news |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12014;team=1610;type=tournament |title=Ranji Trophy, 2017/18: Baroda batting and bowling averages |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=3 April 2018}}</ref> In July 2018, he was named in the squad for India Blue for the [[2018–19 Duleep Trophy]]. He was bought for INR 10 lakhs by [[Kings XI Punjab]] at the 2016 IPL auction and made his [[Indian Premier League]] debut during the season. He played for [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in 2023 and for [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] in 2024.<ref name="Duleep18">{{cite news |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/24173214/sanju-samson-picked-india-passing-yo-yo-test |title=Samson picked for India A after passing Yo-Yo test |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=23 July 2018 |accessdate=23 July 2018}}</ref>

'''Kulwant Khejroliya''' (born 13 March 1992) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1083033.html |title=Kulwant Khejroliya |access-date=26 February 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in the [[2016–17 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 26 February 2017.<ref name="LA">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1053739.html |title=Vijay Hazare Trophy, Group B: Delhi v Himachal Pradesh at Bhubaneswar, Feb 26, 2017 |access-date=26 February 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Prior to his debut, he was bought by the [[Mumbai Indians]] team for the [[2017 Indian Premier League]] for 10 [[lakh]]s.<ref name="IPL">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2017/content/story/1083407.html |title=List of players sold and unsold at IPL auction 2017 |access-date=20 February 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Delhi in the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]] on 6 October 2017.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1118612.html |title=Group A, Ranji Trophy at Delhi, Oct 6-9 2017 |access-date=6 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Delhi in the [[2017–18 Zonal T20 League]] on 9 January 2018.<ref name="T20">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1130675.html |title=North Zone, Inter State Twenty-20 Tournament at Delhi, Jan 9 2018 |access-date=9 January 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Later the same month, he was bought by the [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] in the [[List of 2018 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2018 IPL auction]].<ref name="IPL2018">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22218394/ipl-2018-player-auction-list-sold-unsold-players |title=List of sold and unsold players |access-date=27 January 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In October 2018, in the quarter-finals of the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]], he took a [[Hat-trick (cricket)|hat-trick]] for Delhi against [[Haryana cricket team|Haryana]], finishing with figures of six wickets for 31 runs from his ten overs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8890/report/1158650/delhi-vs-haryana-2nd-quarter-final-vijay-hazare-trophy |title=Gambhir 104, Khejroliya hat-trick book Delhi's semi-final berth |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 October 2018}}</ref> He was released by the Royal Challengers Bangalore ahead of the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28087425/where-do-eight-franchises-stand-2020-auction |title=Where do the eight franchises stand before the 2020 auction? |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 November 2019}}</ref>

|access-date=2025-08-25 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} Shakib Al Hasan made his Test debut in 2007 against [[India national cricket team|India]]. His breakthrough came in the Test against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] in [[Chittagong]] in 2008, where he picked up 7 wickets for 36 runs, the best figures by a Bangladeshi bowler at that time. He quickly established himself as one of the team's leading performers. He has scored over 4,000 runs and taken more than 200 wickets in this format. He has also captained the team on their first-ever Test match win over [[England cricket team|England]] in 2016.{{Cite news |last=Marks |first=Vic |date=2016-10-30 |title=Bangladesh claim historic Test win over England as collapse ensures tied series |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/oct/30/bangladesh-beat-england-draw-test-series |access-date=2023-05-05 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=5 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505200845/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/oct/30/bangladesh-beat-england-draw-test-series |url-status=live }} In ODIs, Shakib has been more successful. He has scored over 6,000 runs and taken more than 270 wickets in the format, becoming the fastest player in history to achieve the double of 5,000 runs and 250 wickets in ODIs.{{Cite news |date=2019-06-02 |title=Quickest to 5,000 Runs and 250 Wickets, Shakib Al Hasan Joins Elite All-Rounders Club |url=https://www.news18.com/news/sports/bangladesh-south-africa-shakib-al-hasan-cricket-quickest-to-5000-runs-and-250-wickets-joins-elite-all-rounders-club-2169465.html |access-date=2023-05-05 |work=News18 |language=en |archive-date=5 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505200845/https://www.news18.com/news/sports/bangladesh-south-africa-shakib-al-hasan-cricket-quickest-to-5000-runs-and-250-wickets-joins-elite-all-rounders-club-2169465.html |url-status=live }} In the [[2012 Asia Cup]], Shakib scored 237 runs, including three fifties, and took six wickets. Bangladesh progressed to the tournament's final for the first time but eventually lost to Pakistan by 2 runs, and he was awarded the Player of the tournament award in that edition of the tournament.{{Cite web |date=22 March 2012 |title=Asia Cup – Final |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asia-cup-2011-12-524504/bangladesh-vs-pakistan-final-535800/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en}} He is considered one of the most impactful players of the [[ICC Cricket World Cup 2019|2019 ICC Cricket World Cup]],{{Cite web |date=2019-07-16 |title=Why Shakib Al Hasan, not Kane Williamson, deserved to bag ICC World Cup 2019 Player of the Tournament award |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/was-peerless-shakib-al-hasan-robbed-off-icc-world-cup-2019-player-of-the-tournament-award/454386 |access-date=2023-07-22 |website=www.timesnownews.com |language=en |archive-date=22 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722070432/https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/was-peerless-shakib-al-hasan-robbed-off-icc-world-cup-2019-player-of-the-tournament-award/454386 |url-status=live }} where he broke the record of maximum runs scored in the group stages of the World Cup which was previously held by [[Sachin Tendulkar]] and finished as the third-highest run-scorer, scoring 606 runs in total at the tournament.{{Cite web |title=Most runs in ICC Cricket World Cup, 2019 |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=12357&type=tournament |access-date=2022-10-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} He has played for various T20 tournaments around the world for many teams, including [[Kolkata Knight Riders]], [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]], [[Jamaica Tallawahs]] and [[Dhaka Dynamites|Dhaka Dominators]], where he won the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) twice with Kolkata Knight Riders in 2012 and 2014. He also won the [[Bangladesh Premier League]] (BPL) title 3 times in 2012, 2013 and 2016 with [[Dhaka Dominators]]. He was named the player of the tournament in BPL a record four times, in 2012, 2013, 2018 and 2022.{{Cite web |date=2022-02-18 |title=Shakib adjudged player of the tournament for the fourth time in BPL |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/sports/shakib-adjudged-player-tournament-fourth-time-bpl-372622 |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=The Business Standard |language=en}} He has won 41 man-of-the-match awards, the highest for any Bangladeshi player and 16 man-of-the-series awards in all formats. Between 2009 and 2022, he captained the Bangladesh cricket team in 120 matches across all three formats. Shakib Al Hasan has been a consistent performer for the Bangladesh cricket team over the years.{{cite news | url=https://en.prothomalo.com/sports/cricket/ysuww9o47g | title=Shakib first cricketer to bag 700 intl wickets, 14,000 runs |work=Prothom Alo | date=26 May 2024 }} His career has been filled with controversies over the years, consistently making it to the top of domestic media headlines.{{Cite magazine |date=2022-01-11 |title=Shakib Al Hasan Disciplinary Issues: Ten Times When Bangladesh Superstar Got Involved In Controversies |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/sports/sports-news-shakib-al-hasan-disciplinary-issues-ten-times-when-bangladesh-superstar-got-involved-in-controversies-news-385047 |access-date=2022-10-07 |magazine=Outlook |language=en |archive-date=7 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007094850/https://www.outlookindia.com/website/story/sports-news-shakib-al-hasan-disciplinary-issues-ten-times-when-bangladesh-superstar-got-involved-in-controversies/385047 |url-status=live }} He is considered one of the most influential and followed people on [[social media]] in Bangladesh.{{citation needed|date=January 2026}} He was ranked the 90th most famous athlete in the world by [[ESPN.com|ESPN]] in 2019. He was included in the [[ICC Men's ODI Team of the Year|ICC Men's Team of the Year]] twice (2009, 2021).{{citation needed|date=January 2026}}

He is the current captain of the Test team, reappointed in 2026 having previously held the role from 2017 to 2022. He plays for [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]] in [[County cricket|English domestic cricket]]. Root is currently the leading run-scorer among active batsmen, the [[List of players who have scored 10,000 or more runs in Test cricket|second highest run-scorer of all time]] in [[Test cricket]] and the [[List of England Test cricket records|highest run scorer for England]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/live/cx0092z3n9xt|title=England vs West Indies LIVE: Second Test, day four, Trent Bridge – cricket score, radio commentary, video highlights and text updates|website=BBC Sport|access-date=3 January 2026}}</ref> Root is widely regarded as one of the greatest cricketers of his era and among the finest England has produced.<ref>{{cite web |title=Joe Root 'England's best player of all time' - Gooch |date=15 June 2023 |url=https://au.sports.yahoo.com/joe-root-englands-best-player-134800507.html |publisher=Yahoo Sport |access-date=1 December 2023}}</ref> He was part of the England team that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], where he top scored for England. {{As of|2026|03}}, he has topped the [[ICC men's player rankings|ICC rankings]] for Test batsmen on ten occasions.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=31 July 2024 |title=Joe Root goes to No. 1 on the ICC rankings for Test batters |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/joe-root-goes-to-no-1-on-the-icc-rankings-for-test-batters-1445561 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=2 August 2024}}</ref>

Root made his Test debut in 2012, his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut in 2013 and played for the England [[Twenty20 International]] team between 2012 and 2019. He captained England's Test team between February 2017 and April 2022,<ref name=espncricinfo>{{cite web |title=Root named England Test captain |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/joe-root-named-england-test-captain-1082205 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170213122031/http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/story/1082205.html |archive-date=13 February 2017 |access-date=13 February 2017 |work=[[Cricinfo]]}}</ref> and holds the records for most Test matches (65), wins (28) as England captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/individual/list_captains.html?class=1&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats | ESPNcricinfo.com|website=Cricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> On the occasion of England's 1,000th Test in 2018, Root was named in the country's greatest all-time Test XI by the [[England and Wales Cricket Board]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/790131|title=England's greatest Test XI revealed|date=30 July 2018|work=ICC|access-date=26 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190726130545/https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/790131|archive-date=26 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> He was named both the [[ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year]] and the [[Wisden Leading Cricketer in the World|''Wisden'' Leading Cricketer in the World]] for 2021.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/61163498 | title=Root named Wisden's leading cricketer in the world | work=BBC Sport |access-date=20 April 2022}}</ref>

A right-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batsman]], Root originally played as an [[Batting order (cricket)#Opening batters|opener]] but has played the majority of his cricket for England in the middle order. He is both England's highest run-scorer in Tests<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/stats/index.html?class=1;filter=advanced;orderby=runs;team=1;template=results;type=batting|title=Batting records | Test matches |website=Cricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> and in ODIs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/stats/index.html?class=2;filter=advanced;orderby=runs;spanmax1=02+Sep+2022;spanval1=span;team=1;template=results;type=batting|title=Batting records | One-Day Internationals |website=Cricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> He holds the record for both most Test (41) and most ODI (20) [[Century (cricket)|centuries]] for England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_hundreds_career.html?class=2&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats|website=Cricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> In June 2022, he became the second batsman for England, and fourteenth overall, to score [[List of players who have scored 10,000 or more runs in Test cricket|10,000 Test runs]].<ref name="BBC Sport">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/61675741 |title=Joe Root: England batter passes 10,000 Test runs |work=BBC Sport |access-date=5 June 2022}}</ref>
Along with [[Harry Brook]], he holds the world record for highest fourth-wicket stand (and fourth highest overall) in Tests (454), and with [[James Anderson (cricketer)|James Anderson]] the highest tenth-wicket partnership (198).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/254836.html|title=Records | Test matches | Partnership records | Highest partnerships by wicket |website=Cricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> He is also England's leading run scorer<ref>{{cite web |title=Joe Root Reopens His Run Factory To Top England's World Cup Charts |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/timellis/2023/10/11/joe-root-reopens-his-run-factory-to-top-englands-world-cup-charts/?sh=44dee41a4ca6 |work=Forbes |access-date=1 December 2023}}</ref> in the ICC World Cup and the only English player to score over 1000 runs in the competition.<ref>{{cite web |title=Root becomes first England batter to score 1000 World Cup runs |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/icc-cricket-world-cup/joe-root-first-england-batter-1000-world-cup-runs-eng-vs-pak-graham-gooch-list-records-news-updates/article67524515.ece |website=Sportstar |date=11 November 2023 |access-date=1 December 2023}}</ref> Root also bowls occasional [[off spin]], and regularly fields at first slip, holding the record for most Test catches by an outfield player.<ref>{{cite web |title=Joe Root breaks Test catch record with 211th grab for England against India |url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12123/13395522/joe-root-breaks-test-catch-record-with-211th-grab-for-england-against-india|website=SkySports|date=11 July 2025 |access-date=14 July 2025}}</ref> As of July 2026, Root is one of only 2 players, along with [[AB de Villiers]], to have a career batting average of 50+ in both Tests and ODI's in the history of international cricket.<ref>{{cite web |title=Root joins AB in exclusive 50 club |url=https://www.sacricketmag.com/root-joins-ab-in-exclusive-50-club/ |website=SACricketMag |access-date=16 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Travis Michael Head''' (born 29 December 1993) is an Australian international [[cricket]]er who represents the [[Australia national cricket team]] in all formats and is the current Test [[Captain (cricket)|vice-captain]].<ref name=ESPNcricinfo/> Known for his high strike rate, Head is a left-handed batter and part-time right arm [[off-spin]] bowler. He is contracted to [[South Australia cricket team|South Australia]] at the state level and the [[Adelaide Strikers]] for the [[Big Bash League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Travis Head Profile – Cricket Player Australia {{!}} Stats, Records, Video |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/travis-head-530011 |access-date=2023-11-23 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> Head has served as both a co vice-captain and vice-captain in Tests in multiple stints.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-test-squad-pakistan-gabba-adelaide-bancroft-neser-burns-head-paine-smith-warner/2019-11-14|title=Bancroft, Burns named in Australia Test squad|work=Cricket Australia|access-date=14 November 2019|archive-date=6 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206221645/https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-test-squad-pakistan-gabba-adelaide-bancroft-neser-burns-head-paine-smith-warner/2019-11-14|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="cricket.com.au">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-test-squad-selections-india-series-green-pucovski-abbott-burns-tour-games/2020-11-12|title=Pucovski, Green headline Test and Australia A squads|website=cricket.com.au|language=en|access-date=12 November 2020|archive-date=12 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112010758/https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-test-squad-selections-india-series-green-pucovski-abbott-burns-tour-games/2020-11-12|url-status=live}}</ref> Head captained Australia in [[Twenty20 International|T20Is]] and served as vice-captain in [[One Day International|ODIs]] in 2024.

Head was a key member of the Australian team that won the [[2023 World Test Championship final]] and [[2023 Cricket World Cup final]], having been adjudged [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Player of the Match]] in both those finals. He also became the second player ever to score a century when batting second in a World Cup final.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A tournament of wonders: All the records that broke at the Cricket World Cup 2023 |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/3790555 |access-date=2023-12-06 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref> He also became the first player to score centuries in two consecutive ICC tournament finals in a same calendar year.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wigmore |first=Tim |date=2023-11-19 |title=Whatever the format, Travis Head has become the ultimate big-game player |language=en-GB |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2023/11/19/travis-head-ultimate-bazballer-become-big-game-player/ |access-date=2023-12-06 |issn=0307-1235}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/certified-freak-travis-head-blows-cricket-world-away/news-story/08431a6963ceac61f1d3026a7e3d57a0|title='Certified freak': Travis Head blows cricket world away|publisher=news.com.au|date=23 November 2023}}</ref>

'''Yudhvir Singh Charak''' (born 13 September 1997) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1206052.html |title=Yudhvir Singh |access-date=12 November 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He currently plays for [[Jammu and Kashmir cricket team|Jammu and Kashmir]] in domestic cricket and for [[Rajasthan Royals]] in the [[Indian Premier League|IPL]].  He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 12 November 2019, for [[Hyderabad cricket team|Hyderabad]] in the [[2019–20 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]].<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1205781.html |title=Group C, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Chandigarh, Nov 12 2019 |access-date=12 November 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 17 December 2019, for Hyderabad in the [[2019–20 Ranji Trophy]].<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1203464.html |title=Elite, Group A, Ranji Trophy at Patiala, Dec 17-20 2019 |access-date=17 December 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> In February 2021, Singh was bought by the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[List of 2021 Indian Premier League personnel changes|IPL auction]] ahead of the [[2021 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2021-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1252152 |title=IPL 2021 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=18 February 2021}}</ref>

In December 2022, he was bought by the [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the IPL auction ahead of the [[2023 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=2023 IPL Players Auction |url=https://cricbuzz.com/cricket-series/ipl-2023/auction/players/15749 |access-date=3 April 2023 |work=Cricbuzz |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for LSG on April 15, 2023, and bowled an economical spell taking 2 wickets.<ref name="IPL 2023: LSG debutant Yudhvir Singh strikes twice in his first two overs, removes PBKS openers in chase">{{cite news |title=IPL 2023: LSG debutant Yudhvir Singh strikes twice in his first two overs, removes PBKS openers in chase |url=https://www.firstpost.com/firstcricket/sports-news/ipl-2023-lsg-debutant-yudhvir-singh-strikes-twice-in-his-first-two-overs-removes-pbks-openers-in-chase-12460682.html |access-date=15 April 2025 |publisher=Firstpost |date=15 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415102114/https://www.firstpost.com/firstcricket/sports-news/ipl-2023-lsg-debutant-yudhvir-singh-strikes-twice-in-his-first-two-overs-removes-pbks-openers-in-chase-12460682.html |archive-date=15 April 2025 |language=en-us}}</ref> Ahead of IPL 2025, [[Rajasthan Royals]] secured the pacer for 35 lakhs.<ref name="IPL 2025 auction: Complete list of sold, unsold players, teamwise remaining purse {{!}} Mint">{{cite news |title=IPL 2025 auction: Complete list of sold, unsold players, teamwise remaining purse {{!}} Mint |url=https://www.livemint.com/sports/cricket-news/ipl-auction-2025-sold-unsold-full-players-list-costliest-cricketer-remaining-purse-amount-teamwise-rishabh-pant-11732478575379.html |access-date=15 April 2025 |work=mint |publisher=Mint |date=25 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415102416/https://www.livemint.com/sports/cricket-news/ipl-auction-2025-sold-unsold-full-players-list-costliest-cricketer-remaining-purse-amount-teamwise-rishabh-pant-11732478575379.html |archive-date=15 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Vijaykumar Vyshak''' (born 31 January 1997) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Karnataka cricket team|Karnataka]] in domestic cricket and [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/777815.html |title=Vijaykumar Vyshak |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=24 February 2021}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 24 February 2021, for [[Karnataka cricket team|Karnataka]] in the [[2020–21 Vijay Hazare Trophy]].<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1250937.html |title=Elite, Group C, Bengaluru, Feb 24 2021, Vijay Hazare Trophy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=24 February 2021}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 5 November 2021, for Karnataka in the [[2021–22 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280239.html |title=Elite, Group B, Guwahati, Nov 6 2021, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=5 November 2021}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 17 February 2022, for Karnataka in the [[2021–22 Ranji Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280412.html |title=Elite, Group C, Chennai, Feb 17 - 20 2022, Ranji Trophy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=17 February 2022}}</ref>

'''Raghav Goyal''' (born 26 January 2001) is an Indian cricketer, who bats left-handed and bowls [[left-arm unorthodox spin]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profile: Raghav Goyal |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/raghav-goyal-1350770 |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He started learning to play cricket at the age of 11.<ref>{{Cite web |title=राघव गोयल का IPL डेब्यू:राघव गोयल ने 11 की उम्र में क्रिकेट खेलना शुरू किया, 21 में IPL डेब्यू |url=https://www.bhaskar.com/local/haryana/panipat/news/raghav-goyal-started-playing-cricket-at-the-age-of-11-ipl-debut-at-21-131253594.html |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=Dainik Bhaskar |language=Hindi}}</ref> He hails from [[Panipat]], a city in [[Haryana]], although he received training from [[Vijay Yadav (cricketer)|Vijay Yadav]] Cricket Academy in [[Faridabad]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=फरीदाबाद के ये 4 खिलाड़ी आईपीएल 2023 में जलवा दिखाने को तैयार, 3 एक ही एकेडमी के |url=https://www.etvbharat.com/hindi/haryana/state/faridabad/faridabad-players-in-ipl-2023-from-vijay-yadav-cricket-academy-faridabad/haryana20230331110517071071327 |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=ETV Bharat News |language=hi}}</ref> He is known for his economical spin bowling and his ability to play big shots.<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=CSK vs MI: कौन हैं मिस्ट्री स्पिनर राघव गोयल? मुंबई इंडियंस ने चेन्नई के खिलाफ चुना, अबतक फर्स्ट क्लास डेब्यू नहीं हुआ |url=https://hindi.news18.com/news/sports/cricket-who-is-raghav-goyal-player-to-make-ipl-debut-for-mumbai-indians-against-chennai-super-kings-ipl-2023-49th-match-6110511.html |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=News18 हिंदी |language=hi}}</ref> 

He took five wickets at an [[economy rate]] of 6.90 in the 2023 DY Patil T20 Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |date= |title=CSK vs MI: Who is Raghav Goyal? Player to make IPL debut in Chennai Super Kings vs Mumbai Indians game |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/sports/cricket/csk-vs-mi-who-is-raghav-goyal-player-to-make-ipl-debut-in-chennai-super-kings-vs-mumbai-indians-game-rohit-sharma-ms-dhoni-2023-05-06-869185 |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=India TV |language=en}}</ref> Consequently, he was bought by the [[Mumbai Indians]] at a price of ₹20 [[lakh]], to play for them in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 IPL auction: The list of sold and unsold players |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/2023-ipl-auction-list-of-sold-unsold-players-1350272 |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> With this, he also became the first player from Panipat to get an IPL call-up.<ref>{{Cite web |title=पानीपत के राघव का IPL में सिलेक्शन:पिता ने कहा- हाथ में बॉल पकड़कर सोता था, शेन वॉर्न-राशिद खान आइडल |url=https://www.bhaskar.com/local/haryana/panipat/news/ipl-cricket-2023-panipat-cricketer-raghav-goyal-selection-in-mumbai-indians-team-130717680.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230520203034/https://www.bhaskar.com/local/haryana/panipat/news/ipl-cricket-2023-panipat-cricketer-raghav-goyal-selection-in-mumbai-indians-team-130717680.html |archive-date=2023-05-20 |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=Dainik Bhaskar}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for the Mumbai Indians on 6 May 2023, against the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[2023 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CSK vs MI, Indian Premier League 2023, 49th Match at Chennai, May 06, 2023 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/indian-premier-league-2023-1345038/chennai-super-kings-vs-mumbai-indians-49th-match-1359523/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He was called in by MI skipper, Rohit Sharma to bowl in defence of MI's 139 score.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Malik |first=Varun |date=2023-05-06 |title=CSK vs MI: Who is Raghav Goyal? Player to make IPL debut in Chennai Super Kings vs Mumbai Indians game |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/sports/cricket/csk-vs-mi-who-is-raghav-goyal-player-to-make-ipl-debut-in-chennai-super-kings-vs-mumbai-indians-game-rohit-sharma-ms-dhoni-2023-05-06-869185 |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=www.indiatvnews.com |language=en}}</ref> Prior to being bought by MI, he had never played any professional cricket match at senior level.<ref>{{Cite news |date= |title=IPL 2023: Left-arm wrist spinners Kartikeya, Goyal impress Mumbai Indians spin consultant Brad Hogg |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-2023-left-arm-wrist-spinners-kartikeya-goyal-impress-mumbai-indians-spin-consultant-brad-hogg/articleshow/99290550.cms |access-date=2024-01-03 |issn=}}</ref>

Before joining the Mumbai Indians, he was a cricket player at Reliance 1 and Sukhna Zone in India.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raghav Goyal Profile - Cricket Player, India {{!}} News, Photos, Stats, Ranking, Records - NDTV Sports |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/players/117317-raghav-goyal-playerprofile |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=NDTVSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

the [[Australian national cricket team|Australian national team]] and [[New South Wales cricket team|New South Wales]] in domestic cricket. A left-arm [[Fast bowling|fast]] bowler and a lower order left-handed batsman, he is Australia's fourth highest wicket-taker in both [[Test cricket|Test]] and [[One Day International]] (ODI) cricket.{{cite web |title=Most wickets for Australia in Tests |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/team/bowling-most-wickets-career/australia-2/test-matches-1 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2025}}{{cite web |title=Most wickets for Australia in ODIs |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/team/bowling-most-wickets-career/australia-2/one-day-internationals-2 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2025}} Starc began playing international cricket in 2010, but the early part of his career was disrupted by persistent injuries. He came to worldwide attention as a prominent member of the Australian squad that won the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]], and was declared Player of the Tournament as a result of his consistent performances throughout the matches. He also was a part of the team that won the [[2023 ICC Cricket World Cup]]. At the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], he picked up 27 wickets, which is an all-time record for the most wickets taken in a single edition of the tournament. In doing so, he became the leading wicket-taker in successive Cricket World Cup tournaments, having previously achieved the feat in 2015 as well. As of November 2023, he is the 3rd-highest wicket taker of all time in ICC Cricket World Cups. He is the fastest bowler in the history of ODI cricket to reach 150 and 200 wickets, taking 77 and 102 matches respectively to reach the milestone. He is also the fastest bowler in the history of Cricket World Cups to reach 50 wickets, taking just 19 WC games to reach the milestone. Starc was also a key member of the Australian team that won the [[2021 ICC T20 World Cup]], and the [[2023 World Test Championship final|2023 ICC World Test Championship final]]. He is one of five players who have managed to win an ICC trophy in all three formats of the game. Starc has been noted for his ability to bowl at great pace, with his fastest delivery being measured at over 160.4 km/h (the fastest ever recorded in a Test match), and for generating [[Swing bowling|reverse swing]] with his bowling.

'''Ricky Bhui''' (born 29 September 1996) is an Indian [[cricket]]er. He is a right-handed batsman and occasional leg spinner.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/642531.html| title = Ricky Bhui profile and biography, stats, records, averages, photos and videos}}</ref> Bhui scored an unbeaten hundred on his List A debut and also scored an unbeaten fifty on his Twenty20 debut.

He currently plays for [[Andhra cricket team|Andhra]] in domestic cricket and [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. In December 2015 he was named in [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup squads|India's squad]] for the [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]] and is the youngest player to feature in the tournament so far.<ref name="India">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-under-19-world-cup-2016/content/story/954021.html |title=Ishan Kishan to lead India at U19 World Cup |accessdate=22 December 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Bhui has also captained the India u17 side for a Triangular series. In January 2018, he was bought by the [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in the [[List of 2018 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2018 IPL auction]]. He studied at Visakha Valley School in Visakhapatnam after graduation in 2020.<ref name="IPL2018">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22218394/ipl-2018-player-auction-list-sold-unsold-players |title=List of sold and unsold players |accessdate=27 January 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>  The only player from the Andhra Pradesh Ranji team to make the cut for [[2018 Indian Premier League|IPL 2018]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ricky Bhui Profile |url=https://m.cricbuzz.com/profiles/9425/ricky-bhui |publisher=CricBuzz|accessdate=21 September 2018}}</ref>

He was bought by [[Delhi Capitals]] for 20 lakhs as an uncapped Wicket-Keeper in [[List of 2024 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2024 IPL auction]].

He was the leading run-scorer for Andhra in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]], with 775 runs in eight matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12592;team=1592;type=tournament |title=Ranji Trophy, 2018/19 - Andhra: Batting and bowling averages |work=ESPNcricinfo |accessdate=10 January 2019}}</ref> In August 2019, he was named in the India Blue team's squad for the [[2019–20 Duleep Trophy]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27331972/shubman-gill-priyank-panchal-faiz-fazal-lead-duleep-trophy-sides |title=Shubman Gill, Priyank Panchal and Faiz Fazal to lead Duleep Trophy sides |work=ESPNcricinfo |accessdate=6 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cricketcountry.com/news/duleep-trophy-2019-shubman-gill-faiz-fazal-and-priyank-panchal-to-lead-duleep-trophy-2019-squad-fixtures-schedule-876560 |title=Duleep Trophy 2019: Shubman Gill, Faiz Fazal and Priyank Panchal to lead as Indian domestic cricket season opens |work=Cricket Country |accessdate=6 August 2019}}</ref> He was released by the Sunrisers Hyderabad ahead of the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28087425/where-do-eight-franchises-stand-2020-auction |title=Where do the eight franchises stand before the 2020 auction? |work=ESPNcricinfo |accessdate=15 November 2019}}</ref>

'''Kumar Kushagra''' (born 23 October 2004) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Jharkhand cricket team|Jharkhand]] in domestic cricket and [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1207295.html |title=Kumar Kushagra |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 February 2021}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 20 February 2021, for [[Jharkhand cricket team|Jharkhand]] in the [[2020–21 Vijay Hazare Trophy]].<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1250896.html |title=Elite, Group B, Indore, Feb 20 2021, Vijay Hazare Trophy |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 February 2021}}</ref> Prior to his debut, he was named in India's squad for the [[2020 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcci.tv/articles/2019/news/139375/four-time-champion-india-announce-u19-cricket-world-cup-squad |title=Four-time champion India announce U19 Cricket World Cup squad |work=Board of Control for Cricket in India |access-date=2 December 2019}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 4 November 2021, for Jharkhand in the [[2021–22 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280205.html |title=Elite, Group C, Vadodara, Nov 4 2021, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=4 November 2021}}</ref>

He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 24 February 2022, for Jharkhand in the [[2021–22 Ranji Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280441.html |title=Elite, Group H, Guwahati, Feb 24 - 27 2022, Ranji Trophy |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=24 February 2022}}</ref> In March 2022, in the preliminary quarter-final match of Ranji Trophy, Kushagra scored his maiden century in first-class cricket,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ranji-trophy-2021-22-1280196/jharkhand-vs-nagaland-preliminary-quarter-final-1280465/match-report |title=Jharkhand in the driver's seat after Kumar Kushagra and Virat Singh hit centuries |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 March 2022}}</ref> before going on to convert it into his maiden double century in first-class cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/ranji-pre-quarters-singh-kushagra-tons-propel-jharkhand-to-402-5-against-nagaland-7816930/ |title=Ranji Pre-quarters: Kumar Kushagra's double ton propel Jharkhand to 763/9 against Nagaland |work=The Indian Express |access-date=13 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ask-steven-who-has-the-most-test-wickets-without-dismissing-the-same-man-twice-1307791 |title=Who has the most Test wickets without dismissing the same man twice? |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=29 March 2022}}</ref> His innings of 67 off 37 balls for Jharkhand in the Vijay Hazare Trophy impressed many.
