'''Angkrish Raghuvanshi''' (born 5 June 2004) is an Indian [[cricket]]er.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |title=Angkrish Raghuvanshi profile and biography, stats, records, averages, photos and videos |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/angkrish-raghuvanshi-1292495 |access-date=23 February 2022 |work=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en}}</ref> He played for the [[India national under-19 cricket team]] in the [[2022 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup]], where he was India's highest run scorer.<ref name="U-19 WC: India Rewrite Record Books With Massive 326 Run Victory Over Uganda">{{cite news |title=U-19 WC: India Rewrite Record Books With Massive 326 Run Victory Over Uganda |url=https://www.thequint.com/sports/cricket/u-19-wc-india-rewrite-record-books-in-massive-win-against-uganda |access-date=27 March 2025 |publisher=TheQuint |date=23 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327061703/https://www.thequint.com/sports/cricket/u-19-wc-india-rewrite-record-books-in-massive-win-against-uganda |archive-date=27 March 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Bawa, Raghuvanshi centuries power massive India win |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/under-19-world-cup-bawa-raghuvanshi-centuries-set-up-massive-win-for-india-against-uganda-1298462 |access-date=23 February 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He won the [[2024 Indian Premier League]] with the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]].

Angkrish Raghuvanshi made his T20 debut for Mumbai against Haryana in October 2023. He made his List A cricket debut for Mumbai against Sikkim on 20 November 2023.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}}

Raghuvanshi, born in Delhi, relocated to Mumbai at the age of 11, where he commenced his training under the guidance of [[Abhishek Nayar]] and Omkar Salvi. Subsequently, he made a permanent move to Mumbai.<ref name=":0" /> KKR acquired him for INR 20 lakh at the IPL 2024 auction.<ref name="Who is Angkrish Raghuvanshi, player who scored blistering half century for Kolkata Knight Riders against Delhi Capitals?">{{cite news |title=Who is Angkrish Raghuvanshi, player who scored blistering half century for Kolkata Knight Riders against Delhi Capitals? |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/ipl/angkrish-raghuvanshi-kolkata-knight-riders-vs-delhi-capitals-9249642/ |access-date=27 March 2025 |publisher=The Indian Express |date=3 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240618040458/https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/ipl/angkrish-raghuvanshi-kolkata-knight-riders-vs-delhi-capitals-9249642/ |archive-date=18 June 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2024 he made his debut in the [[Indian Premier League]] for the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]], scoring 54 runs from 27 balls in his first match against the [[Delhi Capitals]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-07 |title=Angkrish Raghuvanshi has limitations, but he won't let them come in his way |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2024-csk-vs-kkr-angkrish-raghuvanshi-wants-to-realise-his-dreams-like-no-one-has-done-before-1428324 |access-date=2024-04-08 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Who Is Angkrish Raghuvanshi: Former U-19 World Cup Star Setting IPL 2024 On Fire For KKR {{!}} Cricket News">{{cite news |title=Who Is Angkrish Raghuvanshi: Former U-19 World Cup Star Setting IPL 2024 On Fire For KKR {{!}} Cricket News |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/ipl-2024/who-is-angkrish-raghuvanshi-kolkata-knight-riders-youngster-who-dismantled-delhi-capitals-bowlers-5368352 |access-date=27 March 2025 |publisher=NDTVSports |date=3 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241113110852/https://sports.ndtv.com/ipl-2024/who-is-angkrish-raghuvanshi-kolkata-knight-riders-youngster-who-dismantled-delhi-capitals-bowlers-5368352 |archive-date=13 November 2024|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Who is Angkrish Raghuvanshi? Singh, a Leader of India Who Defended Poor, Dies at 77 |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/11/30/world/asia/30singh.html |access-date=2022-05-06 |issn=0362-4331}} In 1969, he joined the [[Indian National Congress]] party and was elected as a member of the [[Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly]].{{Cite news|last=Pandya|first=Haresh|date=2008-11-30|title=V. P. Singh, a Leader of India Who Defended Poor, Dies at 77|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/11/30/world/asia/30singh.html|access-date=2021-11-19|issn=0362-4331}} In the [[First Rajiv Gandhi ministry|Rajiv Gandhi ministry]], Singh was given various cabinet posts, including [[Minister of Finance (India)|Minister of Finance]] and [[Minister of Defence (India)|Minister of Defence]]. Singh was also the [[Leader of the House (Rajya Sabha)|Leader of the Rajya Sabha]] from 1984 to 1987. During his tenure as Minister of Defence, the [[Bofors scandal]] came to light, and Singh resigned from the ministry. In 1988, he formed the [[Janata Dal]] party by merging various factions of the [[Janata Party]]. In the [[1989 Indian general election|1989 elections]], the [[Third Front (India)|National Front]], with the support of the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] (BJP), formed the government and Singh became the prime minister. During his tenure as prime minister, he implemented the [[Mandal Commission]] report for India's [[Other Backward Class|backward castes]], which led to major [[Mandal Commission protests of 1990|protests]] against the act. Under Singh's prime ministership in 1989, the Government of India released five terrorists in exchange for the release of kidnapped Rubaiya Sayeed, daughter of the Union Home Minister, Mufti Mohammad Sayeed. This was a turning point in the history of Kashmir militancy, which left a long lasting impact in Kashmir. In 1990 the [[exodus of Kashmiri Hindus]] from the valley of [[Kashmir Valley|Kashmir]] took place. Following his opposition to the [[Ram Rath Yatra]], the BJP withdrew its support for the National Front, and his government lost the [[Motion of no confidence|vote of no-confidence]]. Singh resigned on 7 November 1990. His prime ministerial tenure lasted for 343 days. Singh was the prime ministerial candidate for the [[Third Front (India)|National Front]] in the [[1991 Indian general election|1991 elections]], but was defeated. He spoke out against the [[Demolition of the Babri Masjid|Babri Masjid demolition]] in 1992. He turned down prime ministership after the [[1996 Indian general election]] even though he was the first choice and relinquished the prime ministership to [[H. D. Deve Gowda]].{{cite web | last=Mukerji | first=Debashish | title=Before Deve Gowda, VP Singh was asked to be PM of United Front. He hid in his flat, car | website=ThePrint | date=8 December 2021 | url=https://theprint.in/pageturner/excerpt/before-deve-gowda-vp-singh-was-asked-to-be-pm-of-united-front-he-hid-in-his-flat-car/777894/ | access-date=29 June 2024}}{{cite web | last=Srinivasaraju | first=Sugata | title=Deve Gowda and the accidental prime ministers | website=The New Indian Express | date=5 June 2021 | url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/opinions/2021/Jun/05/devegowda-and-the-accidental-prime-ministers-2311864.html | access-date=29 June 2024}} After 1996, Singh retired from political posts, but continued to remain a public figure and political critic. He was diagnosed with [[multiple myeloma]] in 1998, and ceased public appearances until the cancer went into remission in 2003. He died from complications of multiple myeloma and kidney failure in 2008. He was cremated with full state honours.

'''Mujeeb Ur Rahman Zadran''' ({{langx|ps|مجیب الرحمن ځدراڼ}}; born 28 March 2001) is an Afghan [[cricket]]er, who plays for the [[Afghanistan national cricket team]]. Two months after his international debut, at the age of 16 years and 325 days, he became the youngest player to take a [[five-wicket haul]] in a [[One Day International]].<ref name="Young5wkt">{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/624507 |title=Mujeeb Ur Rahman continues to makes history |access-date=17 February 2018 |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref> He was one of the eleven cricketers to play in Afghanistan's first [[Test cricket|Test match]], against [[India national cricket team|India]], in June 2018. Afghanistan lost the one-sided Test within two days. Mujeeb scored 15 and 3 in the two innings, respectively, and got one wicket after conceding 75 runs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IND vs AFG, AFG in INDIA 2018, Only Test at Bengaluru, June 14 - 15, 2018 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/afg-in-india-2018-1133249/india-vs-afghanistan-only-test-1133983/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-12-18 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> It was also Mujeeb's [[first-class cricket]] debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27899598/which-bowler-dismissed-most-opening-batsmen-tests |title=Which bowler has dismissed the most opening batsmen in Tests? |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=22 October 2019}}</ref> His uncle, [[Noor Ali Zadran]], is also an Afghan international cricketer.

'''Jhathavedh Subramanyan''' (born 16 September 1999) is a Hong Kong [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/919531.html |title=Jhathavedh Subramanyan |accessdate=8 April 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref><ref name="Wisden">{{Cite web |url=https://www.wisden.com/players/jhathavedh-subramanyan |title=Jhathavedh Subramanyan |accessdate=15 April 2018 |work=Wisden |archive-date=25 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240325102111/https://wisden.com/players/jhathavedh-subramanyan |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 7 April 2018 for [[Durham MCC University|Durham MCCU]] against [[Middlesex County Cricket Club|Middlesex]] as part of the [[2018 Marylebone Cricket Club University Matches|Marylebone Cricket Club University fixtures]].<ref name="FC">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1127753.html |title=Marylebone Cricket Club University Matches at Northwood, Apr 7-9 2018 |accessdate=8 April 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

Prior to his first-class debut, Subramanyan captained the Hong Kong U-19s in the [[Under-19 Cricket World Cup]] qualifiers and took five wickets against Oman in October 2016.<ref name="five">{{Cite web|url=http://timesofoman.com/article/93400 |title=Cricket: Hong Kong too good for Oman at ICC U-19 World Cup Qualifier |accessdate=8 April 2018 |work=Times of Oman}}</ref> In September 2017, he was named in Hong Kong's squad for fixtures in the [[2015–17 ICC World Cricket League Championship]] and the [[2015–17 ICC Intercontinental Cup]].<ref name="squad">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/96867/hong-kong-name-anshuman-rath-vice-captain-for-world-cricket-league-fixtures |title=Hong Kong name Rath vice captain for WCL, I-Cup fixtures |accessdate=8 April 2018 |work=CricBuzz}}</ref>

In August 2018, he was named in Hong Kong's squad for the [[2018 Asia Cup Qualifier]] tournament.<ref name="HKACQ">{{cite web |url=http://www.hkcricket.org/en/media/news/hong-kong-squad-for-the-acc-asia-cup-qualifiers-2018-%EF%BC%8D-27th-august-8th-september-2018 |title=Hong Kong Squad for the ACC Asia Cup Qualifiers 2018 － 27th August - 8th September 2018 |work=Hong Kong Cricket |accessdate=4 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180804200907/http://www.hkcricket.org/en/media/news/hong-kong-squad-for-the-acc-asia-cup-qualifiers-2018-%EF%BC%8D-27th-august-8th-september-2018 |archive-date=4 August 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was ruled of the tournament due to injury.<ref name="injury">{{cite web |url=https://www.hkcricket.org/zh/news/aftab-hussain-replaces-jhatha-subramanyan-in-asia-cup-qualifiers-squad |title=Aftab Hussain replaces Jhatha Subramanyan in Asia Cup Qualifiers squad |work=Hong Kong Cricket |accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref> In April 2019, he was named in Hong Kong's squad for the [[2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two]] tournament in Namibia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/1173815 |title=All to play for in last ever World Cricket League tournament |work=International Cricket Council |accessdate=11 April 2019}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Hong Kong against [[Canada national cricket team|Canada]] in the 2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two tournament on 20 April 2019.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1174829.html |title=2nd match, ICC World Cricket League Division Two at Windhoek, Apr 20 2019 |accessdate=20 April 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In 2023, Subramanyan soon was picked up by the cricket team Lyca Kovai Kings in the first ever TNPL (Tamil Nadu Premier League) auction upon recommendation from the team's captain [[Shahrukh Khan (cricketer)|Shahrukh Khan]], and took 11 wickets in 9 matches. Due to his stellar performance, he was subsequently picked up by the team [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in the 2024 IPL (Indian Premier League) auction.

The '''Indian men's national Under-19 cricket team''' represents [[India]] in cricket at Under-19 level. The team has won a record six [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]] titles, and has the best win percentage in ODIs among all Under-19 national teams. Also, this team has won a record eight  [[Under-19 Men's Asia Cup|U19 Asia Cup]] titles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Under-19s Youth One-Day Internationals / Team records / Results summary|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/337074.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=30 June 2012}}</ref> India are the current holders of the [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]].

The team has won the [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]], a record six times and finished runners-up four times. In [[2000 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2000]], they won it under the captaincy of [[Mohammad Kaif]], in [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2008]], they won it under [[Virat Kohli]]'s leadership, in [[2012 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2012]] under [[Unmukt Chand]], in [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2018]] under [[Prithvi Shaw]], and in [[2022 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2022]] under [[Yash Dhull]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/boys-do-a-men-lift-under-19-cricket-world-cup/story-IndRmyY12yP3Y2x0lVwOUJ.html|title=Boys do a men, lift Under 19 cricket World Cup|first=|last=|date=26 August 2012|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/u19-world-cup-raj-bawa-nishant-sindhu-the-stars-as-all-round-india-beat-england-to-win-record-extending-fifth-title-101644073386391.html|title=U19 World Cup: Raj Bawa, Nishant Sindhu the stars as all-round India beat England to win record-extending fifth title|date=6 February 2022|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/icc-under-19-cricket-world-cup-final-india-vs-australia/story-yjJKkAHHschqhAr1IIV89H.html|title=ICC Under-19 World Cup: Manjot Kalra ton, bowlers give India record 4th title|date=3 February 2018|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref> [[Ayush Mhatre]] led the team to their 6th title in [[2026 Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|2026]].<ref>{{cite web |title=U19 World Cup: India Beat England by 100 Runs to Win 6th Title |url=https://www.khelwire.com/articles/u19-world-cup-india-beat-england-by-100-runs-to-win-6th-title |website=KhelWire |date=6 February 2026 |access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref>

The team has also won the [[Under-19 Men's Asia Cup|U19 Asia Cup]], a record eight times, in 1989, 2003, 2012, 2013–14, 2016, 2018, 2019, and 2021.

The team is currently captained by [[Ayush Mhatre]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 December 2025 |title=India’s U-19 World Cup 2026 squad: Ayush Mhatre to lead; Vaibhav Suryavanshi selected - full team |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/u19-world-cup-2026-india-cricket-team-squad |access-date=31 December 2025 |website=www.olympics.com}}</ref> and coached by former India cricketer [[Hrishikesh Kanitkar]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rahul Dravid replaced as India A India U19 coach| url=https://www.mykhel.com/cricket/rahul-dravid-replaced-as-india-a-india-u-19-coach-125777.html|access-date=24 Jan 2020}}</ref>

'''Abdul Samad''' '''Abdul Samed''', etc. <ref name=ahmed>{{cite book| title=A Dictionary of Muslim Names| author=Salahuddin Ahmed| publisher = Hurst & Company| location=London| year=1999}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://webconte.com/kids/baby_names/boy/abdul_samad|title=Abdul Samad Arabic, Muslim and Urdu Language meaning}}</ref><ref name=rahman>{{cite book| title=A Dictionary of Muslim Names| author= S. A. Rahman| publisher=Goodword Books|  location=New Delhi| year=2001}}</ref> It may be roughly translated as "servant of the Self-sufficient Master" or "servant of the Eternal Refuge".

Because the letter s is a [[sun and moon letters|sun letter]], the letter l of the ''al-'' is assimilated to it. Thus although the name is written with letters corresponding to ''Abd al-Samad'', the usual pronunciation corresponds to ''Abd as-Samad''. Alternative transliterations include ''Abdus Samad'' and others, all subject to variant spacing and hyphenation.

'''Joshua Patrick Inglis''' (born 4 March 1995) is an English-born Australian [[cricket]]er who represents the [[Australia national cricket team|Australia national team]] as a [[wicket-keeper-batter]] in all three formats of the game. '''Himmat Singh''' (born 8 November 1996) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in domestic cricket. He bats right-handed and bowls right-arm [[off break]]. He represented Delhi at the Under-16, Under-19 and Under-23 levels and North Zone at the Under-19 level.<ref>{{cite web|title=Teams Himmat Singh played for|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/1196/1196832/all_teams.html|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=25 December 2015}}</ref>

Himmat was selected in the Delhi squad for [[2014–15 Ranji Trophy]] after his fine performance for the Delhi Under-19s, but did not appear in any of the matches.<ref>{{cite web|title=Himmat Singh, 18, included in Delhi Ranji Trophy squad|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/himmat-singh-18-included-in-delhi-ranji-trophy-squad/|publisher=The Indian Express|access-date=25 December 2015}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket]] debut at the age of 19 during the [[2015–16 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] in December 2015. Later that month, Himmat's father Tejbir Singh filed a criminal defamation case against [[Kirti Azad]], [[Bishan Singh Bedi]], [[Surinder Khanna]] and [[Sameer Bahadur]] for allegedly stating that Tejbir had exchanged {{INR}}25 lakh for his son's selection in the Delhi squad for the Vijay Hazare Trophy.<ref>{{cite web|title=DDCA row: Cricketer's father files defamation case against Kirti Azad, Bishan Singh Bedi|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/defamation-case-filed-against-kirti-azad-bishan-singh-bedi/|publisher=The Indian Express|access-date=25 December 2015}}</ref>

He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Delhi in the [[2017–18 Ranji Trophy]] on 14 October 2017.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1118626.html |title=Group A, Ranji Trophy at Delhi, Oct 14-17 2017 |access-date=14 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Delhi in the [[2017–18 Zonal T20 League]] on 9 January 2018.<ref name="T20">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1130675.html |title=North Zone, Inter State Twenty-20 Tournament at Delhi, Jan 9 2018 |access-date=9 January 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In December 2018, he was named in India's team for the [[2018 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/1167689.html |title=India Under-23s Squad |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 December 2018}}</ref> Later the same month, he was bought by the [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] in the [[List of 2019 Indian Premier League personnel changes|player auction]] for the [[2019 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/25390461/ipl-2019-auction-was-sold-whom |title=IPL 2019 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-auction-2019-who-got-whom/articleshow/67144375.cms |title=IPL 2019 Auction: Who got whom |work=The Times of India |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref> He was released by the Royal Challengers Bangalore ahead of the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28087425/where-do-eight-franchises-stand-2020-auction |title=Where do the eight franchises stand before the 2020 auction? |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 November 2019}}</ref>

'''Rasikh Salam Dar''' (born 5 April 2000) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who previously played for [[Jammu and Kashmir cricket team|Jammu and Kashmir]] and now plays for [[Baroda]] in domestic cricket. He also plays for [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL).<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1161489.html |title=Rasikh Salam |access-date=3 October 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In December 2018, he was signed by the [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[List of 2019 Indian Premier League personnel changes|player auction]] for the [[2019 Indian Premier League|2019 Indian Premier League Season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/25390461/ipl-2019-auction-was-sold-whom |title=IPL 2019 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-auction-2019-who-got-whom/articleshow/67144375.cms |title=IPL 2019 Auction: Who got whom |work=The Times of India |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref> He became the third cricketer from [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]] to play in the Indian Premier League.<ref name=times/> At 17 years and 353 days, he became the youngest player to make his debut for the Mumbai Indians.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-2019-rasikh-salam-surprise-from-mumbai-indians/articleshow/68556558.cms|title=IPL 2019: Rasikh Salam surprise from Mumbai Indians - Times of India|website=The Times of India|access-date=25 March 2019}}</ref> However, in June 2019, the [[Board of Control for Cricket in India]] (BCCI) banned him for two years following a "discrepancy" in his birth certificate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1189770.html |title=BCCI hands Rasikh Salam two-year ban for age fraud |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=19 June 2019}}</ref>

He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Jammu & Kashmir in the [[2018–19 Vijay Hazare Trophy]] on 3 October 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1156897.html |title=Elite, Group C, Vijay Hazare Trophy at Chennai, Oct 3 2018 |access-date=3 October 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Jammu & Kashmir in the [[2018–19 Ranji Trophy]] on 30 December 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157066.html |title=Elite, Group C, Ranji Trophy at Guwahati, Dec 30 2018 - Jan 2 2019 |access-date=30 December 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Jammu & Kashmir in the [[2018–19 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]] on 22 February 2019.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157109.html |title=Group A, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Krishna, Feb 22 2019 |access-date=22 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He was released by the Mumbai Indians ahead of the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28087425/where-do-eight-franchises-stand-2020-auction |title=Where do the eight franchises stand before the 2020 auction? |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 November 2019}}</ref> In February 2022, he was signed by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League|2022 Indian Premier League Season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He was acquired by Delhi Capitals in the [[List of 2024 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2024 Indian Premier League auction]] as a fast bowler. In the 2025 Indian Premier League auction, he was sold to Royal Challengers Bengaluru, winning his maiden IPL title that same season. The following season, he took 19 wickets, as RCB won back-to-back IPL titles.<ref name="IPL 2025 auction: Complete list of sold, unsold players, teamwise remaining purse {{!}} Mint">{{cite news|url=https://www.livemint.com/sports/cricket-news/ipl-auction-2025-sold-unsold-full-players-list-costliest-cricketer-remaining-purse-amount-teamwise-rishabh-pant-11732478575379.html|title=IPL 2025 auction: Complete list of sold, unsold players, teamwise remaining purse {{!}} Mint|date=25 November 2024|work=mint|access-date=15 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415102416/https://www.livemint.com/sports/cricket-news/ipl-auction-2025-sold-unsold-full-players-list-costliest-cricketer-remaining-purse-amount-teamwise-rishabh-pant-11732478575379.html|archive-date=15 April 2025|publisher=Mint|language=en}}</ref>

'''Ashwani Kumar''' (born 29 August 2001) is an Indian [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] in domestic cricket and [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1209126.html |title=Ashwani Kumar |access-date=9 December 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 9 December 2019, for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] in the [[2019–20 Ranji Trophy]].<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1203446.html |title=Elite, Group A, Ranji Trophy at Jaipur, Dec 9-12 2019 |access-date=9 December 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 8 December 2021, for Punjab in the [[2021–22 Vijay Hazare Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280315.html |title=Elite, Group E, Ranchi, Dec 8 2021, Vijay Hazare Trophy |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=8 December 2021}}</ref>

Ashwani was signed for [[Mumbai Indians]] in the IPL 2025 mega auctions for 30 lakhs.<ref name="MI’s newest boombox Ashwani Kumar: Started with Rs 30 for share autos, bowled pace with ordinary canvas shoes and developed quick-arm action">{{cite news |title=MI's newest boombox Ashwani Kumar: Started with Rs 30 for share autos, bowled pace with ordinary canvas shoes and developed quick-arm action |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/ipl/ashwani-kumar-mumbai-indians-profile-share-auto-old-shoes-9916884/ |access-date=13 April 2025 |publisher=The Indian Express |date=1 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250413064824/https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/ipl/ashwani-kumar-mumbai-indians-profile-share-auto-old-shoes-9916884/ |archive-date=13 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

Bowling his very first ball in the IPL, he got the wicket of Kolkata Knight Riders captain [[Ajinkya Rahane]],<ref name="Who is Ashwani Kumar? Mumbai Indians pacer, taking four wickets on IPL debut, dismissed Ajinkya Rahane on first ball">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title=Who is Ashwani Kumar? '''Arshdeep Singh''' (born 1999) is an  Indian professional [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[India national cricket team]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-09-13 |title='Dream come true, want to see him win World Cup for India now': Arshdeep Singh's family |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/t20-world-cup-india-arshdeep-singh-8147237/ |access-date=2022-10-05 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> In Indian domestic cricket, he plays for [[Punjab cricket team (India)|Punjab]] and for [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. Arshdeep is a left-arm [[medium-fast bowler]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web |title=Arshdeep Singh |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1125976.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180601053408/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1125976.html |archive-date=1 June 2018 |access-date=19 September 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He was an integral member of the Indian team that won the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] and [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026]] [[Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cups]], and was the joint-highest wicket taker in the former. Singh was also a member of the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy|2025 Champions Trophy]] and [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2018 U19 World Cup]] winning squads.

Arshdeep made his international debut for the Indian team in July 2022 in a [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] match against [[England cricket team|England]]. He bowled a [[maiden over]] on debut, becoming just the third Indian bowler to do so on their T20I debut.{{efn|The others were [[Jhulan Goswami]], the former captain of the Indian women's team, and [[Ajit Agarkar]] who played for India's men's team between 1998 and 2007.}}<ref name=ie8jul22>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-08 |title=First in 16 years: Arshdeep Singh becomes third Indian bowler to bowl a maiden on T20I debut |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/eng-vs-ind-arshdeep-singh-breaks-16-year-old-record-becomes-first-indian-bowler-to-bowl-a-maiden-on-t20i-debut-8016211/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905153220/https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/eng-vs-ind-arshdeep-singh-breaks-16-year-old-record-becomes-first-indian-bowler-to-bowl-a-maiden-on-t20i-debut-8016211/ |archive-date=5 September 2022 |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> Arshdeep is the first Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in T20 internationals.<ref>{{Cite news |title=New record! '''Ramakrishna Shekhar Ghosh''' (born 28 August 1997) is an Indian [[cricket]]er from [[Nashik, Maharashtra]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramakrishna Ghosh IPL Stats, Career & Records {{!}} IPL 2025 Squad |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/player-stats/ramakrishna-ghosh/98813 |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramakrishna Ghosh Profile, Career Records, Ramakrishna Ghosh T20, ODI, IPL, Test Stats, Ramakrishna Ghosh News |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/live-score/cricket/ramakrishna-ghosh-profile-98813 |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref> A right-arm medium-fast bowler and right-handed batsman, he plays as a bowling all-rounder for [[Maharashtra cricket team|Maharashtra]] in domestic cricket<ref>[https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/ramakrishna-ghosh-1339053 Ramakrishna Ghosh], [[CricInfo]]. Retrieved 6 August 2025.</ref> and was signed by [[Chennai Super Kings]] for the 2025 [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) season.

Ghosh made his T20 debut for Maharashtra in the 2022-23 [[Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy]], notably dismissing [[Mayank Agarwal|Mayank Agarwal.]] In the 2024/25 [[Ranji Trophy]] he took 11 wickets in six matches at an average of 41.45, with a best of 3/50 against Odisha, and scored 313 runs, including two fifties, at an average of 39.12.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramakrishna Ghosh Profile {{!}} Ramakrishna Ghosh ICC Ranking {{!}} Cricket Career, Cricket Info & Stats |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/cricket/player-profile-ramakrishna-ghosh-98813.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603160233/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/cricket/player-profile-ramakrishna-ghosh-98813.html |archive-date=3 June 2025 |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramakrishna Ghosh - Ramakrishna Ghosh Career Info, Achievements, ICC Ranking along with Records & Stats {{!}} Crcikit by HT |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/players/player-name |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> In the 2024 Maharashtra Premier League, he excelled for Puneri Bappa, taking 20 wickets in 15 matches at an average of 17.20, with best figures of 4/30, and scoring 118 runs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramakrishna Ghosh |url=https://www.insidesport.in/cricket/players/ramakrishna-ghosh/ |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=Inside Sport India |language=en}}</ref>

In the IPL, Ghosh was acquired by Chennai Super Kings for INR 30 lakhs in the 2025 auction.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 November 2024 |title=IPL 2025 Auction Full List Of Sold Players: Rishabh Pant Most Expensive, 13-Year-Old Becomes Youngest Buy In History |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/ipl-2025-auction-full-list-of-sold-players-rishabh-pant-most-expensive-13-year-old-vaibhav-suryavanshi-becomes-youngest-buy-in-history-article-115668974 |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=Times Now |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Soory |first=Samarnath |title=Meet CSK'S Ramakrishna Ghosh: The Pace Bowling All-rounder Chennai Super Kings Picked For IPL 2025 With Ruturaj Gaikwad's Recommendation |url=https://cricxtasy.com/features/meet-csks-ramakrishna-ghosh-the-pace-bowling-all-rounder-chennai-super-kings-picked-for-ipl-2025-with-ruturaj-gaikwads-recommendation/ |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=Cricxtasy |language=en-IN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=S |first=Hemkesh |date=26 November 2024 |title=IPL 2025: Emerging Indian talents to watch out for in CSK squad |url=https://www.dtnext.in/news/sports/ipl-2025-emerging-indian-talents-to-watch-out-for-in-csk-squad-812642 |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=www.dtnext.in |language=en}}</ref>

'''Mukul Dalip Choudhary''' (born 6 August 2004) is an Indian cricketer, who plays as a wicket keeper batter. He plays for Rajasthan in domestic cricket and [[Lucknow Super Giants]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lucknow Super Giants {{!}} LSG 2025 Squad & Overview {{!}} IPLT20 |url=https://www.iplt20.com/teams/lucknow-super-giants |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=[[Indian Premier League]] |language=en}}</ref>

Choudhary made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 17 January 2023 in the [[2022–23 Ranji Trophy]]<ref>{{cite web |title=RAJ vs CGR Cricket Scorecard, Elite, Group C at Jodhpur, January 17 - 20, 2023 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ranji-trophy-2022-23-1332913/rajasthan-vs-chhattisgarh-elite-group-c-1333299/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=[[Cricinfo]] |language=en}}</ref> and his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 24 December 2025 in the [[2025–26 Vijay Hazare Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web |title=M. Pradesh vs Rajasthan, Elite, Group A at Ahmedabad, Vijay Hazare Trophy, Dec 24 2025 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/vijay-hazare-trophy-2025-26-1492383/madhya-pradesh-vs-rajasthan-elite-group-a-1492667/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=[[Cricinfo]] |publisher=}}</ref>

Choudhary was purchased by the [[Lucknow Super Giants]] ahead of the [[2026 Indian Premier League]] for ₹2.6 crore in the [[List of 2026 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mallick |first1=Megha |date=2025-12-16 |title=Who Is Mukul Choudhary? 21-Year-Old Rajasthan Star Bags Big IPL 2026 Deal |url=https://www.news18.com/cricket/who-is-mukul-choudhary-21-year-old-rajasthan-wicketkeeper-bags-big-ipl-2026-deal-ws-l-9773862.html |access-date=24 December 2025 |work=2025-12-24 |publisher=News 18}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Acharya |first1=Shayan |date=16 December 2025 |title=Father's dream fuels IPL fairytale as Mukul Choudhary bags Rs. 2.60 crore deal with LSG |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/mukul-choudhary-ipl-auction-lucknow-super-giants-price-lsg-reaction-profile-rajasthan-cricket-news/article70403527.ece |access-date=2025-12-24 |work=Sportstar |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Puri |first1=Sagar |date=16 December 2025 |title=LSG Full Squad IPL 2026 Auction: Lucknow Super Giants strengthen core with smart auction and trade moves |url=https://news24online.com/sports/cricket/lsg-players-auction-ipl-2026-live-updates-lucknow-super-giants-complete-list-of-players-full-squad-retained-release-players/688529/ |access-date=2025-12-24 |work=News24 |language=en}}</ref> On 9 April 2026, Choudhary hit a match winning 54* off 27 deliveries as he single handedly helped [[Lucknow Super Giants]] chase down 182 against [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] on the last ball.<ref>https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ipl-2026-1510719/kolkata-knight-riders-vs-lucknow-super-giants-15th-match-1527688/live-match-blog</ref>

'''Danish Vishnu Malewar''' (born 8 October 2003) is an Indian cricketer who plays for [[Vidarbha cricket team|Vidharba]] in domestic cricket and [[Mumbai Indians]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Danish Malewar |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/danish-malewar-1421992 |url-status=live |archive-date= |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=[[Cricinfo]]}}</ref> 

He made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 11 October 2024 for Vidharba in the [[2024–25 Ranji Trophy|2024-25 Ranji Trophy]]. He subsequently scored 783 runs at an average of 52 in the season and scored 153 off 285 balls in the [[2024–25 Ranji Trophy#Final|final]], which was won by Vidharba.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-26 |title=Remember the name: Danish Malewar hits hundred in Ranji final to power Vidarbha |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/danish-malewar-hundred-ranji-final-vidarbha-kerala-9857939/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2025–26 Duleep Trophy|2025-26 Duleep Trophy]], he scored 203 off 221 balls on debut for [[Central Zone cricket team|Central Zone]] against [[North East Zone cricket team|North East Zone]], hitting 36 fours and a six during his innings.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-29 |title=Duleep Trophy: Vidarbha’s Danish Malewar records history with double century on debut after Ranji final heroics |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/duleep-trophy-vidarbha-danish-malewar-record-double-hundred-debut-10217755/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

Due to his domestic performances, Malewar was signed by Mumbai Indians for the [[2026 Indian Premier League|2026 IPL]] at his base price of INR 30 lakhs.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-04-20 |title=IPL 2026: Who is Danish Malewar? MI’s 21-year-old debutant set for big stage vs GT |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/ipl-2026/ipl-2026-who-is-danish-malewar-mis-21-year-old-debutant-set-for-big-stage-vs-gt/articleshow/130394503.cms |access-date=2026-05-06 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-04-20 |title=IPL 2026: Who are Danish Malewar and Krish Bhagat? '''Luke Wood''' (born 2 August 1995) is an English [[cricket]]er who plays for [[England cricket team|England]] and [[Lancashire County Cricket Club|Lancashire]]. Primarily a left-arm [[Fast bowling|fast-medium]] [[Bowling (cricket)|bowler]], he also bats left-handed. He made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club|Nottinghamshire]] against [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]] in September 2014. He made his international debut in 2022

In April 2022, he was bought by the [[Trent Rockets]] for the [[2022 season of The Hundred|2022 season]] of [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/60477088 |title=The Hundred 2022: latest squads as Draft picks revealed |work=BBC Sport |access-date=5 April 2022}}</ref> The following month, Wood was named in England's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad for their series [[English cricket team in the Netherlands in 2022|against the Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/netherlands-vs-england-2022-sam-billings-overlooked-as-england-name-strong-squad-for-netherlands-odis-1317714 |title=Sam Billings overlooked as England name strong squad for Netherlands ODIs |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=31 May 2022}}</ref> In September 2022, he was named in the England's T20I squad for the [[English cricket team in Pakistan in 2022–23|series against Pakistan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-2022-england-keep-faith-with-old-guard-as-ben-stokes-mark-wood-chris-woakes-return-for-t20-world-cup-1332090 |title=England keep faith with old guard as Ben Stokes, Mark Wood, Chris Woakes return for T20 World Cup |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=2 September 2022}}</ref> He made his T20I debut on 20 September 2022, against [[Pakistan cricket team|Pakistan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1327228.html |title=1st T20I (N), Karachi, September 20, 2022, England tour of Pakistan |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=20 September 2022}}</ref> Wood made his ODI debut on 17 November 2022, [[English cricket team in Australia in 2022–23|against Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-in-australia-2022-23-1317467/australia-vs-england-1st-odi-1317489/match-report |title=Cummins bowls first at start of his ODI captaincy; Luke Wood handed England debut |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=17 November 2022}}</ref>

In the [[Bangladesh Premier League|BPL]] [[2022–23 Bangladesh Premier League|2022–23]], he was taken by [[Sylhet Strikers]] franchise. He played a crucial part in the Qualifier 2 conceding just 3 runs in the penultimate over helping Sylhet reach the final of BPL 2023.

On 18 March 2024, he was signed as a replacement for the injured [[Jason Behrendorff]] by [[Mumbai Indians]] for {{INRConvert|50|l|lk=on|to=GBP}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2024-mi-sign-luke-wood-as-replacement-for-injured-jason-behrendorff-1425350 |title=Mumbai Indians sign Luke Wood as replacement for injured Behrendorff |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=25 March 2024}}</ref>

On 21 March 2025, it was announced that Wood had been signed by [[England and Wales Cricket Board|ECB]], [[Lincolnshire Premier League]] side [[Woodhall Spa]] Cricket Club, when not on white-ball duty.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DHfpvuHIW3X/?igsh=MWVyZXYybm1iMmV5cQ== |access-date=2025-03-27 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref>

[[Janata Dal]] (1988–1999) |signature = Vishwanath Pratap Singh Signature.svg }} }} | prime_minister2 = ''Himself'' | prime_minister1 = ''Himself'' | order = | order2 = | order1 = }} '''Vishwanath Pratap Singh''' (25 June 1931 – 27 November 2008) was an Indian politician who served as the [[Prime Minister of India]] from 1989 to 1990 and the [[Raja Bahadur]] of [[Manda (zamindari)|Manda]].{{Cite web|last=Rathore|first=Abhinay|title=Manda (Zamindari)|url=https://www.indianrajputs.com/view/manda|access-date=2021-11-19|website=Rajput Provinces of India|language=en}}{{Cite web|date=2021-09-01|title=List of all Prime Ministers of India (1947-2021)|url=https://www.jagranjosh.com/general-knowledge/list-of-all-prime-ministers-of-india-1473165149-1|access-date=2021-11-19|website=www.jagranjosh.com}} Some Pakistani historians state that Singh's family originated from a village in the Yaqubi area of District Peshawar (present-day Swabi, Pakistan), and that after the [[Partition of India]] in 1947 he moved with his mother to live at his uncle's home.{{cite news |title=A tale of one city: Revisiting the past of Swabi |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/935149/a-tale-of-one-city-revisiting-the-past-of-swabi |work=The Express Tribune |date=11 August 2015 |access-date=9 August 2025}}{{cite book |last=Jadoon |first=Ziaullah Khan |title=Shakhsiat Swabi |publisher=Ziaullah Khan Jadoon |page=217 |url=https://www.scribd.com/document/486600563/Shakhsiyat-Swabi-by-zia-ullah-Khan-Jadoon |language=ur}} He was educated at [[Allahabad University]] and [[Fergusson College]] in Pune.{{Cite news |last=Pandya |first=Haresh |date=2008-11-30 |title=V. P. Singh, a Leader of India Who Defended Poor, Dies at 77 |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/11/30/world/asia/30singh.html |access-date=2022-05-06 |issn=0362-4331}} In 1969, he joined the [[Indian National Congress]] party and was elected as a member of the [[Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly]].{{Cite news|last=Pandya|first=Haresh|date=2008-11-30|title=V. P. Singh, a Leader of India Who Defended Poor, Dies at 77|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/11/30/world/asia/30singh.html|access-date=2021-11-19|issn=0362-4331}} In the [[First Rajiv Gandhi ministry|Rajiv Gandhi ministry]], Singh was given various cabinet posts, including [[Minister of Finance (India)|Minister of Finance]] and [[Minister of Defence (India)|Minister of Defence]]. Singh was also the [[Leader of the House (Rajya Sabha)|Leader of the Rajya Sabha]] from 1984 to 1987. During his tenure as Minister of Defence, the [[Bofors scandal]] came to light, and Singh resigned from the ministry. In 1988, he formed the [[Janata Dal]] party by merging various factions of the [[Janata Party]]. In the [[1989 Indian general election|1989 elections]], the [[Third Front (India)|National Front]], with the support of the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] (BJP), formed the government and Singh became the prime minister. During his tenure as prime minister, he implemented the [[Mandal Commission]] report for India's [[Other Backward Class|backward castes]], which led to major [[Mandal Commission protests of 1990|protests]] against the act. Under Singh's prime ministership in 1989, the Government of India released five terrorists in exchange for the release of kidnapped Rubaiya Sayeed, daughter of the Union Home Minister, Mufti Mohammad Sayeed. This was a turning point in the history of Kashmir militancy, which left a long lasting impact in Kashmir. In 1990 the [[exodus of Kashmiri Hindus]] from the valley of [[Kashmir Valley|Kashmir]] took place. Following his opposition to the [[Ram Rath Yatra]], the BJP withdrew its support for the National Front, and his government lost the [[Motion of no confidence|vote of no-confidence]]. Singh resigned on 7 November 1990. His prime ministerial tenure lasted for 343 days. Singh was the prime ministerial candidate for the [[Third Front (India)|National Front]] in the [[1991 Indian general election|1991 elections]], but was defeated. He spoke out against the [[Demolition of the Babri Masjid|Babri Masjid demolition]] in 1992. He turned down prime ministership after the [[1996 Indian general election]] even though he was the first choice and relinquished the prime ministership to [[H. D. Deve Gowda]].{{cite web | last=Mukerji | first=Debashish | title=Before Deve Gowda, VP Singh was asked to be PM of United Front. He hid in his flat, car | website=ThePrint | date=8 December 2021 | url=https://theprint.in/pageturner/excerpt/before-deve-gowda-vp-singh-was-asked-to-be-pm-of-united-front-he-hid-in-his-flat-car/777894/ | access-date=29 June 2024}}{{cite web | last=Srinivasaraju | first=Sugata | title=Deve Gowda and the accidental prime ministers | website=The New Indian Express | date=5 June 2021 | url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/opinions/2021/Jun/05/devegowda-and-the-accidental-prime-ministers-2311864.html | access-date=29 June 2024}} After 1996, Singh retired from political posts, but continued to remain a public figure and political critic. He was diagnosed with [[multiple myeloma]] in 1998, and ceased public appearances until the cancer went into remission in 2003. He died from complications of multiple myeloma and kidney failure in 2008. He was cremated with full state honours.

The '''Indian men's national Under-19 cricket team''' represents [[India]] in cricket at Under-19 level. The team has won a record six [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]] titles, and has the best win percentage in ODIs among all Under-19 national teams. Also, this team has won a record eight  [[Under-19 Men's Asia Cup|U19 Asia Cup]] titles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Under-19s Youth One-Day Internationals / Team records / Results summary|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/337074.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=30 June 2012}}</ref> India are the current holders of the [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]].

The team has won the [[Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|U19 Cricket World Cup]], a record six times and finished runners-up four times. In [[2000 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2000]], they won it under the captaincy of [[Mohammad Kaif]], in [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2008]], they won it under [[Virat Kohli]]'s leadership, in [[2012 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2012]] under [[Unmukt Chand]], in [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2018]] under [[Prithvi Shaw]], and in [[2022 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2022]] under [[Yash Dhull]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/boys-do-a-men-lift-under-19-cricket-world-cup/story-IndRmyY12yP3Y2x0lVwOUJ.html|title=Boys do a men, lift Under 19 cricket World Cup|first=|last=|date=26 August 2012|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/u19-world-cup-raj-bawa-nishant-sindhu-the-stars-as-all-round-india-beat-england-to-win-record-extending-fifth-title-101644073386391.html|title=U19 World Cup: Raj Bawa, Nishant Sindhu the stars as all-round India beat England to win record-extending fifth title|date=6 February 2022|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/icc-under-19-cricket-world-cup-final-india-vs-australia/story-yjJKkAHHschqhAr1IIV89H.html|title=ICC Under-19 World Cup: Manjot Kalra ton, bowlers give India record 4th title|date=3 February 2018|website=Hindustan Times}}</ref> [[Ayush Mhatre]] led the team to their 6th title in [[2026 Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup|2026]].<ref>{{cite web |title=U19 World Cup: India Beat England by 100 Runs to Win 6th Title |url=https://www.khelwire.com/articles/u19-world-cup-india-beat-england-by-100-runs-to-win-6th-title |website=KhelWire |date=6 February 2026 |access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref>

The team has also won the [[Under-19 Men's Asia Cup|U19 Asia Cup]], a record eight times, in 1989, 2003, 2012, 2013–14, 2016, 2018, 2019, and 2021.

|access-date=2025-08-25 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} Shakib Al Hasan made his Test debut in 2007 against [[India national cricket team|India]]. His breakthrough came in the Test against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] in [[Chittagong]] in 2008, where he picked up 7 wickets for 36 runs, the best figures by a Bangladeshi bowler at that time. He quickly established himself as one of the team's leading performers. He has scored over 4,000 runs and taken more than 200 wickets in this format. He has also captained the team on their first-ever Test match win over [[England cricket team|England]] in 2016.{{Cite news |last=Marks |first=Vic |date=2016-10-30 |title=Bangladesh claim historic Test win over England as collapse ensures tied series |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/oct/30/bangladesh-beat-england-draw-test-series |access-date=2023-05-05 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=5 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505200845/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/oct/30/bangladesh-beat-england-draw-test-series |url-status=live }} In ODIs, Shakib has been more successful. He has scored over 6,000 runs and taken more than 270 wickets in the format, becoming the fastest player in history to achieve the double of 5,000 runs and 250 wickets in ODIs.{{Cite news |date=2019-06-02 |title=Quickest to 5,000 Runs and 250 Wickets, Shakib Al Hasan Joins Elite All-Rounders Club |url=https://www.news18.com/news/sports/bangladesh-south-africa-shakib-al-hasan-cricket-quickest-to-5000-runs-and-250-wickets-joins-elite-all-rounders-club-2169465.html |access-date=2023-05-05 |work=News18 |language=en |archive-date=5 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505200845/https://www.news18.com/news/sports/bangladesh-south-africa-shakib-al-hasan-cricket-quickest-to-5000-runs-and-250-wickets-joins-elite-all-rounders-club-2169465.html |url-status=live }} In the [[2012 Asia Cup]], Shakib scored 237 runs, including three fifties, and took six wickets. Bangladesh progressed to the tournament's final for the first time but eventually lost to Pakistan by 2 runs, and he was awarded the Player of the tournament award in that edition of the tournament.{{Cite web |date=22 March 2012 |title=Asia Cup – Final |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asia-cup-2011-12-524504/bangladesh-vs-pakistan-final-535800/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en}} He is considered one of the most impactful players of the [[ICC Cricket World Cup 2019|2019 ICC Cricket World Cup]],{{Cite web |date=2019-07-16 |title=Why Shakib Al Hasan, not Kane Williamson, deserved to bag ICC World Cup 2019 Player of the Tournament award |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/was-peerless-shakib-al-hasan-robbed-off-icc-world-cup-2019-player-of-the-tournament-award/454386 |access-date=2023-07-22 |website=www.timesnownews.com |language=en |archive-date=22 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722070432/https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/was-peerless-shakib-al-hasan-robbed-off-icc-world-cup-2019-player-of-the-tournament-award/454386 |url-status=live }} where he broke the record of maximum runs scored in the group stages of the World Cup which was previously held by [[Sachin Tendulkar]] and finished as the third-highest run-scorer, scoring 606 runs in total at the tournament.{{Cite web |title=Most runs in ICC Cricket World Cup, 2019 |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=12357&type=tournament |access-date=2022-10-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} He has played for various T20 tournaments around the world for many teams, including [[Kolkata Knight Riders]], [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]], [[Jamaica Tallawahs]] and [[Dhaka Dynamites|Dhaka Dominators]], where he won the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) twice with Kolkata Knight Riders in 2012 and 2014. He also won the [[Bangladesh Premier League]] (BPL) title 3 times in 2012, 2013 and 2016 with [[Dhaka Dominators]]. He was named the player of the tournament in BPL a record four times, in 2012, 2013, 2018 and 2022.{{Cite web |date=2022-02-18 |title=Shakib adjudged player of the tournament for the fourth time in BPL |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/sports/shakib-adjudged-player-tournament-fourth-time-bpl-372622 |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=The Business Standard |language=en}} He has won 41 man-of-the-match awards, the highest for any Bangladeshi player and 16 man-of-the-series awards in all formats. Between 2009 and 2022, he captained the Bangladesh cricket team in 120 matches across all three formats. Shakib Al Hasan has been a consistent performer for the Bangladesh cricket team over the years.{{cite news | url=https://en.prothomalo.com/sports/cricket/ysuww9o47g | title=Shakib first cricketer to bag 700 intl wickets, 14,000 runs |work=Prothom Alo | date=26 May 2024 }} His career has been filled with controversies over the years, consistently making it to the top of domestic media headlines.{{Cite magazine |date=2022-01-11 |title=Shakib Al Hasan Disciplinary Issues: Ten Times When Bangladesh Superstar Got Involved In Controversies |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/sports/sports-news-shakib-al-hasan-disciplinary-issues-ten-times-when-bangladesh-superstar-got-involved-in-controversies-news-385047 |access-date=2022-10-07 |magazine=Outlook |language=en |archive-date=7 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007094850/https://www.outlookindia.com/website/story/sports-news-shakib-al-hasan-disciplinary-issues-ten-times-when-bangladesh-superstar-got-involved-in-controversies/385047 |url-status=live }} He is considered one of the most influential and followed people on [[social media]] in Bangladesh.{{citation needed|date=January 2026}} He was ranked the 90th most famous athlete in the world by [[ESPN.com|ESPN]] in 2019. He was included in the [[ICC Men's ODI Team of the Year|ICC Men's Team of the Year]] twice (2009, 2021).{{citation needed|date=January 2026}}

[[Rajasthan Royals]] (RR) is a franchise cricket team based in [[Rajasthan]], India, which has played in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) since the first edition of the tournament in [[2008 Indian Premier League|2008]]. They were one of ten teams to compete in the [[2022 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=ESPNcricinfo staff |date=5 September 2010 |title=Next three IPL seasons to comprise 74 matches each |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-news-next-three-ipl-seasons-to-comprise-74-matches-each-475828 |access-date=30 September 2021 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL to become 10 team tournament from 2022 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-to-become-10-team-tournament-from-2022-1275505 |access-date=29 September 2021 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> The Royals have previously lifted the IPL title once, in the [[2008 Indian Premier League|inaugural season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Rajasthan Royals are IPL champions |url=http://ipl.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/3091229.cms |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=2 June 2008 |access-date=2 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080604031604/http://ipl.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/3091229.cms |archive-date=4 June 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The side finished as the runners-up in the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-final-2022-gt-vs-rr-rajasthan-royals-captain-sanju-samson-proud-of-his-team-despite-losing-title-to-gujarat-titans/articleshow/91884353.cms|title=IPL Final 2022, GT vs RR: Rajasthan Royals captain Sanju Samson 'proud' of his team despite losing title to Gujarat Titans|work=The Times of India|date=30 May 2022|access-date=9 June 2022}}</ref>

'''Tejasvi Singh Dahiya''' (born 18 April 2002) is an Indian [[Wicket-keeper|wicket-keeper-batter]] who plays for [[Delhi cricket team|Delhi]] in domestic [[cricket]] and [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[Indian Premier League]].<ref name="Career">{{Cite web |title=Tejasvi Dahiya Profile - Cricket Player India {{!}} Stats, Records, Video |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/tejasvi-dahiya-1460372 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250117055854/https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/tejasvi-dahiya-1460372 |archive-date=17 January 2025 |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

Singh gained wider recognition for his performance in the [[Delhi Premier League T20|Delhi Premier League]], where he was the tournament’s leading six-hitter, striking 29 sixes and scoring 339 runs at a strike rate of 190.44.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Delhi Premier League Stats 2025 {{!}} DPL Players Stats {{!}} Delhi Premier League 2025 Players Stats |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/series-delhi-premier-league-2025/stats |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

He was acquired by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] for ₹3 crore in the IPL 2026 auction on 16 December, having entered the auction with a base price of ₹30 lakh.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2025-12-16 |title=Tejasvi Singh Dahiya: Son of maths and economics teachers, trained in a jungle, and hits sixes for fun |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/tejasvi-singh-dahiya-son-of-maths-and-economics-teachers-trained-in-a-jungle-and-hits-sixes-for-fun/articleshow/126009496.cms |access-date=2025-12-17 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>
